Trump was given the award at the men’s World Cup draw in Washington last December, with Infantino presenting the US president with a golden trophy, a medal and a certificate, but the process behind his selection has never been made public.

The social responsibility committee is expected as part of its review to set strict parameters for any surviving award, and to provide details of a nomination and selection procedure.

Sports.title: Álvaro Arbeloa’s push to make Fulham free-flowing is floundering already
Sports.content:
Fulham fans fretting about life under Álvaro Arbeloa will not feel any better when they remember how things were under Marco Silva, who was one of the most effective managers in the Premier League when it came to making substitutions.

Silva’s substitutes were involved in the fourth-highest goal contributions last season and the most in the 2024-25 season. Fulham knew how to dig in and salvage unlikely points. But Silva left last summer, joining Benfica after concluding he could achieve nothing more at Craven Cottage, and his replacement is already under pressure after some puzzling tactical choices.

The worrying shift under Arbeloa was evident during Fulham’s collapse against Ipswich last weekend. The west Londoners were 1-0 up and looking good for their first league win of the season when Arbeloa weakened his midfield by replacing Shea Charles with Manuel Ángel in the 70th minute.

It was a strange way to shut up shop. Charles is physically imposing, has impressed since joining from Southampton and was doing well alongside Sander Berge. The 22-year-old Ángel is 5ft 7in, was making his Premier League debut and has little experience of senior football. Ipswich’s comeback to win 2-1 was not a surprise, particularly when Arbeloa’s other rejigs included bringing on Rodrigo Muniz and switching from a 4-2-3-1 system to a flat 4-4-2 in an attempt to defend the lead.

The subsequent floundering felt inevitable. Emile Smith Rowe, another late substitute, was slow to close down Abdoul Ouattara when the Ipswich right-back equalised. Fulham have dropped eight points from winning positions. They are managing games badly and their physical shortcomings were exposed by Ipswich, whose winner came from a poorly defended free-kick and left Fulham in last place before facing Hull at home on Saturday.

Arbeloa needs a win. Relegation fears are growing and there are whispers that the Spaniard’s job is under threat. Fulham had a tricky start – they have already faced Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United – but the Ipswich game was supposed to mark a turning point. It was the first of three consecutive meetings with the promoted sides and, with Coventry, Hull and Ipswich surpassing expectations, it is easy to see Fulham’s aim to move to a more expansive style under Arbeloa backfiring.

Questions have to be asked over the decision by the Khan family to appoint someone whose experience of management was limited to an interim spell in charge of Real Madrid last season. Fingers will be pointed at the succession planners. Tony Khan, director of football and son of patriarch Shahid, has faced fierce criticism in the past. Silva offered stability. There was always a fear the project would fall apart once the Portuguese was gone.

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García struggled to make an impression at Ipswich. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters

It does not help Arbeloa to lean on his time at the Bernabéu. He responded to a question about pressure after losing to Ipswich by saying: “I played for the best team in the world … I have coached the best team in the world.” But the optics are awkward. Arbeloa did not win anything as Madrid’s manager, his comments risk making it seem his current employers should be grateful to have him and eyebrows have been raised at three of the 43-year-old’s summer signings coming from his former club.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ángel, César Palacios and Gonzalo García were all promising young Real Madrid players, all share representation with Arbeloa and are now adapting to a new league. Palacios, an inventive passing midfielder, is 21 and Garcia, a nimble forward, is 22. They deserve to be given time, although the clock is ticking. García, signed for £40m, has one league goal from 18 shots and struggled against Ipswich, winning few duels and pressing ineffectively.

Supporters are growing restless. They wonder why Kevin, the Brazilian winger, is being used on the right rather than the left. They feel Arbeloa is chopping and changing too often. They worry about the team conceding costly late goals against Sunderland, Crystal Palace and United. Fulham were ridiculously open in their opening game, the barmy 3-2 defeat by Chelsea, and their expected goals against is 10.3 in six games. They have lost two of their main goalscorers, Raúl Jiménez and Harry Wilson, and are struggling to fill the void.

Equally there is an argument that Arbeloa needs time to implement a new style. There are suggestions some players are unsure about the manager’s tactics. Some stalwarts have been sidelined – Joachim Andersen, the influential Denmark centre-back, is not suited to playing a high line and has lost his spot to David Affengruber – but perhaps a refresh was required. Fulham have looked to lower the age of their squad, in part because of a need to comply with financial regulations, and there is nothing intrinsically wrong with trying to play more exciting football.

There have been encouraging spells. After flirting with European qualification in each of the past four seasons, only to fizzle out and finish in the bottom half, Fulham can be forgiven for wondering how to take the next step. At the same time the fear for supporters is that a club operating with one of the league’s smaller budgets have forgotten what it takes to survive. Silva’s teams could attack but were gritty and streetwise. At the moment Arbeloa looks naive. Fulham lost £45m in the past financial year and spent a lot on the Riverside Stand refurbishment. The Khans need Premier League survival. Arbeloa has big ideas but might not make it past this month without a huge improvement.

Sports.title: South African rugby player Hyron Andrews dead aged 31: Former Sale Sharks star suffers heart attack at team hotel in France on eve of Champions Cup clash with La Rochelle
Sports.content:
Tributes have been paid to ‘funny’, ‘charismatic’ and ‘brilliant team-mate’ Hyron Andrews after the former Sale Sharks lock died of a suspected heart attack in news that has shocked the rugby world.

On Friday morning, French media reported a playing member of the Lions – one of South Africa’s four big domestic teams – had been found unresponsive in a shower at the Atalante-Relais Thalasso Hotel just outside of La Rochelle – the venue where the side is preparing for European Champions Cup game on Saturday which will go ahead as planned.

Just a few hours later, the Lions confirmed the passing of Andrews, 31. Emergency services arrived but were unable to save him and he was pronounced dead at the scene.

Andrews only returned to his native South Africa to join the Lions this summer after departing English club side Sale for whom he made 45 appearances. Of those, 19 came for the Sharks last season. Andrews' former club boss, Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson, said: 'Hyron was just a brilliant guy and team-mate. He was so skilled on the field but off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with.

'He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him. It was a big move for Hyron and his wife Maiglin to come to England but he truly made a second home in Manchester and it was incredible to see how he and his family embraced the club and area.

'Most importantly, he was a loving husband and a doting father to his two gorgeous boys. It was an absolute privilege to get to know him. It’s just absolutely devastating for everyone.'

Lions player Hyron Andrews, 31, has died of an apparent heart attack in La Rochelle, a day before the two sides were due to meet in the European Champions Cup

Hyron and his wife Maiglin along with one of their sons are pictured here

Confirming Andrews’ passing, the Lions said in a statement: ‘The Lions Rugby Company is deeply saddened by the passing of player Hyron Andrews while on tour with the 10bet Lions ahead of their Investec Champions Cup and Vodacom United Rugby Championship fixtures.

'This devastating news has sent shockwaves through the international rugby community. The former Sharks and Sale Sharks lock forward was a valued member of the Lions family and his loss will be felt profoundly by his team-mates, coaches, supporters and all who had the privilege of knowing him. Our deepest and most heartfelt condolences go to Hyron’s wife, Maiglin, their young sons, and the entire Andrews family. We hold them in our thoughts during this time of unimaginable grief and ask that their privacy be respected as they mourn.’ The Lions have confirmed that their scheduled clash with La Rochelle will go ahead with the team’s players keen to pay tribute to Andrews on the field.

Reports in the French media said a psychological support unit had been set up for the Lions franchise's players and staff, as well as the hotel personnel.

Rudolf Straeuli, Lions chief executive, said: ‘We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron. He was not only a gifted rugby player, but also a cherished member of our Lions family having recently joined us this season.

'On behalf of our chairman, Mr Altmann Allers, the board and everyone at the Lions, I extend our deepest sympathies to Maiglin, their young sons Hendrix and Emerson and the entire Andrews family. We stand with them in their sorrow and will remember Hyron with great affection and respect.’

The Lions added: ‘The Lions Rugby Company will communicate further details regarding an appropriate tribute in due course. In honour of Hyron, the 10bet Lions will fulfil their opening match of the Investec Champions Cup against La Rochelle tomorrow evening South African time. May Hyron rest in peace.’

Andrews' former employers Sale said: 'Everyone at Sale Sharks is devastated to learn of the death of our former player Hyron Andrews. Hyron was a much-loved member of the squad during his time with us and everyone at the club is united in sending their love, thoughts and heartfelt condolences to his wife Maiglin, their beautiful boys and the rest of his family and friends and everyone at Lions Rugby.'

PREM Rugby also said in a statement: 'Everyone at PREM Rugby and our clubs is deeply saddened by the passing of Hyron Andrews and we extend our heartfelt sympathies to his family and friends.

'Our thoughts are also with Hyron’s team-mates past and present, everyone at the Lions and Sale Sharks, and the wider South African rugby community at this very difficult time.'

Hyron Andrews career Andrews spent the majority of his career playing in his native South Africa with the lock having joined the academy of Durban-based the Sharks in 2014. He made his debut for the Sharks in 2016 and made 83 appearances for the team, scoring three tries. Andrews was part of the Sharks side that reached the quarter-finals of the Champions Cup in 2023. The 6’8 lock joined Sale Sharks on an initial short-term deal in the 2023-24 season. He ultimately stayed at the PREM Rugby side for a further two seasons, playing 45 times in total. Andrews left at the end of last season to return to South Africa with the Lions. Internationally, Andrews represented South Africa at the 2015 World Rugby Under 20 Championship in 2015. The junior Springboks were beaten in the semi-finals by England, but won the third place match against France.

Andrews was a former South Africa Under-20 international.

Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union, said: 'This is terrible and distressing news. Our hearts go out to Hyron’s family and the whole Lions rugby community.

'There are no words to adequately convey our shock and the depth of sympathy we feel for his wife Maiglin and for his extended family, friends, team-mates and loved ones during this time of immense sorrow.

'Hyron was a respected member of the rugby community whose contribution to the game and impact on those around him will be remembered with great fondness.

'His untimely passing is a devastating loss and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him.

'The thoughts and prayers of the entire South African rugby family are with Maiglin and all those mourning his loss. May they find strength, comfort and peace in the memories they shared with him and in the support of those around them.'

In a bizarre coincidence, Andrews’ tragic passing occurred on the 10-year anniversary of the death of Munster legend Anthony Foley. A former Munster coach and captain, Foley died in his sleep on October 16, 2016, at the age of 42 in Paris on the eve of a European tie against Racing 92 after a heart condition caused fluid to build up in his lungs.

Ronan O’Gara, the current La Rochelle head coach, was an ex-Munster team-mate of Foley’s. Reports have suggested O’Gara headed to the team hotel of the Lions to offer the team’s grieving players and support staff emotional support. La Rochelle said they had learned of Andrews’ death with ‘immense sadness.’ They added: ‘The club extends its deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, team-mates, staff and the entire Lions family.

South African star Andrews played for Sale in England before leaving at the end of last season

‘To honour the memory of their team-mate and out of respect for La Rochelle and its fans, the Lions players and staff have decided, despite the circumstances, to play the match.

‘A minute's silence will be observed before kick-off. La Rochelle invites its supporters to join in this moment of reflection with the utmost respect.

‘La Rochelle remains by the side of the Lions in this ordeal.’

European Rugby organisers said: ‘It is with deep sadness that EPCR has learned of the tragic passing of 10bet Lions player Hyron Andrews while on tour ahead of their Investec Champions Cup and URC fixtures.’

The organisation’s chairman, Dominic McKay, said: ‘The thoughts of everyone at EPCR and the wider international rugby community are with Hyron’s wife Maiglin, his young sons, wider family, friends, team-mates, the 10bet Lions and all those who knew and loved him at this incredibly difficult time.’ In memory of Andrews, a moment’s silence will be held ahead of every Champions Cup and Challenge Cup match this weekend.

Those tributes began when Gloucester hosted French giants and current European champions Bordeaux on Friday night.

Sports.title: The fact Man United cannot drop Lisandro Martinez after his outburst just goes to show he was spot on about Sir Jim Ratcliffe's politburo of under-qualified, over-protected advisors, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
The fact Man United cannot drop Lisandro Martinez after his outburst just goes to show he was spot on about Sir Jim Ratcliffe's politburo of under-qualified, over-protected advisors, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

Lisandro Martinez will be in the Manchester United squad when they face Leeds on Sunday. And of course he will, because he was right about that shambling wreck of a club.

If he was wrong, and United were indeed a functional, intelligent organisation, he wouldn’t be anywhere near the bus for Elland Road. Not after what he said the other night.

A proper recruitment system would have meant there was enough defensive cover to drop a dissenting voice in questionable form. But United don’t have that. Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s politburo of under-qualified, over-protected advisors messed up another transfer window, so kicking Martinez into the long grass wasn’t an option.

In other words, if Jason Wilcox was better at his job then Martinez would have lost his and here’s a little list to support the point: Cristiano Ronaldo, Jadon Sancho, Marcus Rashford.

In the past few years, all of them have spoken out about those above them at United. And with the exception of Rashford, their feet didn’t touch the ground. Straight red. Rashford got put in the freezer for 18 months.

Martinez’s comments were slightly different, of course. He didn’t go after his manager, like Ronaldo and Sancho, and he didn’t turn up late and then flash some leg to potential suitors, like Rashford.

But he did sing a similar song by tearing strips off the regime in public. That used to be a hard no-no at Old Trafford, irrespective of how much truth was in the pudding.

We know that everything Martinez said about Wilcox and the club’s lack of ambition was accurate. We also know that his performance at the microphone was better than anything he has shown on the pitch in quite some time. No one could score points off him for accuracy, only his wisdom in stating the obvious and his reliability as a witness.

Michael Carrick says the club have moved on from Lisandro Martinez's comments after the defeat by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night

Sir Jim Ratcliffe brought in Jason Wilcox from Southampton in 2024

Michael Carrick’s position in all of this is quite interesting. Unlike Wilcox, he has to answer questions about rogue speakers, limited options and poor results and the links between them.

When the Martinez situation was put to him on Friday, he dealt with it the way he used to play, by taking the least fussy option – he managed upwards by not slapping his bosses and he limited his criticisms of Martinez to saying he made a ‘mistake’. Pinned into a tight space, he found a sensible pass.

Carrick couldn’t have done much better in that no-win scenario. But on some level, and in thoughts best kept to himself, he might even wish to thank Martinez. Because who else in-house has pinned United’s difficulties to the lapels of those who are largely responsible for this mess?

It won’t count for much in the long run, as it’s always the manager who carries the can. And some of the flak he has drawn in recent weeks is justified, of course. Same goes for the players.

But it is inconceivable to think Carrick, a smart man, would have supported the thinking behind a summer window in which United prepared for a return to a European workload by signing three midfielders and a back-up goalkeeper.

A window that offered no cover for a left-back in Luke Shaw, who has managed 25-plus Premier League games in four of his 12 seasons at United. A window that left Martinez and Harry Maguire as the first-choice centre-back pairing. A window that marked two years since they last signed a senior defender, the entirety of which has been spent under the watch of Wilcox, the director of directionless football.

Those are the decisions that shape seasons and what we are seeing from United is no surprise. We all called it a mile off. And we can all see Carrick’s points of exposure when Leeds are in the opposite corner.

Wilcox brought in Carlos Baleba from Brighton to complete United's transfer business this summer - he was the third midfielder they signed, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans

In many ways, they are the last thing he needs right now. They are a club that, for a number of reasons, highlight his shortcomings and those of United’s executive tier.

I was at their game against Arsenal and left with three main thoughts – Leeds dominated the champions for an hour, they are brilliantly organised by Daniel Farke and they know the value of a good defender.

Leeds didn’t have a spectacular window, but it was key to the building of a backline that is jointly the best in the Premier League so far. Nico Elvedi has been a good signing and Tarik Muharemovic an exceptional one; between them, they cost roughly the same as Youri Tielemans, with the difference being that Farke had a clear idea of how to use them.

It’s possible that Carrick will crack that code on Sunday – his team are good for attacking moments, if nothing else.

But it is also possible that Elland Road will prove the worst possible place for him to be, because so many of the areas where his side have under-performed are those where Farke has excelled.

A solid, physical midfield, a reliable defence, and a collective that operates with a detailed, well-understood plan has been shown so far this season by only one of the two clubs in the fixtures.

For Carrick, there is some blame to be swallowed there. But only some. The vast majority goes to higher planes, where the responsibility truly lies for United’s problems.

I would doubt Lisandro Martinez’s judgement in designating himself as the man to point it out. But he wasn’t wrong.

Sports.title: Man United WAGs 'forced to cancel night out' after Lisandro Martinez's bombshell outburst targeting club bosses - as Michael Carrick stresses both sides have 'moved on' after defender's public apology
Sports.content:
Man United WAGs 'forced to cancel night out' after Lisandro Martinez's bombshell outburst targeting club bosses - as Michael Carrick stresses both sides have 'moved on' after defender's public apology

Partners of Manchester United stars reportedly cancelled a planned night out amid the fallout from Lisandro Martinez's explosive interview.

A furious Martinez publicly criticised technical director Jason Wilcox and United’s top executives after defeat to Atletico Madrid for not backing manager Michael Carrick in the summer transfer window.

Martinez looked to clarify his remarks with a statement on Instagram on Wednesday – the squad’s allocated day off following the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid – before releasing a fresh statement after talks with Wilcox and the board.

The Argentine was also fined over his comments.

According to the Sun, wives and girlfriends of Man United stars decided to cancel a planned evening out on Thursday to keep a 'low profile'.

The partners are believed to have cancelled a booking at the Italian restaurant Cibo in Hale, an eatery popular with Man United's players and managers alike.

Partners of Man United stars reportedly cancelled a planned night out following the explosive interview given by Lisandro Martinez, left, in midweek (Source: Instagram/Muri Lopez)

Harry Maguire's wife Fern Hawkins, left, was among those expected to attend the dinner at the Italian restaurant Cibo before the cancellation

A floor of the restaurant was claimed to have been booked, but a decision was taken to cancel at the last minute.

The report alleged that the decision was taken after advice was given from the club to keep a low profile as the Red Devils looked to move on from controversy.

Martinez's partner Muri Lopez had reportedly been due to attend, along with Fern Hawkins and Ana Pinho, who are married to Harry Maguire and Bruno Fernandes respectively.

On Friday, Man United boss Michael Carrick insisted the club has moved on from Martinez's comments.

Carrick believes Martinez 'realised he has made a mistake' and insists the controversy will not distract Man United from turning their season around.

'We all understood the situation and what it meant. Lisandro obviously made his statement, and he acknowledges that it was a mistake from him, and that was it really. It's really not a drama for us as a group. We've genuinely moved on,' Carrick said on Friday.

'From our point of view, the acknowledgement of what's been done has certainly been enough. He's released his statement and he's realised he's made a mistake. I think that's enough for all of us to move on with. We're definitely not looking back at it now.'

Martinez is set to be in the Man United squad for their clash with Leeds on Sunday.

Sports.title: Nerves of steel: Trey Nyoni names Thiago as his inspiration as 19-year-old eyes first Premier League start for Liverpool at Brentford
Sports.content:
Trey Nyoni is pushing to start his first Premier League game for Liverpool on Saturday – and the teenage midfielder says he styles his game on Anfield icon Thiago.

The 19-year-old believes he has a stone-cold calmness and is thankful for the trust instilled in him by boss Andoni Iraola.

With Ryan Gravenberch suspended and Dominik Szoboszlai a doubt for the trip to Brentford, Nyoni makes sense to start after excelling in the 6-3 win at LASK on Wednesday night.

Asked who he models his composed game on, Nyoni said: ‘For me, I always watch players like Thiago. For me, Thiago, yeah, he is the guy!’

He added: ‘I don’t feel nervous at all, I don’t get nervous. With all the hard work I have put in to get to this moment and position, no.

‘I just want to show the manager and everyone what I can do, show the fans what I can do. I feel like in games like Wednesday, people have travelled a long way to see us play so I want to give them something back.

‘The manager has given me a lot of trust. He has given me so much responsibility. Ever since he came in, he has tried to make my life easy. He is helping a lot to adapt to the new position I am playing right now. I still have a lot of work to keep improving but right now I feel good.’

Nyoni is just one of several youngsters trusted by new boss Iraola.

Trey Nyoni was excellent in Liverpool's 6-3 win over LASK on Wednesday

Thiago won the FA Cup with Liverpool in 2022 and was a popular figure during his four-year spell at Anfield

Fellow teenager Rio Ngumoha, has elbowed his way into regular starts and has impressed England boss Thomas Tuchel.

‘He knows he is elite at certain things,’ said Iraola on Ngumoha, 18. ‘If you want to put someone one versus one then Rio is one of the best players you would choose because he is difficult to contain. There are areas he has to improve, especially without the ball.

‘Body wise he is becoming stronger and I think he is in a good place. Obviously I had seen him play and we had played against him (at Bournemouth) but for us it is a privilege to have Rio in the team because he has just become 18.

‘He has already played some minutes with the national team and that is not something normal.’

Forward Lewis Koumas is also a favourite of the manager because of his relentless off-the-ball work and unselfish team play.

When asked about the young players keeping experienced heads out of the side, Koumas said: ‘There is a buzz and it gives us all a motivation to keep going. We are getting chances but, ultimately, it is because we are good enough.

'Trey and Rio are unbelievable and, if you are good enough it doesn’t matter how old you are.

Lewis Koumas is another Liverpool youngster making an impression - and scored his first senior goal for the club against LASK

‘Every time you see them play... look at Trey, how mature he is and how he manages the game. He dictates how the game is going to go. He’s 19! He shows levels all the time.’

Koumas missed a chance at 0-0 against Manchester City last week and added: ‘I couldn’t really sleep (after). I just kept thinking about the chance, to be honest. I feel like I couldn’t have hit it any better.

‘The keeper (Gianluigi Donnarumma) is huge and he was just in the right place and I think in normal circumstances it goes in.

‘I just want to keep on improving. You never know when your last game is going to be. I know that sounds like a cliche but it is true. Alex (Isak) will be back soon training, Cody (Gakpo) will be fit soon. I have just got to keep pushing every chance I get.

‘I was thinking about the chance all night. It was the only one I had in the game and I honestly couldn’t have hit it better but I was absolutely gutted it never went in.’

Sports.title: 'When it really matters, England would choose Pickford': Everton boss David Moyes insists his No1 is better than ever despite pressure for his international place... and says he remains a better kicker than rival James Trafford
Sports.content:
Jordan Pickford is better than ever at the age of 32 and is not feeling fazed by James Trafford’s challenge for the England No1 jersey, according to Everton boss David Moyes.

Trafford, who signed for Leeds from Manchester City in the summer after starring in the Carabao Cup and FA Cup finals, elbowed Pickford out of the Three Lions XI for two of four games in the recent international window.

But Moyes said: ‘When Jordan came back from the World Cup, it might be the best I have ever seen him. He was lean, sharp, his footwork was brilliant, he was fast across the goal. He has made a couple of brilliant saves (this season).

‘He is lean and ready to train. I talked to him about it, I said; “You know you have a bit of competition now with Trafford, how are you going to deal with it?” and I don’t see Jordan falling away at the moment.

‘I see Jordan keeping his pride because he wants clean sheets, he wants to keep the ball out of the net. Somewhere along the line there is a whippersnapper coming who tries to challenge you, but if it really mattered to England, Jordan would still be the one who was there.

Jordan Pickford has kept three clean sheets in his first six Premier League games this season

‘He has that experience and he is not ageing. Jordan is a terrific kicker of the ball, he is a better kicker than Trafford, but passing is a different equation. One of the first passes in England’s game against the Czech Republic, Jordan played a long ball and put Morgan Rogers through. So he has got that.’

Pickford is all but guaranteed his spot at Everton but one player under some pressure at Hill Dickinson Stadium is Jack Grealish, with the energetic winger Tyrique George, 20, breathing down his neck after a strong start to the season.

George, who signed from Chelsea in the summer, will face his old team on Saturday if picked and Moyes added: ‘We like Tyrique a lot. I want to get him some rhythm, he had a bit and then we took it away because we wanted Jack’s experience.

‘Tyrique is well in our thoughts. He has to keep learning, getting better, but he has the ability to beat people, to score, we don’t want to knock him down but he is still a young boy.

‘Tyrique is knocking on the door. He started a bit slowly and then picked up. Jack is aware that Tyrique is there. We think he can do a job on both sides as well.’

Jarrad Branthwaite is hopeful of being fit after managing a problem this week, while left back Vitalii Mykolenko is pushing to return from an injury. Christian Norgaard is also on the comeback trail but won’t be fit enough to start.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy opens his account for Burnley as former Leicester star, 39, scores in his 20TH consecutive season - but can't save the Clarets from Wolves comeback
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy scored his first goal for Burnley but the veteran forward was unable to prevent his new club from suffering their fifth league defeat of the season against Wolves. Vardy started up front for the Clarets in a battle between two sides who were relegated from the Premier League last season. The 39-year-old opened his account for his new club in typical fashion, as he raced onto a through ball from Jacob Bruun Larsen and slotted past Wolves goalkeeper Jose Sa. Vardy's strike ensured he has scored in 20 consecutive seasons in his career, which spans from his time in the non-league's Northern Premier League through his rise to Premier League glory with Leicester, and his season in Serie A last term. The forward joined Burnley last month having been a free agent since leaving Italian side Cremonese in the summer following their relegation to Serie B. Vardy, who moved to Italy with his wife Rebekah and their family, scored seven goals and provided three assists in 29 appearances in Serie A last season. Jamie Vardy scored his first goal since joining Burnley on a free transfer last month The veteran forward, now 39, has now scored in 20 consecutive seasons Burnley suffered a 2-1 defeat as Wolves fought back to increase the Clarets' woes Vardy's first goal for his new club gave Burnley a 1-0 lead in their Championship clash with Wolves. The Clarets were unable to hold onto their lead with Kyle Walker at fault for Wolves' equaliser. Walker was dispossessed by Sean Neave, who crossed for Fer Lopez to slot the visitors level with a near post finish. Another defensive error led to Wolves' winning goal with Burnley's Igor Julio's errant touch presenting Mateus Mane with the ball. Mane fed substitute Tawanda Chirewa, who had been on the pitch for 21 seconds, shooting through Burnley goalkeeper Gregoire Coudert. The result increased pressure on Burnley head coach Nicky Hayen, with the Clarets just outside the relegation zone after winning one, drawing five and losing five of their 11 Championship matches to date. Defeat also meant Burnley have gone over a year since winning a league match at home. Wolves' fifth victory of the campaign lifted them into sixth place.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois' second clash with Fabio Wardley promises to be even MORE brutal than their first, writes JEFF POWELL MBE - as May's champion vows to 'bash and smash' his rival
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois' second clash with Fabio Wardley promises to be even MORE brutal than their first, writes JEFF POWELL MBE - as May's champion vows to 'bash and smash' his rival

Even the most hardened boxing fans can be taken aback by the depths of brutality which two men are capable of inflicting on each other. Especially the heavyweights.

So it was on the Saturday night this May when Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley battered hell's bells out of each other in Manchester’s Co-op Live Arena. Wardley dropped his world title challenger twice in the first three rounds. Just 28 seconds into the 11th, Dubois had to be pulled off the champion he had reduced to a bleeding and battered but still-standing wreck.

We mere mortals can only ask: How on earth do they do it? ‘We’re fighters,’ says Dubois. ‘Honoured to share a ring with him.’

‘Born to do it,’ says Wardley, who found out that truth of himself when he tried white collar boxing. ‘Love being in with such a great fighter.’

What in heaven goes through their minds at the prospect of doing it again, as they are on Saturday night at the O2? Do they not realise the danger this sledgehammer head-banging presents to their health?

Prepare yourselves, dear gentle readers, for this stunning answer from Dubois: ‘Dementia? If you’re talking about dementia, no point worrying. We’ve probably got it already.’

Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley have both spoken of their love for stepping into the ring with one another ahead of their rematch on Saturday

But as brutal as their meeting in May was, tomorrow night's clash at the O2 has been teased as even bloodier

A chilling insight, this, into the mentality of men who fight not only for a living but for the lust for glory, the thrill of battle, the roar of the crowd, the smell of the greasepaint, the glare of the lights and not least their manly pride.

And on nights like this, for a world championship. This time the WBO belt which Dubois ripped from Wardley’s fairy-tale grasp five months ago.

What, no nerves? ‘I live with the chaos,’ says Dubois. ‘Chaos all day every day and specially on the night. I love the fear. It gives me the power. I hold the chaos in until it’s at its peak when the first bell goes. Then it explodes as I let it out. Which brings power and clarity.’

Wardley comes not only from his different background in commerce but also with an opposite mindset. He says: ‘No one wants to lose a world title but if it has to be, then what really matters is how it happens.

‘I feel more relaxed and confident having proved I can engage a top-level fighter in a great fight, which everyone expected me to lose easily. Calm makes me better.’

That and the lessons he learned in the five months since his gladiatorial — and only — defeat thus far. ‘We’ve studied every critical moment of the first fight,’ he says. ‘And I’ve adapted where necessary. Had to because I have more to work on than Daniel with all his experience.

‘But we’ve not only looked at me. We’ve looked at him. He’s not as adaptable as me. He’s not suddenly going to become light-footed and free moving. I’ll give him something different.’

To which Dubois says: ‘I’ll give him another beating. Bash him up. Smash him worse than before. And quicker. We didn’t know quite what he might do in the first fight. Now I know what to expect.

‘I also know that he’s not good enough to adapt. I’m his daddy now.’ That is clarity, Dubois style. He also discounts those two knock-downs. As a man who has been a slow starter at times — although not when he demolished Anthony Joshua from the get-go — he says: ‘Things happen in boxing. You can get caught. But I also know now that he doesn’t have the power. No real power.’

Wardley, for his part, denies that he was as badly hurt as it appeared in fight one. Their respective trainers have disagreed about the 11th-hour stoppage. Dubois’ coach Don Charles says the towel should have been thrown in earlier.

Wardley supports his man Ben Davison’s assertion that he was still in the fight throwing punches, saying: ‘The optics looked bad, what with the blood and the bruising and the punches. But I trust my team to take care of me. Trust them with my life.

‘A lot of the punches were glancing and in the 10th round I shook him with an uppercut. If the big right that followed had connected cleanly we might have had a different ending.’

This man who escaped office drudgery to chase his dream hopes to go on to meet the December winner of Joshua v Tyson Fury. Dubois fancies some of that big money but is also looking beyond, to unifying all the other world titles vacated by Oleksandr Usyk.

Will the ending on Saturday be different from Wardley v Dubois One? Probably not. Dynamite Dan likely added the more valuable knowledge to his wider experience and has never looked this bullish before a fight.

What we do know for sure is that this pair will give us another thriller.

Sports.title: Peter Schmeichel explains 'clumsy' Lisandro Martinez interview after Man United fans claimed he 'tried to shift the conversation' to 'the good news' after Argentine's explosive outburst
Sports.content:
Peter Schmeichel explains 'clumsy' Lisandro Martinez interview after Man United fans claimed he 'tried to shift the conversation' to 'the good news' after Argentine's explosive outburst

Peter Schmeichel has conceded his interview with Lisandro Martinez was 'clumsy' following criticism from Man United supporters, after admitting he was caught by surprise when he was presented with the chance to speak to the defender.

Martinez delivered an extraordinary outburst to Amazon Prime accusing Manchester United's chiefs of lacking ambition in the transfer market after his side suffered a 2-0 defeat against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

After his explosive post-match interview, Martinez had joined Man United legend Schmeichel on American network CBS Sports and continued to hit out at the board for failing to build a suitably competitive squad for the season.

Several Red Devils fans were unimpressed by Schmeichel's line of questioning during the interview, disappointed that he appeared to try and find a 'positive' to soften Martinez's attack on the board.

Speaking on the Overlap, Schmeichel revealed he had not been due to interview Martinez post-match and that the defender had been presented to him moments after giving his explosive comments.

Peter Schmeichel has admitted his interview with Lisandro Martinez was 'clumsy' after the former Man United star was criticised by supporters for his 'positive' approach

Schmeichel revealed he had not been due to interview Martinez and was caught by surprise, while admitting he was unaware of his explosive comments moments before to Amazon

'It’s a little bit of a weird one. When I do my job in the Champions League, I do a couple of pieces to camera from the touchline about the atmosphere, and afterwards I go to the flash zone and do interviews,' Schmeichel said.

'You build relationships with the media people from the different clubs, and you can say you want to speak to him or him, but at the end of the day they’re not solely in charge of who you get to speak to, because the UEFA also has media people on.

'There’s one responsible for every team, then there’s one above them, and everything has to go through them.

'When this happened, I was next to TNT Sports, and Gabriel [Clarke] interviewed Martínez. That interview is where everything came out. I knew he was there, but he wasn’t on my list. I wasn’t interviewing him at all. I’d asked for somebody else.

'That interview finished, and they pushed him into mine. So, when you look at the interview, I’m a little bit surprised. At that point I didn’t know what he’d said.

'Then in my interview he says, "We should do a lot better." He’s carrying on from that interview, but I don’t know what he’s saying. Because he’s speaking to a former player, I thought he was saying that we, as players, should do a lot better.

'I had no clue he was on the attack the way he was. I didn’t understand that he was saying all that, so in a way my interview became a little bit clumsy in the greater scheme of things.'

Schmeichel, who won the Champions League in 1999 during Man United's historic Treble-winning season, had begun his interview by asking Martinez to explain the team’s poor run of form having gone five games without a win.

Martinez will be in Man United's squad on Sunday after apologising to Man United chiefs for his comments

Martinez responded by again taking aim at the board by criticising the size of United's squad, insisting a lack of depth makes it difficult to compete.

'The rotation in the team, we have many games and have to rotate players. For me, we don't have the best squad,' Martinez said. 'For sure, when you watch the television, you see the player and the manager and you point the finger, which is right - we take responsibility - but also as a club I expect more.

'I'm not going to close my mouth. We need more ambition, we need to talk more about winning Champions Leagues, winning Premier Leagues.'

To that, Schmeichel responded: 'But the good news is that we're only in October, there's a long way to go.' Cutting him off, Martinez interjected: 'Yes, but every season we are saying the same thing. If we don't say the truth, nothing will change.'

Martinez will be in United's squad to face Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday after he apologised for criticising director of football Jason Wilcox and club bosses in a television interview which landed the 28-year-old defender with a fine.

On Thursday evening, after talks with United, Martinez shared a social media post apologising.

'Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager,' he said: 'It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

'Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

'The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.'

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Points deduction size emerges as Premier League rivals 'fuming'
Sports.content:
All of the latest Manchester City 114 charges news with updates on their potential points deduction and the reaction of Premier League rivals

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live blog on the Manchester City charges case...

Last month, the Premier League confirmed an independent commission found City guilty of 114 financial breaches but the process still has a long way to run. City have appealed the decision and a final outcome this season is seen as unlikely even though a sanctions hearing is also set to take place.

Discussed at that will be all the potential punishments, ranging from a hefty fine to expulsion from the Premier League, with City warned they could face 'multiple double figure' points deductions.

The process being drawn out has already angered other top-flight clubs with many of the belief it is impacting their ability to qualify for the Champions League while others are more concerned about potential legal costs.

With all of that being said, stay with us throughout the day for the latest news and updates on the Man City charges case!

Sports.title: Hollywood star Jude Law to play Liverpool legend Bill Shankly in new TV series
Sports.content:
Hollywood star Jude Law to play Liverpool legend Bill Shankly in new TV series

A new series from Jack Thorne, the acclaimed writer of Adolescence, will focus on Bill Shankly's reign as Liverpool manager which saw the Reds go from the old Second Division to being champions of England

View 2 Images Jude Law will play the iconic manager (Image: Patrick T. Fallon/AFP)

Jude Law is set to play legendary former Liverpool manager Bill Shankly in a new TV series. Written by Jack Thorne of Adolescence fame, the show will be focus on Shankly's success at Anfield, as he transformed Liverpool into a global footballing powerhouse.

‌



‌



Liverpool chairman Tom Werner believes that the series could become like The Crown and follow the club beyond Shankly's reign further seasons. Under the Scot - who passed away in 1981 - Liverpool were promoted from the old Second Division and would go on to win three First Division titles, two FA Cups, four Charity Shields and one UEFA Cup in his 15-year reign on Merseyside.

‌



Werner told Deadline, who broke the news of Law's casting: "It's a story about family and relationships through the lens of a football club. My feeling is, if you do nothing more in that first episode than show 50,000 people singing You'll Never Walk Alone, I defy anyone who won't be moved by that one scene."

‌



Law, who is a BAFTA winner and two-time Oscar nominee, supports one of Liverpool's Premier League rivals, Tottenham. The 53-year-old is also a fan of cricket.

Shankly's granddaughter, Karen Gill, is involved alongside production company Box To Box Films. Filming will take place in Liverpool and at Anfield, giving the series an authentic feel.

Gill commented: "I think it's a wonderful way to share the story of my grandad's time at LFC. Anybody who knows anything about the club knows what it meant to Bill Shankly.

"This is going to be a must watch for all Liverpool fans and it's a privilege to have the chance now to showcase his story to the wider world. I'm looking forward to seeing how this project unfolds and being a part of it."

‌



Where will Liverpool finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bill Shankly had a profound impact on the city of Liverpool (Image: Central Press/Getty Images)

Thorne added: "I'm excited to be telling this incredible story and it's an honour to be working alongside A24 and Liverpool Football Club. Our goal is to focus not just on the club, but on the city itself - because, and this is one thing Bill Shankly made sure, the club belongs to the city and the city belongs to the club.

Article continues below

"We have a chance with this show to celebrate both a magnificent football club and a magnificent city, whilst being honest about the struggles of the 1960s and 1970s in one of our industrial heartlands. We hope to honour the fans, to the city, and the legacy of Liverpool FC in bringing its story to life."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sets Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres challenges amid Arsenal exit talk
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sets Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres challenges amid Arsenal exit talk

Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres have struggled to to find consistent form since joining Arsenal from Chelsea and Sporting Lisbon respectively and both have been linked with moves away

View 3 Images Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres have endured tricky form at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has backed Noni Madueke to show his real quality and deliver for Arsenal when they need him most. Madueke, 24, has been hit-and-miss since joining Arsenal in a huge £52m move from Chelsea in the summer of 2025.

‌



‌



England winger Madueke has struggled to hold down a regular place at the Emirates amid competition from Bukayo Saka, Eberechi Eze and now Christos Tzolis. Madueke has also lost his England place after being dropped for the first squad since the World Cup as he tries to rediscover his form.

‌



But Arteta says that Madueke now has a big opportunity in the next few weeks with Tzolis out injured and he believes the former Chelsea winger will take his chance. Gunners boss Arteta said: “If we give the possibility to any player to give him two or three or four games in a row, I think everybody will appreciate that because they will get more familiar with the players, more minutes, more confidence.

‌



“If things go well, that is the ideal thing to do with all of them. He had a few and he will have more minutes in the next few games. I am sure that we will start to see a closer version of Noni at the highest level.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Madueke has always looked better on the right wing, cutting onto his favored left foot. But he started on the left against Leeds and will probably do the same against Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

Arteta insists that Madueke can adapt and also be effective on either side especially as he can get some momentum with a run of games. Arteta said: “It’s down to necessities as well, sometimes, more than probably tactical decisions so far with him. I think he can play in both positions. He offers something completely different.

“Obviously now we have the necessity of a player on the left side with different qualities than Ebs as well, that can complement all the other unit we have on that left hand side. It’s great because he is comfortable there, he is enjoying playing there, and he is doing well. It’s a good solution.

‌



View 3 Images Noni Madueke joined Arsenal from Chelsea last summer (Image: Getty Images)

“That's what we want, players to be available and robust enough to be available always but if they're not, somebody else. The good thing is that when someone has come in, whether that's Ebs or Noni they have performed.”

Arteta has had a miserable recent record at Forest’s City Ground - just one win from five visits - and the last two have been two goalless draws. They will be looking to improve on that and Arteta says they must take encouragement from back to back wins since the international break.

‌



“We have responded really well in the last two games, two very good performances and results,” said Arteta. “Now we just focus on the game against Forest which I know is going to be a really tough one.”

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres has yet to score for Arsenal this season (Image: Getty Images)

There was also a challenge for Viktor Gyokeres who has yet to score for Arsenal this season and looks off the pace as he has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order. But Arteta says it is down to Gyokeres to repeat his prolific form for Sweden as he even made Nations League history by scoring in six consecutive games in the competition.

‌



Arteta added: “These are moments in a player's career, or in a season, I would say. And we are trying to help him as much as possible.

“The other day, I think, he had some very good moments. He's three or four times in front of goal with no keeper and the ball should arrive to him and it doesn't.

“And maybe you are talking about something else. But these are the strikers. It's very small margins. Scoring or not scoring changes the narrative, for sure not the perception of how much he can help the team.”

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca admits he may have to DROP Erling Haaland for Man City
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca admits he may have to DROP Erling Haaland for Man City

Erling Haaland has started the season on fire by scoring 10 goals in nine games for Manchester City, but Enzo Maresca has admitted that his place in the starting XI isn't certain

View 2 Images Erling Haaland has started every game for club and country this season (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has admitted that he may be forced to drop Erling Haaland and give him some rest. Haaland, 26, has enjoyed a typically prolific start to the season, despite an unusually busy summer.

‌



‌



The striker fired Norway to the quarter-finals of the World Cup in what was his first major tournament appearance with his country. Haaland started all four of Norway's games during the recent international break, and national team manager Stale Solbakken confirmed that his No.9 was fatigued after substituting him during their fourth and final match.

‌



Maresca acknowledges that Haaland needs time off to avoid injury, with City due to play Ipswich on Saturday and AEK Athens in the Champions League, also at home, next Tuesday. "At some point we probably need to give him rest, some days off," Maresca said in his pre-match press conference.

‌



"We are thinking about this not just with Erling because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams. Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernandez], Marc [Guehi], Erling, Ruben [Dias]. So at some point we probably need to give them some rest."

Haaland's double against Paris Saint-Germain in midweek put him on 10 goals in nine games for City this season. The Norwegian leads the Premier League scoring charts with six, one more than Chelsea's Joao Pedro.

City are top of the table with a 100 per cent record after six games. Victory over Ipswich would open up a six-point gap over defending champions Arsenal, who play on Sunday away to Nottingham Forest.

Maresca will have Phil Foden at his disposal following his red card against Manchester United prior to the international break. "Since his red card and the international break, it has been quite long, but he is training well and is very positive," the City boss added.

‌



Can Enzo Maresca afford to rest Erling Haaland? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca knows that he needs to rotate (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

"We have so many games [coming up] so we will decide if he starts [on Saturday] or not. There is no doubt that he is going to give us something."

Article continues below

Ayyoub Bouaddi will be in contention to start against Ipswich after he impressed as a substitute on Wednesday. "I decided to go less physicality and more technical with Rayan [Cherki], but against these teams you need to be quite strong in the middle," Maresca explained.

"Bouaddi, Enzo and Elliot can for sure be a solution in the future. He is a fantastic player. When he is on the pitch, all the players around him improve. They are better players."

Sports.title: Peter Schmeichel reveals what really happened in Lisandro Martinez interview - 'Clumsy'
Sports.content:
Peter Schmeichel reveals what really happened in Lisandro Martinez interview - 'Clumsy'

Peter Schmeichel spoke to Lisandro Martinez moments after the Manchester United star made explosive comments in a separate interview following Tuesday's 2-0 defeat away to Atletico Madrid

View 2 Images Peter Schmeichel was caught off guard by Lisandro Martinez (Image: CBS Sports)

Peter Schmeichel has addressed criticism of his interview with Lisandro Martinez, admitting that it was 'clumsy'. Schmeichel spoke to Martinez moments after the Manchester United defender had, in a separate interview, slammed the club's leadership and called out director of football Jason Wilcox.

‌



‌



The 28-year-old was unhappy with their efforts in the summer transfer window in which United only signed four players. Martinez's comments came in an interview with Prime Video Sport's Gabriel Clarke after the Red Devils had lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

‌



After speaking to Clarke, Martinez chatted with Schmeichel, who was working as CBS Sports' pitchside reporter at the Metropolitano. Fans on social media criticised the United legend for 'trying to be positive' as he attempted to shift the conversation to on-the-pitch matters.

‌



It turns out that Schmeichel didn't know the context behind Martinez's words. Appearing on The Overlap, sponsored by Sky Bet, he explained: "It's a bit of a weird one. My job is I do a couple of things to camera from the touchline, I'm there, I'm talking about the atmosphere and anything I've heard. And afterwards I go to the flash zone and do interviews.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"You're building relationships with the media people from the different clubs and you can say, 'I want to speak to him or him'. But at the end of the day they're not solely in charge of who you get to speak to UEFA also has media people on.

"There's one responsible for every team, then there's one above them, and everything has to go through them. When this happened, I'm actually next to TNT (sic), and Gabriel [Clarke] interviewed Lisandro Martinez. That interview is where everything came out.

"I know he's there, he's not on my list. I'm not interviewing him at all because I've asked for somebody else. This interview finishes and they push him into mine. So, when you look at the interview, I'm a little bit surprised. I don't know what he'd said at this time.

‌



"Then in interview with me he says, 'We should do a lot better'. He's carrying on from that interview, but I don't know what he's saying. Because he's speaking to a former player, I think he's saying that we, as players, should do a lot better.

Should Lisandro Martinez start against Leeds? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez gave a bombshell interview to Gabriel Clarke (Image: Florencia Tan Jun - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

‌



"I had no clue he was on the attack the way he was. So in my interview, I didn't understand that he was saying all that, so in a way my interview became a little bit clumsy in the greater scheme of things."

Joe Hart then asked Schmeichel what he'd have done differently had he known the full context. The former goalkeeper replied: "Definitely, I would've asked him if he felt that he was in a position to say that. I don't think players should ever come out and say anything like that."

United manager Michael Carrick confirmed on Friday that Martinez, who's been fined by the club and has issued an apology, will be part of the squad for Sunday's game against Leeds. Carrick insists that United have moved on from the drama and are focussed on getting their first win since September 10.

Sports.title: Punter collects nearly £20,000 windfall from ‘stroke of genius’ four-fold accumulator
Sports.content:
Punter collects nearly £20,000 windfall from ‘stroke of genius’ four-fold accumulator

The William Hill customer spent £10 on a £5 each way bet involving runners at Perth on Thursday, all of which won including one at odds of 12-1

View Image A William Hill customer won a five figure amount (Image: Getty Images)

A punter has collected nearly £20,000 in winnings from a ‘stroke of genius’ bet. The William Hill customer staked £10 on a £5 each way accumulator comprising four horse running at Perth on Thursday.

‌



The first leg was landed when Kershaw, backed at 13-2, won the 1:55pm maiden hurdle and that was followed by Thunder Rock, who captured the next handicap chase at odds of 11-4. The third selection scored at double digit odds when She’s Notjoeking took the 2m handicap hurdle at a starting price of 12-1.

The punter was in clover when Tanking Along brought up the final leg, winning a 2m4f handicap chase. He had been backed at 13-2 and returned an SP of 4-1.

‌



Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Saturday on ITV READ MORE :

The customer’s winning bet also benefitted from a 50 percent boost on their winning selections through William Hill’s Racing Winnings Boost, resulting in a final return of £19,136.13.

The bookmaker’s spokesperson Lee Phelps said: “One of our customers is heading into the weekend over £19k richer after picking four winners at Perth on Thursday.

“After Kershaw and Thunder Rock kicked off the spree, She’s Notjoeking stepped up to the plate at 12-1 before Tanking Along got the job done at Perth on Thursday afternoon.

“Picking the winner in four consecutive races is no easy feat, but to have them all in the same four-fold accumulator is a stroke of genius, so we have to take our hats off to this punter after their big win.”

Sports.title: Reece James suffers yet another injury blow as Chelsea captain undergoes surgery
Sports.content:
Reece James suffers yet another injury blow as Chelsea captain undergoes surgery

Chelsea have been without Reece James for their last two matches, and Blues manager Xabi Alonso will now have to deal with the absence of his captain for much longer

View 2 Images Reece James faces another lengthy layoff (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Reece James is set be ruled out for THREE MONTHS after having surgery on his knee. James, 26, missed Chelsea's last two games either side of the international break with an injury that forced him to withdraw from the England squad last month.

‌



‌



And now the Blues captain looks unlikely to return before the new year. Chelsea confirmed on Friday that James has undergone a minor knee operation after picking up the injury in training.

‌



A statement from the club added: "Reece has already begun his road to recovery and will be supported by the club's medical department at Cobham during this rehabilitation phase. Everyone at Chelsea wishes Reece a speedy recovery and will support him on his road to return."

‌



James previously suffered a knee injury in 2022 which saw him miss that year's World Cup. The defender's fitness improved last season, allowing him to play a prominent role for England at the 2026 edition.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has used James in midfield this term and on Friday described his absence as 'disappointing'. "It's not going to be a two or three-week thing, it's going to be longer and after that we will see," Alonso told a pre-match press conference ahead of Saturday's game away to Everton.

"Before Christmas, after Christmas, time will tell. Things have to be done properly so that he feels right and is in the best possible condition.

"It's a disappointment for everyone, for him, but we need to have a squad to deal with injuries. We support him, he will stay close to the team, he's a great influence even when he's not available, and we wish him the best recovery."

‌



James' injury coincides with a difficult run of fixtures for the Blues. After facing Everton, Chelsea host Tottenham and then Manchester United either side of a trip to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup.

Will Chelsea beat Everton? Give us your score prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso could be without Reece James until 2027 (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



Levi Colwill has captained Chelsea since James was sidelined and Alonso is confident that he has enough leaders. "We have Moi (Moises Caicedo), we have Levi, we have players who take responsibility and carry that role in a perfect way," the Spaniard stressed.

"They have the support from the rest and the players respect them when they wear the armband, so it's no bother. Their own personality. Each one is different. Levi is different from Reece, Moi is different, Cole [Palmer], Hendo (Jordan Henderson).

"Each one is different, Dibu (Emiliano Martinez) as well. That's why it's so important for me to have a mix of personalities, qualities and stages of their careers. I think we're in a good place in that way."

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star would snub Erling Haaland transfer and prefers two Man City defenders
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star would snub Erling Haaland transfer and prefers two Man City defenders

Erling Haaland has continued his goalscoring exploits at Manchester City ever since his move from Borussia Dortmund at the expense of rivals United on a number of occasions

View 2 Images Erling Haaland has enjoyed a brilliant spell with Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Manchester United star Paul Parker has revealed he WOULDN’T want the Red Devils to sign Erling Haaland. The Norwegian striker has enjoyed a stunning period at Manchester City with his 172 goals in 207 appearances powering the club to two Premier League titles and a Champions League crown, as well as a whole host of other trophies.

‌



‌



Haaland has also put together a brilliant record against United with nine goals in 11 career appearances. But former star Parker has suggested that he would not sign the forward if given the chance.

‌



Speaking to PariuriX.com, he said: “It's probably not realistic anyway, but I wouldn't take Haaland at Man Utd. I wouldn't want to see him at the club with the way he plays. I would say no to him. He is an easy one for everyone to look at but it wouldn't be me. I am not even interested in him.”

‌



“I would be looking at Nico O'Reilly and Marc Guehi. Nico O'Reilly is a super player. Elliot Anderson doesn't interest me at all.

“Marc Guehi isn't the player he was at Crystal Palace, but Man Utd needs straightening in the back four and he is the one I would be looking at.”

Haaland has been linked with moves to United in the past, with former boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer having explained that he urged the Red Devils to make a move.

He said: “I had him [Haaland] in Molde, for two seasons. The summer before I got here, I rang the club and said, ‘You’ve got to sign this boy. He’ll be top class’.

‌



“That was June, July 2018, and they said no. They had enough reports on players. Then I became the caretaker manager, and we’d sold Haaland to RB Salzburg.

I tell the club straight away to buy him while he has a release clause. We knew that then, and no one else would’ve paid the money - €20m, it would’ve been a bargain.

“It was the club’s decision to not go for it then. We never made bids or went in for him, until after he started scoring for Salzburg.

“By then, Borussia Dortmund were there, Juventus were there, everyone was there. His release clause then was still good - €60m.”

Haaland will be aiming to get back on the scoresheet this weekend as City take on newly-promoted Ipswich Town at the Etihad Stadium.
