Sports.title: Bam Rodriguez Offers March, But Inoue May Move On
Sports.content:
Jesse Rodriguez is willing to meet Naoya Inoue in March, yet that timeline still depends entirely on the undisputed champion waiting for him. Inoue may prefer an earlier ring return, which would leave Rodriguez on the outside looking in as he continues handling business at bantamweight.

Trainer Robert Garcia revealed that Rodriguez can make a March date work, moving up his original April or May target. Still, the camp intends to take on WBO champion Christian Medina in December first.

Robert confirmed the updated outlook to The Ring: “I previously said April or May, but we can be ready for March.”

While that shortens the wait, early 2027 remains unresolved. Turki Alalshikh pointed toward a January appearance in Japan. Eddie Hearn mentioned February or March instead. Clear alignment on a date is completely absent.

Rodriguez must fulfill a contract before New Year’s Eve, with Garcia eyeing December 11 or December 19 against Medina. The camp figures Rodriguez can enjoy the holidays, then jump straight into camp for Inoue.

That expectation rests on an ideal outcome against Medina. Cuts, bruised knuckles, or an unexpectedly brutal bout could easily force Rodriguez to take extra recovery time. Inoue would effectively be pinning his calendar on a fighter who still has to survive another bout first.

Inoue is already eyeing an eventual jump to featherweight. Sitting around waiting for Rodriguez to finish his stay at 118 pounds makes little sense for the Japanese star.

Garcia admitted neither he nor Hearn has received an official approach to begin talks. The public chatter is moving much faster than the paperwork.

Putting March on the table does not guarantee Inoue’s cooperation. If March works on both sides, the matchup can happen. If Inoue wants to fight sooner, Rodriguez will either have to scrap his December plans or watch this major fight slip away.

Bam is acting like someone who wants the glory of calling out Inoue without actually taking the risk of meeting him on his terms.

When a fighter gets an invitation to share a ring with the sport’s biggest pound-for-pound attraction, they drop everything. They do not tell the undisputed champion to take a number and wait until spring because Christian Medina is on the calendar. That makes zero sense. A routine belt grab against Medina does nothing for Rodriguez’s profile, brings in a fraction of the money, and accomplishes very little that fans care about.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley’s Team Wants Daniel Dubois Fouls Policed
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley’s team wants tighter control of Daniel Dubois’ head-first attacks in Saturday’s rematch, with manager Michael Ofo calling for stronger officiating after their first fight.

The concern is about Wardley being able to punch without Dubois driving into him with his head. Those collisions can interrupt an attack, knock a fighter out of position, and make him hesitate before throwing again.

Dubois recovered from two knockdowns to stop Wardley in May and take the WBO heavyweight title. Ahead of their return at London’s O2 Arena, Ofo has accused the champion of leading with his head and using a tackle during that fight.

“We’re calling for a stronger referee, because it’s needed,” Ofo told Sky Sports Boxing.

Dubois’ trainer Don Charles rejected the criticism, describing the opposing camp’s complaints as “insecurity and weakness.”

Wardley’s camp has a reasonable case for asking the referee to watch those entries closely. When Dubois comes forward behind his punches, head contact can make it difficult for Wardley to plant his feet and counter. Intent is difficult to establish, but repeated collisions still need attention.

That becomes especially important if Wardley hurts Dubois again. He needs the opportunity to follow up without a foul interrupting his work and giving the champion time to recover.

However, Wardley cannot build his approach around the referee intervening. His jab has to give Dubois something to get past, and combinations would make him less predictable than loading up on individual power shots. Moving after punching could also reduce the opportunities for Dubois to drive into him.

Wardley showed he could hurt Dubois in the first fight. The harder task is turning those moments into a finish while avoiding another punishing battle at close range. Firmer officiating could help, but his own adjustments will have to do most of the work. Wardley cannot rely on the third man to solve that puzzle.

If Dubois is going to be stopped from barreling in head-first, Wardley has to make the physical cost of doing so intolerable, just like Oleksandr Usyk did.

Sports.title: Sugar Ray Robinson’s Unbeaten Run Goes Beyond 50-0
Sports.content:
Sugar Ray Robinson’s 91-fight unbeaten run deserves greater recognition than boxing’s fixation on 50-0 allows. He built it after his first defeat, showing how much a fighter can accomplish once a perfect career record is gone.

Floyd Mayweather finished his professional career at 50-0, an exceptional achievement. Robinson’s sequence lasted 41 fights longer, and the case for its superiority rests on more than the number. It included repeated victories over championship opposition while Robinson won world titles at welterweight and middleweight.

Jake LaMotta handed Robinson his first professional defeat in February 1943. Robinson fought him again just three weeks later and won. That willingness to return immediately against the man who had beaten him helped launch a run that continued until Randy Turpin defeated him in 1951.

During those 91 unbeaten fights, Robinson defeated LaMotta four times and Kid Gavilan twice. Henry Armstrong, Sammy Angott and Bobo Olson were also among his victims. He repeatedly accepted the risk of facing accomplished opponents, including return fights against men who already knew his style.

For this writer, that combination of volume, opposition and repeated tests makes Robinson’s run a greater sustained achievement than Mayweather’s perfect career total. Losing to LaMotta did nothing to prevent Robinson from producing the strongest stretch of his career.

Julio Cesar Chavez also took an unbeaten sequence far beyond 50 fights. He won his first 87 before a controversial draw with Pernell Whitaker in September 1993. Two further victories brought him to 89-0-1 before Frankie Randall ended his 90-fight unbeaten run in January 1994.

Chavez’s run included victories over Edwin Rosario, Roger Mayweather, Meldrick Taylor and Hector Camacho. The Whitaker controversy belongs in any honest account, but so do the championship victories Chavez accumulated before Randall finally beat him.

An unbeaten streak can include draws, so these totals measure something different from 50 consecutive wins. Even with that qualification, Robinson and Chavez show how narrow the discussion becomes when a perfect retirement record receives all the attention.

Mayweather earned his place in boxing history. Robinson’s first defeat, however, opened the way to 91 fights that deserve to be judged above a marketable zero.

Sports.title: Brandon Figueroa Loses Belt and Inoue Bargaining Chip
Sports.content:
Brandon Figueroa gave up his best leverage for a massive payday against Naoya Inoue on Friday, surrendering his WBA title on the scale ahead of Saturday’s matchup with Tomoki Kameda in Las Vegas.

Figueroa weighed in at 127.4 pounds, missing the featherweight mark by 1.4 pounds. A victory over Kameda will not change his status; he exits the ring beltless, stripping away the primary bait he possessed to lure Inoue up to 126 pounds.

The entire draw for Naoya Inoue to face Figueroa was immediate division hardware. Inoue wants belts as soon as he steps foot at 126, and Figueroa holding the WBA strap was the ticket to make that happen.

Without a title to dangle, Figueroa is just an oversized, high-output nightmare matchup with no championship reward attached. Inoue’s side has zero reason to volunteer for that when they can easily target Rafael Espinoza or Angelo Leo and walk away with a recognized belt.

Chris Mannix reports that Kameda made weight and can claim the championship with a victory. If Figueroa wins, the title stays vacant.

Beyond losing the strap, the weight miss creates an immediate red flag for Inoue’s team. Figueroa is 5’9″ and has been draining himself for years to stay down in the lighter classes. If he cannot make 126 cleanly against Kameda, why would Inoue negotiate a massive featherweight bout only to risk Figueroa blowing the scale by two or three pounds and forcing a catchweight debacle? That trust is gone.

Team Inoue can bypass him entirely for an actual beltholder. While Figueroa retains respect for his aggressive style, the championship was the key card ensuring priority treatment.

As for Kameda, Figueroa should have enough in the tank to overwhelm a 35-year-old veteran on sheer work rate and physical pressure, but the hamstring issue Figueroa dealt with in camp makes Saturday trickier than it looked on paper. If that injury compromised his roadwork and directly caused this weight disaster, Kameda might walk into a much more competitive night than expected.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Targets January Return After Haney Collapse
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson is eyeing a January 23 return at Newark’s Prudential Center after his proposed matchup with Devin Haney collapsed, according to veteran boxing reporter Dan Rafael. If that date holds, Stevenson will have been out of the ring for a full year.

Zuffa Boxing has yet to name an opponent. Finding the right fit remains the primary hurdle for the outfit, which must deliver a matchup capable of moving gate tickets, driving new Paramount+ subscriptions, and justifying its financial commitment to the multi-division champion.

If Zuffa lets Shakur take a soft touch, it falls into the exact trap Top Rank and Matchroom struggled with. Putting him in with an overmatched opponent in Newark guarantees ticket sales at the Prudential Center, but it produces the kind of low-output, one-sided sparring session that alienates casual fans and drives away Paramount+ subscribers.

When Shakur faces someone who cannot force him to fight, he defaults to pure defensive control. That does zero favors for an upstart outfit trying to prove its platform is worth a recurring monthly fee.

On paper, Dana White and Zuffa built their entire brand in combat sports by forcing the best to fight the best and refusing to pay fighters to coast through showcase matchups. Contenders like Raymond Muratalla, Richardson Hitchins, or Ernesto Mercado bring real ambition.

A hometown headliner secures a baseline live crowd. The visiting fighter in the opposite corner must convince viewers at home to tune in.

Zuffa has nothing tangible to show in the ring since inking Stevenson over the summer. Stevenson spent months chasing the Haney clash while viable challenges at 140 pounds, such as Raymond Muratalla, remained unpursued in public forums.

Rafael labeled the Haney discussions an “apparent implosion,” detailing Zuffa’s alternate strategy to book the Prudential Center on January 23. The card remains unannounced officially.

Both camps traded blame over the breakdown. Haney argued he agreed to a 145-pound catchweight before Stevenson demanded a rehydration restriction. Stevenson countered by accusing Haney of trying to shift the target to 147 pounds after initially settling on a lower figure.

The promotional outfit faces the task of salvaging that lost calendar time. Entering another protracted back-and-forth only to settle on an unknown replacement would offer little return on a major promotional investment.

Muratalla represents the caliber of contender who presents a legitimate test at light welterweight. Nothing suggests he is in the mix for the January slot, yet Stevenson holds viable options in the weight class that avoid protracted catchweight bickering.

Newark guarantees friendly territory in the seats. Zuffa must secure a rival who captures attention beyond Stevenson’s core fan base, setting up an active return rather than a quiet showcase.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez May Regret Welcoming Christian Mbilli’s Pressure
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez’s eagerness to embrace Christian Mbilli’s volume resembles a fighter attempting to project calm ahead of their October 31 date. Publicly, he invites the relentless incoming salvos, yet his drastic camp overhaul tells the story of an aging champion bracing for an exhausting ordeal.

“Styles is perfect to make a great fight,” Canelo told Mike Coppinger about the matchup. “I love the idea he comes and put the pressure and I’m going to be there. No, I hope not,” said Canelo when asked if Mbilli will take one punch and run around like Edgar Berlanga and William Scull did against him. “I think he don’t have the style to do that. So, he’s going to come, throw a lot of punches and do his best.”

Canelo deserves full credit for taking this fight. He could have opted for a softer touch, but he signed up to face an opponent capable of making him work every single minute. Even if outward bravado is masking deep internal concern, he is stepping directly into the line of fire rather than running away from it.

That bravery, however, cannot manufacture the youth or stamina required once Mbilli shifts into high gear. Canelo’s lack of self-awareness will not spare him from the physical toll once that opening bell rings on October 31. Mbilli is built to break an engine that is already running on empty.

Suffering a one-sided defeat in Riyadh would strike a fatal blow to Canelo’s standing at the elite level. It would demonstrate that his gas tank can no longer support him against the premier engines in the sport. The optical disaster for Canelo in Riyadh would be immense. Getting thoroughly outworked, backed up against the ropes, and battered while tucked behind his gloves would look dreadful to the judges and the ringside brass.

Mbilli would not even need a clean one-punch knockout. The referee stepping in to rescue a defenseless, exhausted Canelo, or Eddy Reynoso waving the towel from the corner between the ninth and tenth rounds, would be the ultimate humiliation. It would signal the definitive close of the Canelo era, exposed by the very pressure fighter he claimed to want.

Sports.title: Repeat or Revenge? Dubois vs Wardley 2
Sports.content:
The first fight was a classic, and the rematch is guaranteed to be equally entertaining, as the WBO world heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs) will defend his title against Fabio Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs).

Wardley wants to avenge his loss, while Dubois plans on making a successful title defense. The action is set to take place on Saturday, October 17th at London’s O2 Arena, live on DAZN PPV.

The first fight between Wardley and Dubois took place in Manchester, England in May 2026. Wardley was coming off an upset victory over Joseph Parker while Dubois was entering the fight after a disappointing loss to Oleksandr Usyk.

Wardley scored the first knockdown ten seconds into the bout when he landed an overhand right. With 1:46 remaining in the third round, Wardley landed another overhand right that sent Dubois back down to the canvas.

After the third round, Daniel Dubois took over the fight by using his jab to set up his power shots. In the sixth round, the damage caused by the right hand of Dubois became visible, as blood was flowing out of Wardley’s nose.

In the 7th round, Dubois and Wardley closed the round out by standing in the pocket and trading heavy shots. With 53 seconds remaining in the 9th, Wardley connected with a solid right hand, and then Dubois started dictating the action.

Dubois proceeded to land a flurry of devastating punches. Seconds later, Dubois closed out the ninth round by landing a powerful right hand that knocked Wardley off balance as it looked like Wardley was out on his feet.

Wardley showed a lot of courage while suffering more damage to his nose and face in the 10th. After witnessing Dubois connect with a hard right hand early in the 11th, the referee decided to step in and put a halt to the contest.

With the victory, Daniel Dubois became a two-time heavyweight world champion. Now in the rematch, Fabio Wardley will attempt to avenge his loss and join Dubois in obtaining the status of two-time heavyweight champion.

As we saw in the first fight, both boxers possess a powerful punch, but Dubois holds advantages in skill set and overall boxing experience. Despite losing the first fight, Wardley feels confident he will be successful on October 17th.

Fabio Wardley says he and his team took the time to identify what he did wrong in the first fight, and during the course of his training camp they have made the adjustments.

On Saturday, October 17th, the Queensberry Promotions main event features the return match between two incredible warriors. The fight is guaranteed to be entertaining and crowd-pleasing. The only question is, will it be a repeat or revenge?

Sports.title: Liam Paro Calls Haney and Shakur Talks Embarrassing
Sports.content:
Liam Paro calls the Devin Haney–Shakur Stevenson negotiations “embarrassing,” and the months of public bargaining have made both fighters look bad without either taking a punch.

Each wants fans to believe the other is responsible for the fight failing to happen. Instead, their arguments over weight and rehydration conditions have given fans reasons to doubt how much risk either is willing to accept. Both have taken something resembling a defeat, except the damage is to their reputations rather than their records.

“These guys obviously don’t really want to fight each other,” Paro said. “There’s always some little problems that’s not making it happen. And in a way, it’s a bit embarrassing.”

The IBF welterweight champion understands the frustration firsthand after his own unification talks with Haney fell apart. Paro denied pricing himself out of that matchup, though he withheld specific numbers during the interview.

His critique also targeted Stevenson’s conditions for jumping up to 147 pounds. In Paro’s view, Stevenson should meet Haney at the standard welterweight limit without caveats.

“Shakur is a hell of a fighter. I’ve shared the ring with him,” Paro remarked. “He’s got all the tools to be victorious against Haney. But fight him at 147, then call yourself a true 147 champion.”

Haney claimed Stevenson tried inserting a 10-pound rehydration clause after both sides settled on a 145-pound catchweight, though Paro declined to quote an exact number.

Promoters observing this saga face an uncomfortable reality about future matchmaking. Name recognition sells tickets, yet getting marquee talent to sign contracts remains a major hurdle.

Winning social media debates does nothing positive for Haney or Stevenson. Prolonging this dispute simply makes it tougher for either champion to claim he wants the challenge.

The biggest problem for both Haney and Stevenson is that neither owns the kind of explosive, crowd-pleasing style that forgives this level of nonsense. When knockout artists or charismatic brawlers play hardball, fans usually grumble, pay the pay-per-view fee anyway, and tune in for the inevitable explosion. But Haney and Shakur are safety-first purists.

The public was already skeptical about whether their matchup would turn into a low-volume chess match of feints and clinches. Piling endless, petty negotiations on top of a fight style that already tests casual fan patience is box office suicide.

Instead of looking like hungry young champions chasing greatness, they managed to make Liam Paro look like the mature adult in the room. Paro called it what it is: embarrassing. If a fighter genuinely believes he is the pound-for-pound king, he steps in the ring and proves it, rather than whining on an app about rehydration terms after already getting a catchweight concession.

Even if they sign the contracts tomorrow, the energy is completely gone. The narrative will no longer be about which fighter establishes his legacy. The narrative will be that two over-entitled divas finally ran out of excuses because the public stopped caring about their tweets.

Ghana News.title: I sacrificed my dream of becoming a maxillofacial surgeon for politics – Ekua Amoakoh
Ghana News.content:
Spokesperson for NPP Flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee, Dr Ekua Amoakoh, says her involvement in politics cost her the opportunity to pursue a long-held ambition of becoming a maxillofacial surgeon.

The medical doctor said she had hoped to specialise in head and neck surgery but had to give up some career opportunities when her political work began earlier than she had anticipated.

Speaking in a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, Dr Amoakoh said she did not consider the missed opportunity a personal loss, describing it instead as a sacrifice.

“No, maybe some job opportunities, yes. So some job opportunities I could not take. I had to make a decision. But for me, I don't really see it as a loss. I think they are sacrifices,” she said.

Dr Amoakoh said her interest in maxillofacial surgery began during her first year in medical school and continued during her clinical work at Ridge Hospital.

She described the specialty as a niche field and said she had spent a year at the hospital working towards that path.

“That's what I was doing at Ridge for the whole year. It's very niche. So that's what I was doing, and I think I was very interested in it, and I knew even from my first year in medical school that's exactly what I wanted to do,” she said.

She recalled enjoying her work as a house officer and believing she had the ability to build a career in the field.

“I enjoyed that. So I feel like if I've lost anything, it's probably my ability to become a specialist in that field,” she said.

One of her ambitions was to treat children born with cleft palates, a condition that can require specialised surgical care.

“I always thought I would end up being one of those nice cleft doctors, you know, fixing kids' clefts. I always thought I would be a good doctor,” she said.

Dr Amoakoh said she had expected to complete more of her medical career before becoming deeply involved in politics.

“If anything, maybe that has been the highest price I've had to pay, because I always thought I would be able to get to the end of that before I started. But politics kicked off for me earlier than I expected,” she said.

Her comments suggest that the timing of her political involvement, rather than a loss of interest in medicine, was central to the career decision.

Asked whether she now loved politics more than medicine, Dr Amoakoh answered in the affirmative, saying political work came naturally to her.

“Yes, yes, yes. It comes to me naturally, and I don't find it really difficult. You know, they say that you find something that you're good at or something that you love, and you don't feel like you're working,” she said.

She acknowledged that her schedule had become more demanding but said she remained engaged by the work she was doing.

“My schedule has gotten way crazier. But it's not too much for me because I'm doing things I find interesting. The reading that I'm doing is reading that I would have done anyway,” she said.

She made the remarks during her personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti.

Ghana News.title: ‘It was very difficult to be NPP in 2024’ – Ekua Amoakoh
Ghana News.content:
Spokesperson for NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee has recounted how her research into the party’s health sector record ahead of the 2024 elections sparked clashes with her own colleagues.

The medical doctor said her assignment involved gathering and analysing data from the Ministry of Health, the Ghana Health Service and the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) to document the party’s record in the sector.

Speaking in a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, Dr Amoakoh said she was tasked with using her research skills to develop a comprehensive account of the NPP’s performance in health, tracing its record across successive administrations.

“So my first job was to go to the Ministry of Health and collect all their data. Because I came with a skill set, I was given the health sector to do all the research,” she said.

She explained that the exercise covered several areas, including health infrastructure and national health insurance, with the findings intended to support the party’s campaign messaging.

Dr Amoakoh said the work became difficult amid intense political disagreements during the election year, with some of her fellow party members challenging her findings.

“It was very difficult to be an NPP person. My own colleagues were fighting me. And I was like, ‘You people, I don't understand. I sound like I was in government. I'm here with you people. I've just gone there, and you are coming to fight me,’” she recounted.

She said the disagreements became so frequent that she eventually left a group chat in 2024 after exchanges with colleagues grew increasingly heated.

According to her, the tensions arose partly because the information she gathered from official records sometimes contradicted claims being made in political discussions.

Dr Amoakoh attributed the disagreements to the intense propaganda and political contest surrounding the 2024 general election.

She said some colleagues reacted angrily when she presented documents that challenged particular claims, making it difficult to have discussions based on the available evidence.

“That was in the height of propaganda. It was in the height of the election. There was so much propaganda. And you are looking at documents that disprove something someone is saying, right? But they are so angry that they are arguing with you with their heart and soul and mind,” she said.

She acknowledged that she also contributed to the disagreements by refusing to back down from arguments.

“So we can be fighting, and one time I realized that, nah, this is getting too far,” she said.

Dr Amoakoh said her research went beyond the NPP’s time in government, taking in records from the Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC) era, the administration of former President John Agyekum Kufuor and that of the late President John Evans Atta Mills.

The exercise was intended to help the party assess developments in the health sector over time and build a narrative around its own record.

Dr Amoakoh made the remarks during her personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti.

Ghana News.title: Ablakwa challenges Minority to identify an evacuee denied GH¢5,500 allowance
Ghana News.content:
Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has challenged the Minority in Parliament to identify a Ghanaian evacuated from South Africa who did not receive the GH¢5,500 allowance, dismissing allegations of unaccounted funds as attempts to create a scandal.

The government evacuated Ghanaians from South Africa following heightened anti-immigrant sentiment and attacks targeting foreign nationals in the country.

The operation ended on September 4, 2026, after three days, according to Mr Ablakwa. He said his September 7 briefing was intended to provide an account of the exercise to the public.

Mr Ablakwa said the evacuation exercise ended on September 4, 2026, and that he briefed the press three days later to account for the operation.

He questioned claims that some people on the evacuation list could not be traced and that the funds allocated for the exercise had not been fully accounted for.

“All of that propaganda out there that some people on the list cannot be found and that some voodoo analysis they have done showed that there's some money that has not been accounted for,” he said.

The Minister said he had been looking for an evacuee who could publicly state that they did not receive the allowance.

“I have been looking for one Ghanaian to step forward and say that when we were evacuated from South Africa, the 5,500 Cedi reintegration allowance I didn't get it as a Ghanaian. Or the 500 Cedi transportation allowance, I didn't get it. Have you heard of any one Ghanaian? One,” he said.

He questioned why the evacuation had become controversial, insisting there was no scandal to uncover.

“So what is this desperate attempt to create a scandal when there is none? When the whole world is commending that all of that propaganda...” he said.

His remarks came in response to concerns over the handling of the evacuation, including questions about individuals listed as beneficiaries and the disbursement of funds.

The dispute centres on the government's management of the evacuation and the use of public funds to support returning Ghanaians.

While Mr Ablakwa maintains that the allowances were paid, the Minority's concerns include the whereabouts of some individuals on the evacuation list and whether all expenditure has been properly accounted for.

Ghana News.title: Debate, leadership and governance drew me to politics – Ekua Amoakoh
Ghana News.content:
Spokesperson for NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee, Dr Ekua Amoakoh, says her lifelong interest in debate, governance and leadership inspired her to pursue a career in politics.

In a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, she said she had always been vocal about how institutions and society should be run and wanted to contribute to decisions affecting Ghana’s development.

“I always enjoyed debates and, you know, governance. And I always had opinions on stuff. So I think that's why I wanted to be a politician. I always had opinions on what to do, how everything should be run,” she said.

Dr Amoakoh said she frequently found herself in leadership positions during her education, from junior secondary school through senior secondary school.

“At every point in my life, whether in JSS or secondary school, I always end up in some position of leadership because I'm very verbose,” she said.

She recalled an incident from medical school involving a lecturer known among students as “Captain”, whom she described as intimidating.

Dr Amoakoh said students were sometimes too frightened to approach him with difficult issues, prompting them to ask her to speak on their behalf.

“We all needed to tell Captain something that he really wouldn't understand. But everybody was just too frightened to tell him. They'd say, ‘Akua, go and do it,’” she recounted.

She said the experience reflected a pattern in her life in which she often became the person expected to speak up when others were reluctant to do so.

“So I always knew that I always had that ability to be able to speak when I needed to. And I had opinions on everything,” she said.

Dr Amoakoh said her political ambition was also driven by a desire to contribute directly to Ghana’s development.

She explained that she did not want to remain outside the decision-making process when she believed she could help shape the country's direction.

“I didn't want to be in a position where I couldn't influence the growth of this country, for instance,” she said.

Ghana News.title: ‘My Grandmother is an NPP Founding member’ – Ekua Amoakoh reveals family’s NPP roots
Ghana News.content:
Spokesperson for NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee, Dr Ekua Amoakoh, has revealed that her grandmother was a founding member of the party and served as one of its early treasurers in the Ashanti Region.

Speaking in a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, Dr Amoakoh said she spent considerable time with her grandmother while growing up and learnt a great deal from her.

She described her grandmother as a politician who played a role in the NPP’s early organisation.

“My grandma is a founding member of the NPP. She was one of the first people to be treasurer in Ashanti Region. She is a council of elders—like she is,” she said.

Dr Amoakoh said she spent much of her childhood with her grandmother, particularly when her mother enrolled at the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA) to pursue further qualifications.

She recounted the period humorously, suggesting that her mother’s studies gave her more time with her grandmother.

“I spent a lot of time with my grandmother. And I think I learned a lot of things from her,” she said.

Her account offers a glimpse into the family relationships that influenced her upbringing and her later involvement in politics.

Dr Amoakoh’s account places her grandmother’s political involvement among the family experiences that preceded her own work with the NPP.

The party was established in 1992 and draws from Ghana’s Danquah-Busia-Dombo political tradition.

Her grandmother’s reported role as an early treasurer in the Ashanti Region points to a family association with the party dating back to its formative years.

Dr Amoakoh also spoke about growing up at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital in Kumasi, where her grandmother worked as Director of Nursing.

She said her parents encouraged her to study medicine, although she initially resisted the decision and questioned her choice even after entering medical school.

She has since come to appreciate the experience and the discipline it instilled in her.

“I'm glad they insisted because even if it's not something you are going to practice or something you are going to use, that whole process of training, I think it can forge any person into a formidable person,” she said.

Dr Amoakoh’s interview on PM Express explored her childhood, family background and the experiences that helped shape her career in medicine and politics.

Ghana News.title: Dr. Ekua Amoakoh recounts childhood at Komfo Anokye and how parents pushed her into the medical profession
Ghana News.content:
Spokesperson for NPP Flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee, Dr Ekua Amoakoh, has recounted how her parents’ insistence led her to study medicine, despite her initial interest in other pursuits.

In a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, she spoke about growing up at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital in Kumasi, resisting her parents’ career choice and eventually appreciating the value of her medical training.

Dr Amoakoh said her childhood was closely tied to Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, where her grandmother served as Director of Nursing.

She said her family lived in the hospital’s doctors’ flats when she was a baby, making the medical environment a familiar part of her upbringing.

“I grew up in a hospital. I grew up in Komfo Anokye. My grandmother was the director of nursing of Komfo Anokye when I was born. So we lived at the flats at the doctors' flats when I was a baby,” she recounted.

She said the environment influenced her parents’ decision about her future career.

“That's all I knew. So when I got to the time to decide what to do, quite frankly, I think that decision was made for me by my parents,” she said.

Despite growing up around medical professionals, Dr Amoakoh said she was initially reluctant to follow the same path.

She recalled resisting her parents’ decision even after entering medical school.

“Initially I kicked against it, or I fought them. Even in medical school, up until about third year, I said, ‘I don't want to do this. I told you I didn't want to do this,’” she said.

She also recalled sensing that her career had already been decided before she completed secondary school at Holy Child School.

She said her parents viewed medicine as a natural choice because of her upbringing and exposure to the profession.

Dr Amoakoh offered a glimpse into how her university application was handled, saying her mother completed the application form and presented it to her for her signature.

She recalled that she was still in Form Three when her mother arrived with the completed paperwork.

“My mom just turns up one day, and then she just brings me the paper to sign. She filled it all out and just brought it to me. All I had to do was sign,” she said.

She said she was unhappy at the time because she felt she had little say in the decision about her future.

Dr Amoakoh said her interests at the time differed from her parents’ expectations, explaining that she was attracted to wealth creation and the opportunities associated with business.

“I always liked the nicer things in life. That's why I'm a typical capitalist. You will not find me doing anything socialist,” she said.

She argued that allowing people to pursue their creativity and create value was important for economic growth.

“I don't actually see anything wrong with trying really hard to make some money. So I was always more attracted to that. And I was like, I grew up in the hospital. I've seen all these doctors. No, I want more money,” she recounted.

She said those interests contributed to disagreements with her parents over her choice of profession.

Although she initially opposed the decision, Dr Amoakoh said she has come to appreciate the experience of studying medicine.

She said the demands of medical training can help develop discipline, resilience and the ability to handle challenges, even for those who eventually pursue other careers.

“I'm glad they insisted because even if it's not something you are going to practice or something you are going to use, that whole process of training, I think it can forge any person into a formidable person,” she said.

Dr Amoakoh also spoke about her family, revealing that she is the fourth of six children.

She said the family had five girls for a long time, with her younger sister Ama close to her in age.

“It was an army of girls, and I was number four, and my little sister Ama was five. We were very close in age. So we are almost twins—Irish twins, as she likes to call us. So we grew up very close together,” she said.

She added that the family later welcomed a sixth child, a boy.

Ghana News.title: NPP will be better prepared for 2028 election security – Ekua Amoakoh
Ghana News.content:
Spokesperson for NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Health Committee, Dr Ekua Amoakoh, says the party’s recent national executive elections show that delegates want stronger security arrangements ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Speaking in a personality profile interview on JoyNews’ PM Express with Emefa Adeti, Dr Amoakoh reflected on the security challenges the party faced during the 2024 elections, describing the situation as chaotic and saying party officials were often unable to protect their polling agents.

She said she was in the NPP’s war room during the elections and witnessed reports of violence at various polling stations and collation centres.

“All we were seeing was various pockets of violence being directed at our polling agents. There was even an instance in the Upper East Region where some of our polling agents were held at gunpoint to confirm certain results,” she said.

“These are all things we saw that day, and there was nothing we could do about it.”

Dr Amoakoh said the two major political parties had agreed to leave election security arrangements to the Ghana Police Service rather than rely on party-based security or vigilantism.

However, she argued that the police presence at some locations was insufficient to contain disturbances.

She cited an example of a collation centre where about 100 people were present, but only around 10 police officers were available, adding that the officers were unarmed.

She said the party’s grassroots members and polling agents bore the consequences of the situation, while disputes over some parliamentary results led to re-collation exercises.

Dr Amoakoh said the outcome of the NPP’s recent national executive elections suggested that delegates had taken lessons from the 2024 experience and wanted the party to prepare differently.

“I think the election results from this past Saturday just show that the party took notice of what happened in 2024. And they want to do something about it,” she said.

She added that the results reinforced her view that delegates understood what the party needed at different stages of its development.

“It's clear that we will not be as unprepared security-wise as we were in 2024,” she said.

Her comments come as the NPP reorganises its structures following its defeat in the 2024 general elections and prepares for the next polls in 2028.

Dr Amoakoh also criticised what she described as the governing National Democratic Congress’ (NDC) interest in the NPP’s internal affairs.

She argued that the NDC should focus on governance rather than the opposition party’s internal processes.

“I think especially since they have the responsibility of governance, I would expect that they focus on more interesting, more important things. This is like a family matter for the NPP,” she said.

Asked why she believed the NDC was paying attention to the NPP’s internal affairs, she suggested that the opposition party’s preparations had unsettled the governing party.

“It's because it has driven some fear into their hearts that, no, this time we will not be pushed around,” she said.

Her remarks reflect her own interpretation of the NDC’s response to the NPP’s internal elections.

The NPP held its National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi on October 3, 2026, as part of its reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Dr Amoakoh’s comments place election security among the issues she believes the party must address following the challenges reported during the 2024 polls.

The party’s preparations will take place against the backdrop of concerns about violence at polling stations and collation centres, as well as disputes over election results.

Ghana News.title: Newsfile to discuss GH¢49.72m evacuation cost, EC appointments and Obuasi SHTS abuse case
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews’ flagship current affairs programme, Newsfile, will on Saturday, October 17, examine four major national issues that have dominated public debate over the past week.

Hosted by Samson Lardy Anyenini, the programme will discuss the GH¢49.72 million spent evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa, controversy over appointments to the Electoral Commission (EC), allegations of sexual abuse at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), and the dismissal of a GH¢15 million defamation suit filed by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin.

The programme airs from 8:00am to 12:00 noon on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms.

GH¢49.72m evacuation bill under scrutiny

The programme will examine questions surrounding the GH¢49.72 million spent on evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa following xenophobic attacks.

Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has said GH¢38.84 million was used for chartered flights, air tickets, ground transportation, feeding, accommodation and medical care, while GH¢10.80 million went towards reintegration support and transportation allowances.

The government contributed GH¢33.72 million, while businessman Ibrahim Mahama’s company, Engineers and Planners, donated GH¢16 million.

The Minority in Parliament has demanded a detailed breakdown of the expenditure, including the cost per evacuee.

The Ministry has reportedly submitted a 200-page report in response to a Right to Information request. Mr Ablakwa has also requested an independent audit of evacuation exercises undertaken by successive governments since 2017.

The discussion will consider the expenditure, the documentation supporting it and the accountability questions raised by the Minority.

EC appointments raise questions about neutrality

The programme will also consider the controversy surrounding President John Dramani Mahama’s appointment of Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah and Emelia Afi Agbenyo as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission.

Madam Agbenyo’s previous role as an NDC manifesto spokesperson has prompted concerns about the political neutrality of the electoral management body.

The New Patriotic Party has called for her appointment to be withdrawn, citing her perceived political affiliation.

Minister of State in charge of Government Communications Felix Kwakye Ofosu has defended the appointments, arguing that institutional changes can also address perceived imbalances in state institutions. He has also pointed to appointments made under the previous administration.

The NDC maintains that Madam Agbenyo has the qualifications and integrity required for the role.

The discussion will examine the concerns surrounding political affiliations and the standards expected of officials entrusted with overseeing elections.

Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations

Allegations of sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, and female students will form another part of the programme.

Investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni has reported that the number of students alleging abuse has risen to 16.

The Ghana Education Service has suspended the headmaster pending investigations. Reports have also linked him to the National Democratic Congress in Juaben, where he is said to have served as constituency secretary and sought to contest the chairmanship.

Some parents have reportedly alleged that they were being pressured to withdraw their complaints.

Parliament’s Committee on Human Rights has condemned the alleged abuse and called for speedy action.

The programme will examine the allegations, the ongoing investigations and questions about whether warning signs were missed or concerns were not acted upon.

The allegations remain subject to investigation and must be established through due process.

Afenyo-Markin’s GH¢15m suit dismissed

The final issue will be the Accra High Court’s dismissal of the GH¢15 million defamation suit filed by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin against Ghana Gold Board Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi.

The court struck out the case on October 14, ruling that the writ of summons was “incurably defective and incompetent”.

The ruling centred on compliance with Order 57 Rule 2 of the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2004 (C.I. 47), which sets out requirements for actions involving defamation.

The court’s decision was procedural and did not determine whether Mr Gyamfi’s remarks were defamatory.

The suit followed comments Mr Gyamfi made on JoyNews’ Newsfile in August 2026, when he described Mr Afenyo-Markin as an “extortionist”.

The programme will examine the implications of the ruling and whether the Minority Leader’s legal team will seek to correct the defects and pursue the case again.

Newsfile airs on Saturday, October 17, from 8:00am to 12:00 noon on Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews and other platforms.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: US coastguard rescues 16 after boat sinks off Mexico’s Baja coast
World.content:
At least 11 people believed to still be missing, with rescue operations underway.

Share US coastguard rescues 16 after boat sinks off Mexico’s Baja coast on social media

The US coastguard has said it rescued 16 people from the Pacific Ocean after a boat sank off Mexico’s Baja coast.

The coastguard said on Friday it responded to a Mayday call reporting that a boat was sinking. The search is ongoing for 11 people believed to be still missing.

The boat went down about 225km (140 miles) west of Ensenada, Mexico.

A rescue helicopter reached the site about two hours after someone on the boat transmitted the Mayday call at about 1am (08:00 GMT) on Friday, said coastguard Lieutenant Santiago Tamburini.

It took about 90 minutes for the coastguard crew, which included a rescue swimmer, to pull the 16 people from the water, Tamburini said.

The people rescued were Mexican nationals, according to the Mexican consulate.

One survivor was being treated for a suspected shark bite and two were in critical condition, authorities said.

The rescued were flown by helicopter to San Diego, California, and transported to hospitals. The Mexican consulate in San Diego said it offered consular assistance.

The coastguard and US Navy are continuing to search the area with two helicopters, a fixed-wing plane, a cutter and a navy combat ship.

The boat sank in an area frequented by smugglers transporting migrants to the US. It is also popular with fishing and leisure boats.

Details about the boat’s origin, destination and what it was doing are not clear. No vessel, only debris, was found, and it was unclear what type of boat was involved, the coastguard said.

“Boats in that area can be for fishing, leisure, personal recreation. We just don’t know what they were doing out there. We all know it’s a suspected smuggling route,” Tamburini said.

World.title: Oregon school shooter was former special needs student, police say
World.content:
A teacher fought the teenage shooter and a parent shot him dead, police say on Friday, a day after four people were killed.

Share Oregon school shooter was former special needs student, police say on social media

The 16-year-old who killed three children and a teacher at an elementary school in the US state of Oregon was a former special-needs student at the school, police and school officials have said.

Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz identified the attacker on Friday, a day after the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School, as Griffin J. John II.

He said the teenager attacked a classroom of special-needs students, where all the victims were shot.

Steven Cook, superintendent of Bend-La Pine Schools, said John was not enrolled in the local public school system at the time.

“That classroom was a special needs classroom, and the suspect was a special needs student in that school,” Cook told a news conference.

Krantz said John shot his way through locked doors with a 12-gauge shotgun, firing as many as 15 shots, and had about 44 rounds left when he was killed. Police are still trying to determine how he obtained the gun.

Under Oregon law, a minor may possess a shotgun if provided by a parent or with a parent’s consent.

The shooter’s mother, Shauntai Nickerson, separately told reporters outside her apartment: “I’m so sorry, I wish I could have done something.”

A teacher threw her phone at the gunman, then tackled and fought him, likely saving lives, Krantz said, calling her actions “heroic”. She was not injured.

A 36-year-old father, Kaylub Giamanco, who has two children at the school, then followed the gunman inside and shot him dead minutes after the first 911 call.

US President Donald Trump called Giamanco a “great hero”. “It’s a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it,” Trump said.

The children killed were aged five, eight and 11, and the teacher was Meghan Lambert, 25, police said.



A seven-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to hospital in critical condition.

The shooting is the 28th mass killing in the US this year, according to a database by The Associated Press, USA Today and Northeastern University.

The Gun Violence Archive in the US has documented 369 mass shootings in 2026, defined as incidents in which four or more people are shot.

The Everytown for Gun Safety group has counted at least 100 incidents of gunfire on school grounds this year, with 34 deaths.

World.title: Albanian PM blames ‘foreign hands’ for unrest as student protests intensify
World.content:
Riot police clash with protesters for fourth day, as young Albanians protest corruption and poor university conditions

Share Albanian PM blames ‘foreign hands’ for unrest as student protests intensify on social media

Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama has blamed “foreign hands” for the increasingly violent student-led protests that are calling on him to resign.

Riot police clashed with protesters outside the education ministry for the fourth day in a row, as thousands of young Albanians marched through the capital, Tirana, on Friday to protest government corruption and poor university conditions.

“This is not a student phenomenon,” Rama said in a video address on Friday. He said there were “foreign hands that do not wish for Albania to be at peace”.

Rama insisted that the protest had “absolutely nothing to do with the hardships, problems or legitimate aspirations of anyone who desires a better life”.

Police officers used water cannon and tear gas as demonstrators hurled rocks.

The protests have spread beyond the capital to Elbasan, Shkodra and Korca, where demonstrators broke windows and set fire to rubbish bins, local media reported.

The ongoing escalation follows months of mostly peaceful demonstrations, originally sparked by the sale of part of Albania’s coastline to a luxury resort development linked to Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law.

Days of unrest have increasingly targeted banks and government buildings. Protesters hurled bricks and concrete blocks at the education ministry on Tuesday. They also set fire to several buildings across the city, including the prime minister’s office, the finance and justice ministry buildings and branches of several banks.

According to a police statement, 160 people were detained over alleged acts of violence on Thursday evening.



The EU question

Demonstrators are demanding Rama’s resignation, as well as electoral and education reforms.

The prime minister, whose government denies corruption, said he would be ready to discuss rising education costs but rejected the calls to resign.

He said on Thursday, “My responsibility is to listen, address legitimate concerns and keep Albania moving forward.”

His dismissal “would be a betrayal of the Albanians who gave me a strong mandate to complete negotiations on European Union membership”, he added.

Corruption scandals have complicated Albania’s efforts to join the EU. Analysts say the country is a hub for gangs seeking to launder money from drugs and weapons trafficking.

Rama won a fourth term last year on promises to take Albania into the EU, aiming for membership as early as 2028.

World.title: Leeds vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
World.content:
Manchester United are mired in poor form – and Lisandro Martinez’s meltdown – now they face on-the-up rivals Leeds.

Share Old rivalry has new twist as Man United head to Leeds – all to know on social media

Who: Leeds United vs Manchester United

What: English Premier League

Where: Elland Road, Leeds, United Kingdom

When: Sunday, October 18, at 2pm local time (13:00 GMT)

How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up from 9:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Manchester United against Leeds United has long been one of the fiercest rivalries in football.

The former’s closest shot to ending their wait since 1967 for an English top flight title came in 1993 when Sir Alex Ferguson’s side were pipped to the title by the latter.

The following year United’s wait was over as Ferguson’s side – buoyed by the arrival of Eric Cantona from Leeds – lifted the inaugural Premier League crown.

The rest for United and Ferguson was history, but since the most successful manager in English football retired the Old Trafford club have been in decline.

The fortunes of Leeds, who have won three league titles, dipped dramatically after that last piece of domestic silverware. Ten years later, they were relegated and three years were even spent in League One, the third tier of English football.

Now the Elland Road club are back in the top flight, having won the Championship two seasons ago, and have an eye on the top four this weekend.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at the match that for Leeds marks the arrival of their fiercest rivals, who have lurched to a 40-year low.

How have Leeds United fared this season?

Leeds have lost only one of their six league games this season, a 2-1 reverse at Arsenal in their last match when the Premier League holders were second best for much of the match and were forced to come from behind.



Two wins and two draws in their first five league matches saw Leeds holding onto the coat-tails of Arsenal and City.

That run culminated with a stunning 4-1 home win against Newcastle United.

A disappointing home draw with Crystal Palace sat in between the defeat at Arsenal.

A 6-3 defeat at Chelsea ended their League Cup hopes, but the home side needed two goals in the last ten minutes to pull clear in the thrilling encounter.

How have Manchester United fared this season?

United’s season – and Michael Carrick’s start as permanent manager – couldn’t have got off to a worse start with a 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull City.

When the Red Devils fell a goal behind against another promoted side, Ipswich Town, at Old Trafford in their next match, the warning signs were there.

Carrick’s side came back to win 5-2 – and that remains United’s only league win of the season.

A contentious 1-0 home defeat by Manchester City – in which a controversial VAR decision separated the sides – has been one of United’s better performances with deflating draws against Everton, Fulham and Tottenham surrounding the derby.

United were also dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton, who overcame the home side’s early 2-0 first-half lead to the disbelief of Old Trafford.

What is the latest on Lisandro Martinez’s Manchester United criticism?

Defender Lisandro ‌‌Martinez will be available for Sunday’s game after ⁠⁠United accepted ⁠⁠his apology for criticising its transfer policy, Carrick told reporters on Friday.

Martinez met Carrick and senior club officials on Thursday, two days after suggesting United ⁠⁠needed greater investment to compete at the highest level following their 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid.

The centre back later apologised for his remarks and Carrick ⁠⁠sought to downplay the episode when he spoke to reporters on Friday.

“We’ve moved on from that. It was one of those things. It’s really not a drama for the group,” Carrick said.

“The squad have trained really well and they are in good spirits. There is ‌‌a freshness about the group…

“He’s part of the squad [for Sunday].”

What happened the last time Leeds played Manchester United?

Leeds were 2-1 winners at Old Trafford when the sides met in the Premier League in April.

Noah Okafor scored both goals for Leeds to inflict the only defeat of Carrick’s interim tenure, having replaced Ruben Amorim as manager.

Martinez was sent off early in the second half, but Casemiro offered United some hope just after the hour mark.

What happened in the corresponding Leeds-Man Utd game last season?

The teams shared a 1-1 draw in the Premier League match at Elland Road last season. Leeds’ Brenden Aaronson opened the scoring in the 62nd minute with Matheus Cunha levelling three minutes later.



When did Manchester United last beat Leeds?

United were 2-0 winners when the sides met at Elland Road in Leeds’ relegation season in 2022-23.

Marcus Rashford and Alejandro Garnacho netted the goals.

When did Leeds last beat Manchester United at home?

Leeds haven’t beaten United at home since Harry Kewell scored the only goal of the game in a Premier League match in 2002.

There have been seven matches between the sides at Leeds since then, with United winning five of those.

Prediction – Leeds vs Manchester United

The Opta supercomputer has given Leeds a 42 percent chance of victory, while offering United a 32 percent chance of winning.

Head-to-head – Leeds vs Manchester United

This will be the 116th meeting between the sides, with United winning 50 and Leeds claiming the spoils on 27 occasions. Another 38 matches were draws.

Leeds United team news

Joe Rodon and Mateo Joseph will both miss the game due to injury, while former United winger Daniel James is a doubt with a back problem.

Predicted Leeds United starting lineup

Trafford, Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin

Manchester United team news

Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko all remain sidelined by injury, while Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo face late fitness tests. Matthijs de Ligt is nearing a return to action following his long-term back injury.

Predicted Manchester United starting lineup

Lammens; Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Baleba, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Diallo; Cunha

World.title: Italy probes Israel’s Katz over abuse, sexual assault of flotilla activists
World.content:
Rome prosecutors also name 12 senior military, police and prison officials over alleged abuse of detained activists.

Italian prosecutors have placed Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz and 12 senior military, police and prison officials under investigation over the treatment of activists detained on Gaza-bound solidarity boats, widening a probe that had centred on far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.

The Rome prosecutors’ office said on Friday that the case concerns suspected torture, kidnapping, personal injury, robbery and damage when Israeli forces intercepted small fleets of activist boats heading towards Gaza in 2025 and 2026.

It opened the investigation after complaints from 50 Italian citizens who were detained following two Global Sumud Flotilla missions last year and this year.
