Those named as suspects include Israeli military chief Eyal Zamir.

Prosecutors said activists detained after the first mission in 2025 reported beatings, injuries, death threats, insults and accusations of terrorism. Those on the second mission in 2026 reported harsher treatment, including beatings in the dark and the use of tasers and rubber bullets, the statement said.

The activists reported at least 15 cases of sexual assault, including rape.

Luca Poggi, an Italian economist who was detained, told Reuters news agency in May: “We were stripped, thrown to the ground, kicked.”

Ben-Gvir dismissed news of the investigation in June, saying he would “continue to stand proudly alongside” Israeli soldiers.

Flotilla organisers say they aim to break Israel’s blockade of Gaza by delivering humanitarian aid.



What prompted the case

The first Global Sumud Flotilla set sail from Barcelona in September 2025 with 42 boats and 462 activists. Israeli forces intercepted it in international waters in early October that year, with hundreds detained and later deported.

The second mission left Barcelona in April 2026. Israeli forces began intercepting its vessels near the southern Greek island of Crete on April 30, and by May 19 had detained about 430 people on some 50 ships in international waters, with the final interceptions taking place off Cyprus.

Ben-Gvir later posted a video showing him taunting activists who were cable-tied and kneeling at a makeshift prison at the port of Ashdod while Israel’s national anthem played.

Prosecutors said they sent Israel a request for judicial assistance in June, seeking information to reconstruct events and establish individual responsibility, but did not say whether Israel had responded.

They also held talks at Eurojust, the EU’s judicial cooperation agency, as other similar investigations are under way in other European countries.

Under Italian law, crimes committed abroad against Italian citizens can be prosecuted in Rome.

If the investigation finds the charges warranted, prosecutors could formally request a trial.

World.title: Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role
World.content:
A Russian drone zips across the computer screen, startling the commanders keeping watch over the battlefield via a live stream in their bunker.

Cigarette in one hand, radio in the other, one of them calls in their own drone to bring it down and warns the soldiers below of the threat. The men are dangerously exposed, on the long walk across open ground from their front line positions. They are being replaced after three months forcing the Russians back.

This is part of Operation Vivaldi, a Ukrainian counter-offensive which they say has liberated 277 sq km (106 square miles) in the eastern Donbas region in recent months.

The name reflects the offensive's four stages, or seasons - like the Italian composer's violin concerto. The successful assault blunted an attempted Russian pincer movement that threatened to encircle the key Fortress Belt cities still under Ukrainian control.

While Russia this month pummels Ukraine from the air, crippling its energy infrastructure and killing scores of civilians across the country, at the front, it is Ukraine that has made recent gains. Kyiv says it has inflicted heavy losses - 8,000 Russian casualties in Vivaldi alone, and close to 50,000 along the front in the month of September â and suffered few casualties in return.

World.title: Oregon teacher fought school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'
World.content:
Some readers may find this article distressing.

An Oregon teacher threw her mobile phone before she tackled and tried to wrestle away a shotgun from the arms of a teen suspect who opened fire on a special educational needs class.

As she tussled with him on the floor of the class - where three children and a teacher were killed - a bystander armed with a pistol ran inside and killed the teen.

The bystander, a father of two girls at the school, had been driving past Silver Rail Elementary in Bend on Thursday lunchtime when he saw the suspect firing in the car park, then shooting through a window to enter.

Police said the 16-year-old suspect used to be a student at the school.

Police say the suspect was armed with about 44 more rounds of shotgun ammunition when he was stopped. He fired as many as 15 rounds in the class.

"To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence, and intervened to prevent this tragedy from being any worse, we owe you a debt of gratitude," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said on Friday.

Police offered more information on the attack at a news conference on Friday, where they identified two of the four victims. They include five-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert.

The families of the two other students who were killed, an eight-year-old and 11-year-old, did not wish to have them publicly identified yet, police said.

Two others were injured in the attack. Another teacher, a 54-year-old, was still being treated at hospital, and a seven-year-old student, who was in serious but stable condition.

World.title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
World.content:
Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off where the rainforest's future is a key issue.

Left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro.

On 25 October, Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race. Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon.

Satellite data shows that in the year up to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988. The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%.

The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil.

Why the Amazon rainforest is so important | What in the World podcast

Jair Bolsonaro promoted mining in indigenous lands in the Amazon and forest clearances soared at the same time as resources to protect the forest were cut.

During Bolsonaro's presidency from 2019 to 2022, the Amazon lost nearly 60% more in forest lands compared to the previous four years, AFP news agency reported, citing official data.

Lula reversed Jair Bolsonaro's policies and saw deforestation rates drop to a six-year low during his first year in office. Lula tightened up environmental monitoring and penalties for illegal logging.

"Our goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030," he said in a post on X on Friday.

Tropical rainforests like the Amazon are home to millions of species. In a healthy state they absorb vast quantities of planet-warming carbon dioxide, helping to keep the Earth cool.

But they have come under increasing pressure from decades of deliberate land clearance for agriculture and logging, as well as climate change, which scientists warn can create conditions for wildfires.

Brazil's Environment Minister, Joao Paulo Capobianco, described the decline in Amazon deforestation as "absolutely stratospheric".

It is a "historic achievement" for Brazil, said Marcio Astrini, executive secretary at climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima.

It shows that "with political will, it is possible to curb deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions", Astrini said.

World.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as new US law takes effect
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has used his presidential authority to block numerous sanctions on Russia that were recently passed by the US Congress in an effort to punish the country for its war on Ukraine.

In an executive order on Friday night, Trump said that it is in the US "national interests" to withhold some of the sanctions. Trump signed the sanctions bill into law in September, and it was due to take effect on Sunday.

It comes days after Trump said the US would import Russian diesel in an effort to bring down US energy prices before the midterm elections in November, which will decide which party controls Congress.

The plan shocked lawmakers, and has triggered a bipartisan backlash.

The US sanctions law is named for the late Republican South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham, who was one of Ukraine's staunchest defenders in Washington before his death on 11 July.

The law took aim at Russian's economy, and gave Trump broad powers to levy tariffs of up to 100% on the top five purchasers of Russian oil and gas â most significantly China and India.

Additionally, the law includes sanctions against Russian President Vladimir Putin, senior figures within the Russian government as well as banks and other financial institutions and Russia's "shadow fleet" of tankers used to circumvent existing sanctions.

On Thursday, a bipartisan group of 20 US lawmakers issued a letter calling on Trump to respect the new law, which is due to take effect on 18 October.

The lawmakers thanked Trump for signing the sanctions bill, and urged his "full and faithful implementation" of the law.

The lawmakers said it would be "decisive in forcing Putin to take peace talks seriously" and called on the Trump administration "to apply the Graham law's sanctions to their fullest extent and without delay".

Last week, Trump announced that he had held a phone call with Putin, and had agreed to purchase diesel from Moscow.

US allies criticised the move, anxious that it could help Russia in its war effort.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the deal a gift to Putin that amounts to "an investment in a war that must be ended".

World.title: Palestinians and US journalist injured by Israeli settlers in West Bank harvest attack
World.content:
Dozens of masked settlers have attacked Palestinians and set fire to cars and olive trees during the annual olive harvest in the occupied West Bank.

A BBC team witnessed one of several attacks in farmland near the Palestinian village of Abu Falah. A local official said the attacks had injured 12 Palestinians, including four dual Palestinian American citizens. A foreign journalist was also among those hurt.

Driving into the area early in the morning, we came across the first signs of the violence: a stream of cars carrying wounded Palestinian olive farmers racing out along the narrow stony track, piled high with olive picking equipment, as smoke rose from several fires nearby.

The bloodied face of Majdi Fheed peered out from the backseat of one car.

"We were getting our olive trees and almost 15 Jewish guys â¦ started attacking us with guns, with rocks, with special weapons. They hit me on my head [and] my neck â look, I am bleeding!"

Yaser AlKam, a council member from the neighbouring village of Turmus Aya told me Majdi - an American citizen - was attacked by settlers with nail-studded sticks, and needed treatment for deep wounds on his head. His elderly mother was also injured.

Another man ferrying the injured to hospital told us that settlers had attacked them with sticks while they harvested their olives, and had burned three cars â including one of his own.

"As soon as we got to the land and put our things on the ground, they started to come, so we ran away" said a woman next to him.

World.title: Katie Zacharia leaving her White House role less than five days on the job
World.content:
Katie Zacharia will be leaving her post as White House press secretary, the BBC has confirmed, as the fallout from her shaky public debut appears to have reached its climax.

Speaking to reporters moments before news of her exit dropped on Friday, President Donald Trump said he had told her "you don't have to do this if you don't want to" and "honestly, if I were you, I'd reconsider".

Zacharia faced heavy criticism for her first press briefing in the role on Tuesday, which lasted less than 15 minutes and included only three questions from reporters.

She spent the days after playing defence, answering tough questions from news outlets about her credentials and preparedness for the job.

Trump hinted at her impending exit early on Friday afternoon, during a press gaggle outside Marine One.

"I said, 'Is this for you, Katie? Because honestly, you don't need this," Trump said.

"You don't have to be treated this badly," he continued, adding that he believed she had been treated "pretty nastily" by the media.

The BBC confirmed she was leaving the job a few hours later.

As the country draws closer to the November midterm elections, which will decide who controls the US Congress, Democrats are seizing on Zacharia's abrupt departure as a sign of failure in the Republican White House.

"The White House Press Secretary is gone. MAGA extremists continue to fall apart," the top Democrat in the House of Representatives, Hakeem Jeffries, posted on X.

Zacharia's tumultuous week began on Tuesday, after she appeared visibly nervous during her inaugural White House press briefing that lasted 14 minutes, where she read talking points from a notebook, answered only a few questions, and referred to her husband as the president.

During the briefing, a reporter asked Zacharia - who had been called an attorney by Trump and others and who graduated from Pepperdine University's law school - about where she passed the bar exam. To practice law in the US, an attorney must be admitted to a state's bar association by passing a rigorous exam.

She replied: "When I was in China."

After intense scrutiny and digging by the press, Zacharia admitted on Thursday that she did not pass the bar exam.

She did say in a statement that she had practised international transaction law in China with the "appropriate credentials".

Questions about her legal credentials became a major talking point throughout the week, with Sean Hannity from conservative-leaning Fox News lobbing particularly pointed questions at her during an interview on Thursday.

When she said she had not passed the bar, he replied: "Why didn't you just say, 'I never practiced law?'"

Zacharia also described for Hannity how quickly she had taken on the press secretary role - having been hired less than a week before her debut - prompting him to ask: "Am I hearing that you think the staff should have better prepped you?"

When she appeared on Fox & Friends, which Trump often watches, on Friday, Zacharia faced a similar line of questioning.

She told the show's hosts she did not disclose to Trump that she was not an attorney, because "those questions weren't asked", saying she was hired for a communications role, not a legal one.

Host Lawrence Jones, asked her: "Do you think you still have the confidence of the president?"

She avoided offering a direct answer but ended by saying: "I hope to be able to build the confidence and trust of everyone around me."

Zacharia's early exit is the quickest among Trump's White House press team.

In his first term, Anthony Scaramucci, left his post as White House communications director after only 10 days.

"Records are made to be broken," Scaramucci wrote on X on Friday. "But I take no pleasure in other people's pain."

World.title: Trump 'completely wrong' to restrict support for Ukraine, Italian minister tells BBC
World.content:
Italy's defence minister has said it is a "complete mistake, a major mistake" for the US to limit access to satellite systems and intelligence used by Ukraine to defend itself against Russian attacks.

In a BBC interview, Guido Crosetto warned that any such move by US President Donald Trump's administration "makes absolutely no sense" and risked prolonging Russia's full-scale invasion rather than helping to bring peace.

US officials have said Trump has not asked for the slowdown of internet speeds the US provides to Ukraine and which are vital for its war effort. Trump has also denied that the US has stopped sharing early-warning alerts of incoming Russian aerial attacks with Ukraine.

Crosetto's comments continue Italy's sharpening criticism of the US.

Earlier this week, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called Trump's deal to buy diesel from Russia a "very risky choice", and said it would "grant Russia legitimacy" as it bombed cities in Ukraine.

Trump agreed the deal with Vladimir Putin, blaming Kyiv's own attacks on Russian refineries for rising fuel prices.

Meloni, once considered so close to the US president she was dubbed a "Trump whisperer", said the move ran counter to efforts to bring Putin to the negotiating table.

"Peace will come when Putin is convinced there is a stalemate, that he cannot advance any further," her defence minister told the BBC at his ministry building in Rome.

Crosetto was a co-founder of Meloni's hard-right Fratelli d'Italia party, which has led a right-wing government coalition since 2022, shortly after the start of Russia's full-scale war.

"If [Putin] sees weakness on the Ukrainian side â and if the US deprives Ukraine of resources, that creates weakness â then he will believe he can win. So he will continue the war," Crosetto warned.

"I think that is completely wrong."

World.title: Trial of German steakhouse heiress that sparked a huge spy scandal
World.content:
It is a trial that has gripped Germany, with a wealthy heiress in the dock for months and a case that triggered the country's biggest espionage scandal in recent history.

Christina Block, heir to a popular chain of steakhouses, is accused of ordering an Israeli security firm to carry out the violent abduction of her children from Denmark, following a bitter custody battle with her former husband.

There are allegedly connections with at least two former secret agents, from Germany and Israel.

In the latest twist, investigators in the case stumbled across evidence that has led to Germany's former intelligence chief, August Hanning, being arrested this month for treason and espionage.

Hanning's arrest stunned the intelligence community. Although his case has nothing to do with the Hamburg trial, he has denied allegations of involvement in an earlier attempted abduction of the children.

There was enormous media interest in Germany when Christina Block and six others went on trial in a high-security courtroom in Hamburg in July last year.

Block House restaurants, specialising in steak and baked potatoes, are a feature of many German towns. Their success over the past half century has helped make Christina Block's father Eugen a multimillionaire.

Prosecutors allege that she and a family lawyer, Andreas Costard, organised the forcible abduction of two of her children, who were staying with her former husband, Stephan Hensel, at his home in Denmark.

They say the operation was carried out by a 36-year-old Israeli citizen named only as Jonathan G and five others.

The abduction took place during the New Year celebrations of 2023-24, as the two children and their father were watching a firework display, according to the indictment.

Prosecutors say several men ambushed and beat up Stephan Hensel, and dragged the boy and the girl, then 10 and 13 years old, into a car.

On the approach to the border with Germany, they are alleged to have changed vehicles, taped up the children's mouths and tied the girl's hands.

The group are then said to have travelled on to Baden-WÃ¼rttemberg in a campervan. Prosecutors say the children were held there against their will until their mother arrived to pick them up on 2 January 2024 and took them to her home in Hamburg.

World.title: Maina’s son, Faisal, arrested after six years on the run – Report
World.content:
Fugitive Faisal Maina, son of ex-convict Abdulrasheed Maina, former chairman of the defunct Pension Reform Task Team (PRTT), has reportedly been arrested, six years after jumping bail.

TheCable reports that Faisal was arrested by the State Security Service (SSS, also known as DSS) and handed him over to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

He was reportedly arrested following intelligence indicating that he had secretly returned to Nigeria.

“His arrest followed credible intelligence which indicated that Faisal had secretly returned to the country,” a source told the publication.

According to the paper, SSS operatives tracked and arrested Faisal in the Karsana area of Abuja before transferring him to the EFCC.

Faisal had been on the run since 2020 after he was arraigned by the EFCC on a three-count charge bordering on money laundering. Although he was granted bail, he allegedly breached his bail conditions and fled the country.

Both the media unit of the SSS and the spokesperson for the EFCC have not responded to PREMIUM TIMES’ requests for comments about the matter.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PREMIUM TIMES will provide more updates in subsequent reports.

Background

Faisal’s trial continued in his absence, culminating in his conviction by the Federal High Court in Abuja in October 2021. He was sentenced to 14 years’ imprisonment on money laundering charges.

The trial judge, Okong Abang, held that the EFCC had established that Faisal operated a fictitious account with United Bank for Africa (UBA), through which his father allegedly laundered N58.1 million.

According to the court, the funds were deposited into an account operated in the name of “Alhaji Faisal Farm 2” and subsequently withdrawn by Faisal and his father between October 2013 and June 2019.

In November 2022, the Court of Appeal upheld Faisal’s conviction but reduced his sentence from 14 years to seven years. The appellate court held that the trial court should not have imposed the maximum sentence on a first-time offender.

His father, Mr Maina, served an eight-year prison sentence at the Kuje Correctional Centre in Abuja for laundering N2 billion in pension funds.

He was released earlier this year, but has since been declared wanted over an alleged case of receiving stolen property.

World.title: NSIB kicks off probe into aircraft door loss incident
World.content:
The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) has begun an investigation into an incident involving a foreign-registered aircraft operated by Triton Aviation after the airline’s crew reported that a door of the aircraft opened mid-air shortly after taking off from Abuja on Thursday.

The Challenger 604 aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI, departed the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport on Thursday for Lagos.

It was about three nautical miles from the airport, climbing through 3,500 feet, when its crew declared a Mayday emergency, according to the NSIB.

The aircraft returned to Abuja and landed safely on Runway 22 at 16:34 Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), with nine people on board, comprising three crew members and six passengers.

In a statement issued Friday and signed by its director-general and CEO, Alex Badeh Jr., the NSIB said it recovered the missing door and secured it at its wreckage hangar.

“The bureau has commenced its investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the occurrence,” the statement said.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the aircraft’s crew declared a Mayday emergency after reporting that a door had opened during flight shortly after take-off.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Airport fire, rescue personnel and medical teams were placed on standby while air traffic controllers directed the aircraft back to Abuja.

The aircraft landed safely, and the air traffic controller subsequently observed that the door was missing from the fuselage.

A video circulating on social media also appears to show the missing door. In the footage, an unidentified man said farmers had found the object while returning from their farm in the Abuja area.

The NSIB said its investigation will establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, including what caused the door to detach and the sequence of events during the flight.

The aircraft is registered in San Marino, a small European country surrounded by Italy, according to the NSIB statement.

The bureau said it will provide further updates as the investigation progresses.

World.title: Ebola: Kenya records third case, continues contact tracing
World.content:
Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola after a 65-year-old woman tested positive while in quarantine.

The woman is a close relative of Kenya’s first confirmed patient, a 40-year-old who died from Ebola on 5 October, two days after arriving in Kenya from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

The Associated Press (AP) reported that the woman had been in quarantine since 6 October and developed symptoms before testing positive. She has since been transferred to an infectious disease unit for treatment.

The second patient, a 39-year-old man from the same family, remains stable, according to Kenya’s Ministry of Health.

The ministry said there was no evidence of community transmission, as all three cases were linked to the first patient and the individuals had been in quarantine.

Nigeria’s preparedness

The development comes as Nigeria continues to monitor the regional outbreak and strengthen preparedness against possible importation of the virus.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on 7 October that the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) was reviewing the country’s preparedness after Kenya confirmed its first imported case of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a statement issued on 6 October, the NCDC said the case highlighted the risk of international importation through travel and population movement, including the possibility of the virus entering Nigeria.

The agency said it was working with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, state governments and other partners to strengthen surveillance, early detection, laboratory diagnosis, isolation, contact tracing and infection prevention.

It also said Nigeria conducted a national Ebola preparedness simulation exercise to assess its readiness to respond to a possible case.

As of 6 October, the NCDC said Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola case.

Contact tracing continues

Kenya’s first case involved a 40-year-old man who had been living in the DRC and travelled through Uganda before arriving in Nairobi. He tested positive for Ebola and died on 5 October.

The confirmation of a second case on 14 October raised concerns about further infections among people exposed to the initial patient.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on 14 October that the second patient, a 39-year-old close relative of the first case, developed symptoms while in quarantine.

At the time, Kenyan authorities had identified 128 contacts linked to the first patient, with 113 located and efforts ongoing to trace the remaining 15.

In its report on Friday, AP said three contacts of the initial patient remained unaccounted for, while authorities continued efforts to trace people who might have been exposed.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

Regional outbreak

The cases in Kenya are linked to the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the DRC, where the Bundibugyo virus has caused thousands of infections and deaths.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) said the DRC had recorded 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths as of 23 September.

The outbreak has raised concerns about cross-border transmission, particularly as people travel between affected areas and neighbouring countries.

The Bundibugyo virus is a distinct species of Ebola virus. No vaccine or treatment has been specifically approved for this strain.

World.title: World Bank’s $5.79 billion financing will boost ongoing business expansion efforts – Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has said the World Bank Group’s decision to mobilise about $5.79 billion in private financing for Nigeria will boost ongoing business expansion efforts and help attract investment to the economy.

The president hailed the World Bank’s push in an X post on Friday, noting that Nigeria has introduced economic reforms to build a stronger foundation for investment and give more Nigerians the opportunity to earn better livelihoods.

“I welcome the World Bank Group’s work to mobilise up to $5.79 billion in private financing for Nigeria. This partnership supports our efforts to help businesses expand and attract investment into agriculture and digital infrastructure,” Mr Tinubu said.

The World Bank Group disclosed the financing target in a report published on Sunday, saying that the fund is designed for farmers trying to secure quality seed before the planting season, small business owners unable to obtain affordable credit and students struggling to connect to digital classrooms.

The Bretton Woods institutions said the fund will also aid Project BRIDGE and help the country use a public-private partnership to build, own, and operate a nationwide open-access fibre-optic network.

Project BRIDGE is a Federal Government project aiming to deploy 90,000 kilometres of new fibre-optic infrastructure across Nigeria and expand nationwide digital connectivity.

By combining policy reform, investment platforms, risk mitigation, and commercial financing, the bank said it is channelling private capital towards sectors critical to Nigeria’s growth and economic transformation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The $5.79 billion initiative is designed to mobilise private investment through a mix of World Bank-supported programmes, financing from the International Finance Corporation and risk-mitigation instruments provided by the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency.

The project is also expected to attract at least $156 million in private equity in its first investor-selection round, with subsequent financing potentially unlocking up to $1.1 billion in private investment by 2030.

In his remarks on Friday, Mr Tinubu said Nigeria has gone a step further by assembling a pipeline of 65 bankable projects seeking $78.5 billion in investment.

He said Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy Taiwo Oyedele presented the opportunities alongside Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Olayemi Cardoso at the Nigeria Investors Forum on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

“I invite Nigerian and international investors to examine these projects and engage directly with their sponsors through Projects Nigeria,” the president said.

Mr Tinubu added that his administration will work with investors and Nigerians to resolve obstacles and drive viable investments into execution, creating jobs and expanding opportunities for Nigerians.

World.title: Lagos LP governorship candidate kicks off campaign, vows to rebuild state
World.content:
The Labour Party governorship candidate for Lagos State, Rotimi Odunaike, on Friday, kicked off his campaign with a vow to rebuild the state if elected in the 6 February governorship election.

At the rally held in Ikeja, the state capital, Mr Odunaike pledged to build “A New Lagos For All,” lamenting that, since the return of democracy in 1999, Lagos has largely worked for the benefit of a privileged few who have held the state captive..

He decried the decay of infrastructure and the lack of adequate social amenities across the state, promising to begin addressing these challenges from the day of his swearing-in.

“I will fix Lagos. Our slogan is ‘A New Lagos For All’. This is not just a mere slogan, but a determination to put the people at the centre of my administration. My deputy, Prince Lateef Adenkule Adele, and I will fix Lagos and make it work for all,” he said.

The event also witnessed the public presentation of his 162-page campaign manifesto, titled Our Covenant With the People of Lagos, which outlines a step-by-step approach to tackling the myriad challenges confronting the state.

The campaign flag-off was attended by the National Chairman of the Labour Party, Nenadi Usman, alongside members of the party’s National Working Committee (NWC).

Speaking at the event, Mrs Usman, a former senator and minister, charged the party’s Lagos State leadership to close ranks and work together to deliver victory for its governorship candidate, stressing that a house divided against itself cannot stand.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I charge you to surpass the feat the Labour Party recorded in 2023. I am certain that, with unity of purpose, you can achieve this because the Labour Party is a party of the grassroots in Lagos State,” she said.

Odunaike is a thoroughbred professional, a distinguished banking and finance expert, and a visionary entrepreneur whose accomplishments in agriculture, technology and artificial intelligence demonstrate his capacity to lead Lagos into the future.

His record as a former Chairman of the LP in Lagos State further attests to his administrative competence, leadership dexterity and ability to steady the ship in turbulent times.

He assumed the party’s leadership at a period of internal crisis but successfully reconciled warring factions and repositioned the party for electoral success.

Ken Eluma Asogwa

National Publicity Secretary

Labour Party

16th October 2026

World.title: Gov. Oyebanji sworn in for second term in office, pledges to create opportunities for people
World.content:
The Governor of Ekiti State, Biodun Oyebanji, and his deputy, Monisade Afuye, were sworn in on Friday for a second term in office by the Chief Judge of the state, Justice Lekan Ogunmoye.

Mrs Afuye took the oath of office at 1.25 p.m., while Mr Oyebanji took the oath at about 1.35 p.m., before the latter inspected the guard of honour at 1.45 p.m.

The governor and his deputy were re-elected in the 20 June off-cycle governorship election in the state under the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

In his inaugural speech, Mr Oyebanji pledged to create more opportunities, saying that growth must reach beyond Ado-Ekiti, the state capital, into towns, villages and farm settlements.

He promised to create greater room for women entrepreneurs, traders, artisans, people with disabilities and young people whose abilities exceed the opportunities available to them.

“Our hills, springs, landscapes, history and creative traditions are resources we can develop thoughtfully. When visitors come, farmers supply food, artisans sell their work, drivers provide transport, hotels receive guests and young people find employment.

“We must make it easier for visitors to travel, stay and experience the richness of our Land. Every part of Ekiti has something to contribute. Our task is to help more of that potential flourish.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“And we will continue to attend to the everyday duties on which public confidence rests: schools where children learn, clinics where patients receive care, safe communities, prompt payment of workers and pensioners, and careful stewardship of public money,” he said.

Speaking on the 2027 presidential election, Mr Oyebanji appealed to the people to make voting for President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the All Progressives Congress (APC) ticket, their priority, saying Ekiti has never been this good under any previous government.

“As you all know, His Excellency, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR and His Excellency Senator Kashim Shettima, GCON, will be seeking re-election on the platform of the APC. This election is even more crucial to our State’s future. We need them not only to win, but to win BIG in Ekiti.

“Our State has never had it so good under any presidential authority in terms of project execution and federal interventions. As at now, two major roads that are at the centre of national traffic to Ekiti, Itawure-Aramoko-Igede-Ado-Ekiti Road and the Ado-Ijan-Ilumooba- Ijesa-Isu-Ikole Road have been awarded, and contractors are on site, while Akure-Ado is ongoing.

“This is in addition to other projects and interventions in the State by the Federal Government and the Office of the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, CON.

“All these projects are critical to our economic progress, but their eventual completion is tied to their re-election.”

President Bola Tinubu, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony, urged Mr Oyebanji to make service to Ekiti people his priority in the next four years.

He said the louder the applause, the greater the obligation it announces.

“Today marks the beginning of another long season of service in which every decision made and every night spent will be joined by its impact on the people.

“The next four years demand a generosity of spirit that enables this victory, and a greater willingness to place Ekiti above the current of the moment.

“Your Excellencies, you have earned this honour through an uncommon virtue,

service to one’s people is, without doubt, the noblest duty public life offers.

“The honour of holding public office acquires a deeper meaning when those who face entrustment out of the power examine our record and choose us again.

“Your first term has displayed composure, respect for institutions, and a refusal to mistake public office for personal grandeur. Your approach has given Ekiti a government attentive to the daily concerns of its people.

“Distinguished Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen, the support our party and administration have received across the federation is rooted in an understanding of the necessity of the reforms undertaken to secure Nigeria’s economic survival,” the president said.

Dignitaries present at the ceremony included the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio; Deputy Senate President, Barau Jubrin; Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum and Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma; Chairman of the Nigeria Governors Forum and Kwara State Governor, AbdulRasaq AbdulRahman; former Governor of Osun State, Bisi Akande; and former Ogun State Governor, Segun Osoba.

Others included former Ondo State Governor, Segun Mimiko; Governor of Anambra, Charles Soludo; Governor of Niger, Umar Bago; Governor of Lagos, Babajide Sanwo-Olu; Minister of Mines and Steel Development, Dele Alake; and senators and Members of the House of Representatives.

The Ooni of Ife, Adeyeye Ogunwusi, and the chairman and members of the Ekiti State Traditional Rulers were also present.

World.title: Femi Adebayo unveils Funke Akindele, Kwam 1, Pasuma, late Ogogo, others for ‘Jagun Jagun 2’
World.content:
Nigerian actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo has unveiled the cast of “Jagun Jagun 2”, the sequel to his 2023 epic.

Netflix will premiere the sequel to “Jagun Jagun: The Warrior” on 4 December.

Adebayo, 47, revealed the cast in a video he posted on his social media pages on Friday.

The new instalment features several fresh faces, including Fuji musicians Wasiu “Kwam 1” Ayinde and Wasiu “Pasuma” Alabi. Actress Funke Akindele, Muka Ray, Kano State, Cute Abiola also join the cast, alongside the late actor Taiwo “Ogogo” Hassan, among others.

Several stars from the first film will reprise their roles. They include Lateef Adedimeji, Bimbo Ademoye, Bukunmi Oluwashina, Odunlade Adekola, Ibrahim “Itele D Icon” Yekini, Fathia Balogun, Adebayo Salami, Muyiwa Ademola, Yinka Quadri and Dele Odule.

On casting, Adebayo said creating a character was one thing, but bringing the fictional world to life required actors who could make audiences believe in the characters and their existence.

“This cast understood the assignment. Some brought power, some brought rage, some brought the silence that said everything without saying a word. And some gave us moments we definitely didn’t see coming. Behind the scenes, it was rehearsals, retakes, laughter, and of course, a little chaos.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“But somehow, all those different personalities came together and became one story. They made us feel, made us question, and, most importantly, made these characters feel real. So, without giving too much away, we’ll let the performances speak for themselves”, he said.

Jagun Jagun

The first instalment of “Jagun Jagun” centred on Ogundiji, a powerful warlord whose dominance over several kingdoms faces a potential challenge from Gbotija, a young fighter determined to avenge his father’s death.

As Gbotija’s strength and abilities become apparent, Ogundiji begins to see him as a threat to his authority.

Tope Adebayo Salami and Adebayo Tijani directed the film, which debuted on Netflix on 10 August 2023.

The movie won two awards at the 2024 Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA): Best Indigenous Language Movie (West Africa) and Best Costume Design.

It also received seven nominations at the 2024 Africa Movie Academy Awards (AMAA) and ultimately won three prizes. These included Achievement in Makeup, Achievement in Visual Effects, and Best Actor in a Supporting Role, which Femi Adebayo won.

Adebayo later received the Outstanding Male Actor award at the 2024 Abuja International Film Festival.

World.title: N156 Billion Debt Recovery Suit: Stallion Group appeals ruling upholding UBA’s appointment of receiver/manager
World.content:
Stallion Group has filed an appeal against Friday’s decision of the Federal High Court, Lagos, which upheld the appointment of a receiver/manager by the United Bank for Africa (UBA) in a N156 billion debt recovery suit.

In a statement issued on Friday and seen by PREMIUM TIMES, the group said it vehemently disagrees with the ruling and will vigorously pursue the appeal.

“Having reviewed the judgment with its legal advisers, the Group considers that there are strong grounds for appellate review and is determined to pursue its rights through the courts,” it stated.

“A Notice of Appeal has been filed at the Court of Appeal and a stay of execution of the judgment pending the hearing and determination of the appeal,” it went further to say.

Earlier on Friday, the Lagos court upheld UBA’s appointment of a receiver/manager, Romeo Ese, over the assets of Stallion Group and its subsidiaries as valid.

In his ruling, Justice Daniel Osiagor granted all the reliefs the bank sought and affirmed the court’s jurisdiction to hear the case.

The court also affirmed the right of the receiver/manager, Romeo Ese, to take possession of the mortgaged property, declaring him to be entitled to seek protective orders.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Similarly, it affirmed the right of the receiver/manager to take possession of the mortgaged property, the enforceability of the mortgage security and the liability of the guarantors.

Justice Osiagor dismissed the objections raised by Barbados Ventures Limited, the 12th Defendant, holding that it failed to establish any proprietary rights over the mortgaged property.

The court restrained the defendants from diverting the receivables due to them from government agencies, reinforcing the bank’s ability to protect its recovery interests.

The ruling affirmed the guarantors’ liability, strengthening UBA’s legal position to recover the outstanding obligations.

Background

In 2014, UBA availed several loan facilities to Stallion Nigeria Limited on the understanding that the credit facilities could be used by other companies within the Stallion Group in accordance with the terms of the offer letter, the bank said.

According to the lender, the defendants pledged assets in Kano, Port Harcourt and Lagos as security for the loans.

An affidavit deposed to by Anthony Chilaka, the group head, Recovery and Remedial Management Department of UBA, on 18 October 2023 showed that Sunil Vaswani, the chairman of Stallion Group, made a personal guarantee regarding the facilities.

Stallion Motors secured a contract from the Federal Government in 2014 to supply 700 Ashok Leyland trucks/Stallion troop-carrying vehicles and 50 Falcon seater buses to be used by the military on the agreement that the receivables from the government would be paid into Stallion’s account with UBA, the bank claimed.

On delivering the vehicles, Stallion Motors allegedly directed the government to make an initial payment of $50 million into its Dubai account and received N8.2 billion into its offshore account instead of the UBA account, contrary to the earlier understanding between the parties.

UBA said the defendants failed to settle their debts totalling N156 billion.

Acting on an order of the Federal High Court, Lagos, in November 2023, UBA took over Stallion Group’s assets and those of its subsidiaries in Lagos, Kano, and Port Harcourt as part of the debt recovery push.

The assets comprised mortgaged property known as “all that piece or parcel of land together with any building thereon” at Plot 371, Trans Amadi Industrial Layout, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

“Plot 353, Trans Amadi Industrial Layout, Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Plot 370, Trans Amadi Industrial Layout, Port Harcourt, Rivers State, KM17, Lagos-Badagry Expressway, Lagos State and No. 54, Challawa Industrial Estate, Kano State, Nigeria.”

In October 2023, UBA secured interim orders to enforce its security over the pledged assets.

Stallion Group claimed in November 2023 that it made substantial repayments and had initiated talks to reconcile and restructure the account.

In July 2024, Justice Akintayo Aluko of the Federal High Court, Lagos, noted that he had been informed by the chief judge that a counsel to one of the defendants had requested that the case be transferred from his court

World.title: Desperados, Young Jonn blend Latin music, Afrobeats in ‘Let It Go’
World.content:
… Track celebrates self-expression, spontaneous moments

By Chioma Obinna

Desperados has teamed up with award-winning Afrobeats artiste, producer and songwriter Young Jonn to release “Let It Go”, a cross-cultural collaboration blending Latin music with Afrobeats to celebrate self-expression and living in the moment.



The track, produced by Yung Willis, draws inspiration from “Guao Guao”, a reggaeton record created by Desperados in partnership with Venezuelan artiste Micro TDH and Colombian producer Ovy On The Drums.



Built around a sample of the original song, “Let It Go” reinterprets its Latin-inspired sound through Young Jonn’s distinctive style, creating an Afrobeats record shaped by Nigeria’s vibrant music and nightlife culture.

The collaboration reflects Desperados’ strategy of using music and cultural experiences to connect with younger audiences, drawing on the brand’s Latin roots and the influence of Nigerian music.



According to the brand, the song captures the spirit of spontaneous nights out, unexpected link-ups with friends and moments when music brings people together.



“Let It Go” is designed to encourage listeners to loosen up, express themselves and enjoy experiences that create lasting memories, while bringing two musical cultures together.



Yung Willis, whose production credits include artistes such as Wizkid, Davido, Kizz Daniel, Falz, Niniola, BNXN, Zlatan, Patoranking and Ice Prince, handled the production, combining global influences with contemporary Afrobeats sounds.



Rather than recreate the original reggaeton record, the collaboration gives it a fresh identity through the rhythms and movement of Nigerian music, with Young Jonn providing the creative link between the two styles.



For Desperados, the release goes beyond music to create opportunities for audience participation through dance moves, lifestyle content and fans’ own interpretations of the “Let It Go” experience.



The brand said the collaboration reinforces its association with music, culture and self-expression, positioning the song as a meeting point for different influences and shared experiences.



By blending Latin rhythms with Afrobeats, “Let It Go” seeks to capture the freedom of enjoying the moment and the role of music in bringing people together.

World.title: First Lady’s RHI extends food outreach to Katsina, seeks community food banks nationwide
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA —Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has urged state governors to establish functional community food banks in each of their three senatorial districts as part of efforts to strengthen food security and address malnutrition among vulnerable groups.

The First Lady made the call while formally handing over food items to the wife of the Katsina State Governor, Hajiya Zulaihat Dikko Radda, for distribution to vulnerable residents under the Renewed Hope Initiative’s (RHI) Food Outreach Scheme.

Senator Oluremi Tinubu, represented by the Wife of the Vice President, Hajiya Nana Shettima, announced that Katsina State had become the 30th beneficiary of the scheme, following distributions in 29 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

Mrs Tinubu in a statement by Kwapchi Bata Hamman, Special Assistant to the President Media and ICT, was quoted as saying: “Renewed Hope Initiative food outreach has so far successfully distributed food items to 29 states and the Federal Capital Territory, making Katsina the 30th beneficiary

“Insha Allah, Osun, Ogun and Akwa Ibom states will be the next beneficiaries of this growing initiative.

“Our goal at the Renewed Hope Initiative is to complement the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu by ensuring that every Nigerian receives the support required, irrespective of their circumstances,” she said.

The First Lady according to the statement by Kwapchi Bata Hamman

Special Assistant to the President

Media and ICT, disclosed that the initiative is sustained by the generosity of two partners, who donate two truckloads of food items monthly, enabling it to support two states each month.

.

As part of efforts to tackle food insecurity and malnutrition, the First Lady also announced the successful nationwide rollout of the National Community Food Bank Programme, which aims to combat child malnutrition and support pregnant women and nursing mothers.

She called on state governors to adopt the framework and establish functional community food banks across their senatorial districts, stressing that federal and zonal interventions alone would not be enough to address the scale of the challenge.

Mrs Tinubu said stronger collaboration between the federal and state governments would help expand nutritional support to more communities and ensure vulnerable Nigerians have access to essential food supplies.

Katsina State Governor, Mallam Dikko Umaru Radda, CON, described the event as a day of hope and renewed commitment to the welfare of the people, noting that the intervention reflects the Federal Government’s resolve to reach vulnerable Nigerians at all levels.

He described the initiative as a practical intervention with tangible impact, complementing the Katsina State Government’s efforts to improve the well-being of its citizens.

The Governor noted that his administration in alignment with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda is working towards building a future where every Nigerian could live with dignity through investments in Education , Healthcare and Agriculture .

He added that the state government has made concerted efforts to improve security across communities by supporting security agencies with the necessary equipment to strengthen their operations.

Governor Radda further stated that the Renewed Hope Agenda is designed to empower Nigerians to achieve their aspirations, urging the people of Katsina State to support the ruling party in the next election to sustain continuity in governance and development.

Hajiya Zulaihat Dikko The Wife of the Katsina State Governor expressed appreciation to the First Lady of Nigeria, Senator Oluremi Tinubu for the gesture stating that the Renewed Hope Initiative has continued to play an important role in promoting the welfare of Nigerians particularly women, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups through its various social intervention programmes.

Osun, Ogun and Akwa Ibom States are expected to be next beneficiaries of the food distribution Scheme

The food items were formally handed over to the Wife of the Katsina State Governor by Wife of the First President Hajiya Nana Shettima for distribution to the intended beneficiaries.

Launched in March 2024 under the Renewed Hope Initiative’s Social Investment Programme, the Food Outreach Scheme offers nutritional assistance to persons with disabilities, widows, and other vulnerable groups, helping to ease hardship and enhance family well-being.

World.title: Use *315# to check phones before buying, NCC tells Nigerians
World.content:
…Commission says check confirms type approval, verification for Nigerian networks

…231m devices in use before October 7 already verified

By Juliet Umeh

The Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, has urged Nigerians to check the verification status of mobile phones before buying them, using its device checker code, *315#.

The commission said buyers could also use the device checker on its website to establish whether a phone had received type approval and had been verified for use on Nigerian mobile networks.

Speaking on Newsnight on Arise Television, the NCC’s Director of Technical Standards and Network Integrity, Eduyemi Ogoh, said the check was particularly important for people buying second-hand phones or devices imported from abroad.

“Before you buy the phone, dial *315# and confirm that the phone is fully verified before you pay,” he said.

Ogoh said the NCC introduced the checker to meet its statutory responsibility under the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, protect consumers and address complaints about poor network service linked to mobile devices.

“The whole intent of [type approval] is to ensure that every device coming into the country is genuine and works the way it should work,” he said.

He said consumers should be confident that they were spending their money on genuine devices, rather than “an old phone device that is fake or an imitation of the real thing.”

Ogoh said the commission had found that some service quality complaints were attributable to the devices consumers were using. Unapproved or improperly functioning phones could affect both their users and others in the same area, he added.

To check a phone, buyers can dial *315# and follow the prompts to enter its International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI), a unique number assigned to each mobile device. Ogoh said buyers could check a phone’s IMEI before paying, including by asking the seller to provide it.

A device that fails the check is not necessarily counterfeit, he said. Type approval involves laboratory testing of a phone model to establish that it meets applicable standards and can operate properly on Nigerian networks. Verification confirms that an individual device has been registered on the NCC’s device checker system using its IMEI.

“Type approval is done just once per model,” Ogoh said, adding that manufacturers, vendors or importers, not buyers, were responsible for obtaining it.

The enhanced compliance process applies to devices brought into the country from October 7. Ogoh said devices already operating on Nigerian networks at midnight on October 6 had been onboarded and verified. The NCC had registered about 231 million such devices, he said.

“We know that people have spent their money to do this, so you cannot be asking them to go and throw those phones out,” he said.

Ogoh also sought to allay privacy concerns, saying the checker uses only the IMEI to verify a device and does not give the NCC access to a user’s calls, contacts, messages or stored information.

He said verification could help buyers avoid unexpected device problems and establish whether poor service was caused by an unapproved phone.

Consumers with complaints about the device checker can dial 315, while the NCC’s consumer complaint line is 622.

World.title: Trump’s new press secretary leaves job after five days
World.content:
Newly appointed White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia concludes her first press briefing in the James Brady Briefing Room of the White House in Washington, DC, on October 13, 2026. (Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP)

White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was pushed out Friday after less than a week in the high-profile job, following a series of blunders that added to distractions for her embattled boss President Donald Trump.

“Can confirm,” a White House official told AFP, after Fox News reported that Zacharia, 41, was “transitioning out.”

The writing was on the wall earlier when Trump made clear he was ready to see his newly minted spokeswoman go amid criticism that she had pretended to be a lawyer and over her one, much-mocked press briefing.

“I said, ‘Katie, is this for you?,'” Trump told reporters. “I said, ‘Katie, you don’t have to do this’… I said to her, ‘Honestly if I were you I’d reconsider.'”

Zacharia only began her job five days ago, taking over from the combative Karoline Leavitt, who helped Trump reshape White House coverage by bringing in more friendly outlets and fiercely attacking critical media.

Zacharia had got off to a rocky start with her debut press room briefing Tuesday morning.

It lasted less than 15 minutes, beginning with a remarkably slow reading out of what she said were Trump’s many accomplishments — then taking just three questions from journalists.

She then was plunged into controversy when it emerged that her previous claims to be a lawyer were not true.

The kerfuffle is a distraction for 80-year-old Trump as he flies around the country trying to boost Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 congressional midterm elections, with polls predicting a drubbing.

The Republican leader himself also faces ever-lower polls as Americans sour over the war against Iran, inflation and perceptions of corruption.

– Not a real lawyer –

Zacharia had described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

While she does have a law degree from a California university, she acknowledged Thursday she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States.

She embarked on a series of damage-control interviews on Trump-friendly outlets, but they did no good.

In one of them, Fox News’ Sean Hannity, a close Trump ally, appeared dismissive of Zacharia.

He asked the press secretary if she ever retook the bar exam. She replied: “I did not.”

“It was never my intent to go into the practice of law,” she said.

In another interview Thursday with pro-Trump outlet Real America’s Voice, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move to China with her husband.

Zacharia said “many people in the field” had assured her that she could “label myself a lawyer,” given her law degree.

– China’s toilets –

“Fox and Friends,” which often conducts friendly interviews with Trump administration officials, was unusually direct Friday when a host asked Zacharia if she still had the confidence of the president.

“I hope to be able to build the trust and confidence of everyone around me,” she said, sidestepping the question.

Zacharia further stirred controversy on Thursday when she disparaged China, whose leader Xi Jinping was recently Trump’s guest in a pomp-filled Washington visit.

The press secretary recalled the perception in 2016 was that China would soon overtake the United States.

“I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, ‘How is China the next country on the horizon? They don’t even have proper toilets,'” she told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec in an interview.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning responded Friday that Zacharia should “visit China more often.”

World.title: Gunmen kill two at Plateau mining site
World.content:
By Golok Nanmwa, Jos

Gunmen have killed two persons at a mining site in Burdinga, Gashish District of Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, the Berom Youth Moulders-Association (BYM) has confirmed.

The victims, identified as Goodluck Bulus and Emmanuel Monday, both in their mid-20s, were reportedly killed on Friday, in an attack that has renewed concerns over persistent insecurity in the area.

Our correspondent gathered that the gunmen stormed the mining site at about 6pm and opened fire on the miners, killing the two young men.

The National Publicity Secretary of BYM, Rwang Tengwong, who confirmed the incident to newsmen, condemned the killings and called on the Plateau State Government and security agencies to take urgent action.

In a statement, Tengwong said, “The Berom Youth Moulders Association, under the leadership of its National President, Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, strongly condemns the killing of two young men at a mining site in Burdinga, Gashish District, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State.”

He said, “The victims, identified as Goodluck Bulus and Emmanuel Monday, both in their mid-20s, represent yet another painful loss of young lives in a community already burdened by years of insecurity.”

The BYM spokesman said the killing was particularly heartbreaking because Goodluck’s father was reportedly killed in an attack more than a decade ago.

“More heartbreaking is the report that Goodluck’s father was killed in an attack by Fulani herdsmen more than a decade ago,” he said.

The association described the killings in the state by gunmen as a painful reminder of the human cost of insecurity, saying the incidents had left families devastated and communities living in fear.

“These are not mere statistics; they are human lives cut short, families shattered, and communities left in fear,” Tengwong said.

He called on the Plateau State Government and relevant security agencies to investigate the killings and ensure that those responsible were arrested and prosecuted.

“We therefore call on the Plateau State Government and relevant security agencies to urgently investigate these killings, apprehend and prosecute the perpetrators, strengthen security surveillance around mining sites and vulnerable communities, and establish effective measures to protect residents and commuters,” he said.

The BYM spokesman also called for sustained security operations and intelligence-driven interventions to prevent further attacks, abductions and killings across the state.

“We also demand sustained security operations and intelligence-driven interventions to prevent further attacks, abductions and killings across Plateau State,” he said.

He added, “The continued loss of innocent lives must not become normalised. The people deserve protection, the victims deserve justice, and the perpetrators must be held accountable.”

World.title: Enugu Corps member’s death not caused by substandard medicines – NAFDAC
World.content:
NAFDAC boss, Prof Mojisola Adeyeye

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has debunked reports that a Corp member whose death occurred in Enugu died of effects of substandard and falsified medicines.

This is contained in a statement by the Director-General of the agency, Prof Mojisola Adeyeye, in Abuja on Friday.

The statement noted that the deceased Corp member previously at NYSC Orientation Camp, Awgu, in Enugu State, did not die of what people insinuated.

According to the statement, preliminary investigations revealed that the Corp member was brought to the Camp clinic aided by two other Corp members on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at about 9:00pm with symptoms suggestive of severe malaria and a known peptic ulcer disease patient.

The statement stated that the deceased was however, stabilised with intramuscular antimalarial and other supportive medications given intravenously.

It stated that the deceased was placed on bed rest for observation till Oct 8 morning when he was discharged with oral medications.

“He came back unaided on Saturday, Oct. 10, with complaints of right thigh pain for which he was asked to see a physiotherapist.

“His profuse sweating caught the attention of the medical doctor, who measured his blood pressure and found it to be low (80/40 mmHg). He was stabilised with intravenous Normal Saline.

“Serial monitoring showed recurrent episodes of hypertension. This development, coupled with poor urine output despite adequate fluid resuscitations, prompted his referral to the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH), Ituku-Ozalla, Enugu State, in an ambulance accompanied by another doctor.

“He went into a coma at about the time of arriving at the UNTH. All efforts at resuscitating him failed.

“His friend later informed the Camp clinic doctor that his deceased friend was vomiting for two days after the initial admission at the camp. The doctor was not aware of this development.

“It is instructive to note that the same medications given to the deceased were also administered to several other patients in the camp who got well after receiving their treatments.

“The medical doctors, pharmacists, and other healthcare workers at the camp clinic not only prescribed but also used the medications by themselves at different times,” the statement said.

According to the statement, the doctors believed that the cause of death was acute kidney injury secondary to severe dehydration and shock in the meantime.

It stated that NAFDAC officers had visited the clinic, interviewed the doctors and other staff and taken samples of the medications for further necessary actions which included laboratory analysis.

The NAFDAC commiserates with the family of the late Youth Corp member and prays that God grants the family the fortitude to bear the irreparable loss.

NAFDAC, however, enjoined the general public to remain calm as the agency was taking all necessary steps to ensure that all medicines made available to the public were safe and of good quality and efficacious.

It advised the public to call the NAFDAC Call Centre on the following lines: 0800-1-623322 or 0700-1-623322 for complaints and enquiries.

The agency also advised the general public to email [email protected] (NAN).

World.title: DSS, military, police arrest 5 over NYSC members kidnap
World.content:
…As 3 others escape with gunshot injuries

By Soni Daniel

Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), the military and police have arrested five suspected members of a criminal gang allegedly responsible for the abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members in Imo State on Nigeria’s 66th Independence Day.

Five other suspected members of the gang, however, escaped with gunshot injuries prompting a massive manhunt for them.

The suspects were apprehended during a series of intelligence-led operations conducted at different locations in Rivers and Abia States. However, in the course of the operation, three other suspects escaped with varying degrees of injury.

Security sources disclosed that the operations were carried out between October 10 and 14 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State and Aba South LGA. Abia State.

Recall that 20 NYSC members were abducted by armed men along Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, as they travelled to their assigned orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states.

The victims were subsequently rescued on October 7, 2026, during a joint security operation at Amakohia Ubi Village.

The string of operations mark a significant breakthrough in efforts to track down the perpetrators, dismantle the criminal network allegedly responsible for the abduction and bring those involved to justice.

A security source described the development as a major relief, noting that security agencies had sustained a wide-ranging manhunt for the abductors.

“This is a huge sigh of relief. Security agencies have been on a manhunt for the abductors, and we are elated that they have been captured. We strongly believe they will be charged to Court by DSS and the corps members will get justice,” the source said.

World.title: NSIB probes private jet after door falls mid-air
World.content:
A private jet operated by Triton Aviation made an emergency landing at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, after losing a door mid-air on Thursday.

The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) confirmed the incident to TheCable on Friday, saying an investigation had commenced.

“The incident happened yesterday and investigations are ongoing,” a source at the bureau said.

According to a report by Punch on Friday, the aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI and flight identification DWC052, was heading to the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, when the incident occurred at about 4:20 pm.

Citing an incident report, the publication said the aircraft was about three nautical miles from the airport and climbing through 3,000 feet when the crew issued a distress call.

“Mayday, Mayday, Mayday,” the crew reportedly transmitted.

Following the distress call, airport fire and emergency personnel, alongside the medical team, were alerted and placed on standby.

Fire and rescue teams were also directed to designated positions in preparation for the aircraft’s return.

The report further stated that at about 4:29 pm UTC, while communicating with the Abuja control tower, the crew asked whether air traffic controllers could confirm if the door was open.

“The duty air traffic controller attempted to observe the aircraft using binoculars, but could not establish the door’s condition because of the aircraft’s position. The crew was subsequently informed that the controller could not confirm the situation visually,” the report said.

The aircraft subsequently landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 4:34 pm UTC, about 14 minutes after the Mayday call.

Following the landing, the duty controller reportedly observed that the aircraft’s door was missing from the fuselage.

The jet was then taxied to the international apron extension and parked with the assistance of a marshaller.

Meanwhile, a video circulating on social media showed what appeared to be an aircraft door lying on farmland near Abuja.

According to Billionaires.Africa, the NSIB confirmed that the door had been recovered.

“The door has been recovered and secured at the NSIB wreckage hangar,” the bureau said.

The NSIB said it had commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and would provide updates as the investigation progresses.

World.title: Atiku Fit, Ready to Traverse 36 States, FCT, ADC-PCC Declares
World.content:
Says Tinubu’s refusal to campaign nationwide is arrogant, insult to Nigerians

Accuses Kwankwaso of doing president’s bidding, describes call for former VP to step down as reckless

Chuks Okocha

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has declared that its presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, is fit and ready to campaign across Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory ahead of the 2027 general election.

The council also criticised President Bola Tinubu over his decision not to campaign in all states, describing it as an act of arrogance and an insult to Nigerians, while accusing former Kano State Governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso of advancing the president’s political interests by calling on Atiku to step down for Peter Obi.

The Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Kola Ologbondiyan, in a statement, was quoted to have made the remarks while receiving a delegation of youths under the aegis of Young Voters for Atiku (YVA) and in a separate response to Kwankwaso’s interview on Channels Television.

Ologbondiyan argued that a president seeking re-election should be willing to engage voters directly, account for his stewardship and present his plans for the country. He said Tinubu’s reported reluctance to campaign nationwide would give the opposition an advantage.

“What President Tinubu has done is a clear act of contempt against the Nigerian people. The APC is known for its contempt for Nigerians. How can a man who wants to be re-elected as president, after failing woefully, say he does not want to visit the people he seeks to govern?” he said.

The ADC-PCC spokesman dismissed the argument that official engagements could prevent Tinubu from campaigning across the country, citing former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo, Goodluck Jonathan and Muhammadu Buhari, as well as former United States President Donald Trump and former Vice-President Kamala Harris, as examples of political leaders who campaigned while holding or seeking public office.

He alleged that Tinubu was reluctant to face voters because of public dissatisfaction over hunger, poverty, insecurity and the state of the economy.

Ologbondiyan maintained that Atiku was physically fit, mentally alert and prepared to visit every state and the FCT to present his manifesto and seek the electorate’s mandate.

He urged Nigerians, particularly young voters, to reject the All Progressives Congress (APC) in 2027, arguing that another term for the ruling party would prolong the hardship citizens were experiencing.

He also expressed confidence that Atiku, if elected, would prioritise economic recovery, wealth creation, national security and improved living standards.

The ADC-PCC further criticised Kwankwaso for urging Atiku to step down for Obi, describing the call as reckless, self-serving and an attempt to weaken the opposition ahead of the 2027 election.

Ologbondiyan questioned why Kwankwaso was focusing on opposition leaders rather than challenging Tinubu’s administration, which the council said Nigerians were eager to vote out.

“Rather than campaigning against President Tinubu, whose administration Nigerians are eagerly working to vote out, Kwankwaso is fixated on Atiku Abubakar, the ADC candidate, whom millions of Nigerians believe can restore economic stability and make life affordable again,” he said.

He alleged that Kwankwaso’s position raised questions about his political intentions, suggesting that his actions could benefit the ruling APC by creating divisions among opposition parties.

“What Kwankwaso is doing amounts to advancing President Tinubu’s interests. It is a familiar APC strategy to use willing collaborators within the opposition to create confusion, sow division and weaken the collective efforts to bring about political change,” Ologbondiyan said.

He also argued that Kwankwaso’s political influence in Kano should not be considered indispensable to any presidential candidate seeking victory in the state. Citing the 2003 and 2007 presidential elections, he said former President Muhammadu Buhari had secured victories in Kano without Kwankwaso’s support, adding that Atiku could also win the state in 2027.

Ologbondiyan further questioned Kwankwaso’s ability to translate his regional influence into nationwide electoral support, citing his fourth-place finish in the 2023 presidential election.

He also alleged that Kwankwaso’s call for Obi’s candidacy was driven partly by personal political ambition and possible calculations ahead of the 2031 election.

The ADC-PCC director maintained that Atiku had built political relationships across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones over more than three decades, which he said positioned the former vice-president to assemble a broad national coalition.

He urged Kwankwaso and other opposition figures to support Atiku, arguing that opposition leaders should prioritise defeating the APC rather than undermining one another.

“The task before opposition leaders is not to undermine one another for personal political advantage but to unite around the urgent national mission of rescuing Nigeria,” Ologbondiyan said.

The council also claimed that it had been politically strengthened by the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, saying the event had not attracted endorsements from ADC members or sympathisers.

World.title: 2027: N32trn FAAC Windfall in 41 Months Puts Governors Under Spotlight
World.content:
· CSOs demand evidence of improved healthcare, education, jobs, infrastructure

· Seek greater transparency

Nume Ekeghe and Sunday Ehigiator

As the 2027 general election approaches, the performance of state governors is coming under renewed scrutiny, with states and local governments receiving a combined N31.77 trillion from the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) between June 2023 and October 2026, according to data compiled by THISDAY.

This is as Governors have been challenged to account for increased FAAC revenues by demonstrating measurable improvements in healthcare, education, infrastructure, employment and poverty reduction, amid concerns that rising public revenues have yet to translate into better living conditions for many Nigerians

The massive inflows have raised questions about how effectively the funds have translated into better infrastructure, improved public services and tangible improvements in the lives of Nigerians, particularly at the grassroots, where local governments are expected to play a critical role in development.

Despite the Supreme Court’s landmark judgment of July 11, 2024, affirming financial autonomy for local governments, many state governors have continued to wield considerable influence over funds allocated to local government areas (LGs), raising concerns about whether the ruling has delivered the intended independence.

Under the existing revenue-sharing formula, the federal government receives 52.68 per cent of distributable revenue, state governments get 26.72 per cent, while LGs receive 20.60 per cent. However, the administration of LG allocations remain a contentious issue, with questions persisting over the extent to which councils exercise effective control over their funds.

FAAC allocations to states and local governments have risen substantially since the removal of the petrol subsidy, which increased the revenue available for distribution among the three tiers of government.

THISDAY’s analysis showed that states and local governments received a combined N3.861 trillion between June and December 2023. While the 36 states received a total of N2.223 trillion in the seven-month period, LGs got N1.637 trillion. Also, in 2024, both tiers of government got N7.870 trillion, with States receiving N4.594 trillion and the LGs N3.276 trillion.

Furthermore, in 2025 both tiers of government got N10.419 trillion, in which N5.988 trillion went to the states and N4.430 trillion to the LGs. Also, in the first nine months of 2026, they received N9.618 trillion, with the States receiving a total of N5.56 trillion and the LGs N4.056 trillion. This brings the total for both tiers of government since President Bola Tinubu announced the removal of petrol subsidy to N31.77 trillion.

The September 2026 revenue which was shared by FAAC this week, further underscored the scale of the revenue windfall. A total of N2.428 trillion from the Federation Account was distributed among the three tiers of government in October 2026, representing an increase of N90 billion from the N2.338 trillion shared in September.

Of the amount, the federal government received N832.242 billion, the 36 state governments received N799.87 billion, while local governments received N560.66 billion.

Leading the call for accountability on the increased allocations actions, the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre (CISLAC) and the Rule of Law and Accountability Advocacy Centre (RULAAC) urged citizens, civil society organisations (CSOs) and the media to intensify scrutiny of state finances and government performance.
