CISLAC, through its Executive Director, Auwal Ibrahim Musa (Rafsanjani), expressed concern over what it described as a widening gap between increased FAAC revenues accruing to state governments and persistent poverty, unemployment, infrastructure decay and economic hardship.

“Governors cannot continue celebrating record allocations while citizens struggle with failing hospitals, deteriorating schools, unemployment, poor roads and inadequate basic services,” the organisation stated.

“The question is no longer how much states receive, but what governments have delivered with the money.”

CISLAC argued that governors should be assessed on measurable improvements in citizens’ welfare rather than political publicity, budget announcements or ceremonial project commissioning.

It identified key indicators for evaluating state performance to include the functionality of primary healthcare centres, availability of medicines and medical personnel, school enrolment and learning outcomes, completed and usable roads, access to clean water, sustainable job creation and poverty reduction.

According to CISLAC, “Development is not measured by the size of government allocations, but by the quality of life of the people.”

It called on state governments to publish accessible monthly revenue reports, quarterly budget implementation records, contract details and independently audited financial statements to enable citizens to track public funds from allocation to actual service delivery.

It urged CSOs, investigative journalists, professional associations and community-based groups to verify projects on the ground, expose abandoned or inflated contracts and compare official expenditure claims with actual conditions in communities.

It also called on State Houses of Assembly to exercise independent oversight, while urging Auditors-General, procurement authorities and anti-corruption agencies to investigate credible allegations of misappropriation, inflated contracts and diversion of public funds.

On the political implications of the increased allocations, CISLAC challenged governors to publish comprehensive, independently verifiable records of revenues received and development outcomes achieved during their tenures.

Similarly, the Executive Director of RULAAC, Okechukwu Nwanguma, said increased FAAC allocations had given state governments greater fiscal capacity, but warned that higher revenue did not automatically translate into development.

“Nigerians should judge governors by measurable outcomes, not by announcements, groundbreaking ceremonies or the number of contracts awarded,” he said.

Nwanguma said citizens should examine each state’s FAAC receipts alongside internally generated revenue, debt profile, recurrent expenditure and actual capital-budget implementation.

“The relevant question is: after salaries, debt servicing and administrative costs, how much was invested in projects and services that directly improved people’s lives?” he asked.

He identified education completion rates, the number of out-of-school children, healthcare access, maternal and infant mortality, youth unemployment, household incomes, food security, road quality, access to potable water and capital project completion rates as essential indicators for assessing governors.

Nwanguma also stressed the importance of comparing these indicators with conditions before the revenue increases, using per-capita spending and adjustments for inflation to establish whether citizens had experienced genuine improvements.

He urged CSOs to obtain and simplify state budgets, monthly FAAC receipts, procurement records, quarterly implementation reports and audited accounts, converting the information into accessible scorecards showing what governments received, budgeted, spent and delivered.

He added that communities should document abandoned or substandard projects, interview beneficiaries and use public hearings, town halls, radio programmes and partnerships with journalists to demand explanations from public officials.

Ahead of the elections, Nwanguma said, CSOs and the media should publish non-partisan performance scorecards based on verifiable evidence.

World.title: Kwankwasiyya, NNPP Petition INEC Over Kano, Oyo Guber Candidates’ Exclusion
World.content:
Protest hits Kano as aggrieved supporters challenge omissions

Tinubu reappoints Bila, nominates five new INEC commissioners

Alex Enumah, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano,

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is facing mounting pressure over the exclusion of some candidates from its final list for the 2027 elections, with the Kwankwasiyya Movement and the New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) petitioning the commission over omissions in Kano and Oyo states, respectively, while a Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) aspirant in Ogun State has threatened legal action.

The development comes as President Bola Tinubu yesterday nominated five new officials to the electoral body and reappointed its National Commissioner representing the North-east, Dr Bala Bila, amid preparations for the forthcoming general election. The president nominated four national commissioners and two resident electoral commissioners, with the Senate expected to scrutinise the nominees.

In Kano, hundreds of supporters of the Kwankwasiyya Movement stormed the state office of INEC to protest the omission of their governorship candidate from the final list.

The protesters, led by the deputy governorship candidate, Mustapha Kwankwaso, on behalf of Aminu Gwarzo, submitted a formal petition demanding the reinstatement of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate.

Responding, the Kano State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Abdu Zango, said the commission had received the complaint and would give it due attention.

“Basically, what they came to do is to present a complaint about the omission of their candidates. INEC has made the point very clear, the reason for the omission and the fact that there is a window of appeal that has been provided up to the 24th of October,” Zango said.

He added that the petition would be forwarded to the commission’s national headquarters for consideration, commending the protesters for presenting their grievances peacefully.

Zango said INEC in Kano remained neutral and urged residents to continue collecting their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), noting that collection would soon be extended to Registration Areas to improve accessibility.

The spokesperson for the Kwankwasiyya Movement, Dr Habib Mohammed, said the protest was not only to demand the reinstatement of the candidates but also to petition against an INEC staff member allegedly involved in the substitution of some candidates.

“We are also petitioning against a staff here, whom we believe colluded with some unauthorised people to hide a decision which led to substitution of some of our candidates,” Mohammed said.

He alleged that letters bearing suspected forged signatures had been submitted to INEC, resulting in the substitution of the candidates. He called for an investigation into the staff member’s alleged role, adding that the Resident Electoral Commissioner had assured the delegation that the petition would be escalated to the national headquarters.

Oyo NNPP Candidate Petitions INEC Chairman

In Oyo State, the governorship candidate of the NNPP, Adebiyi Adedapo, petitioned the INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, over the omission of his name from the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 election.

In an open letter dated October 15, Adedapo urged the commission to investigate the omission and take corrective action in accordance with the law.

He said he emerged as the party’s duly nominated candidate following a consensus primary conducted under the supervision of its National Secretary, Oginni Sunday, in accordance with the party’s constitution and electoral guidelines.

According to him, the NNPP submitted his candidature to INEC, while his EC9 form was displayed at the commission’s Oyo State office, giving him reason to expect that his name would appear on the final list.

Adedapo said he had never withdrawn from the race and had neither submitted nor authorised anyone to submit a withdrawal letter on his behalf.

“I have never withdrawn my candidature from the Oyo State governorship election. I have neither submitted nor authorised the submission of any letter of withdrawal to INEC, the NNPP, or any person or institution acting on my behalf,” he said.

He called on INEC to disclose any document purporting to show that he had withdrawn, including its source and date of receipt, and to investigate any unauthorised withdrawal or substitution.

The candidate also urged the commission to verify his nomination records, provide a written explanation for the omission, preserve all relevant documents and apply any lawful remedies required to ensure that his name appears on the ballot.

He said he was prepared to provide evidence of his nomination, primary results, submitted particulars and party correspondence to assist the investigation.

Tinubu Reappoints Bila, Nominates Five New INEC Officials

Meanwhile, President Tinubu has nominated four new national commissioners and two resident electoral commissioners to fill vacancies at INEC arising from expiring tenures, while reappointing Bila as the National Commissioner representing the North-east.

Presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga disclosed the nominations in a statement on Friday, saying the nominees would be scrutinised by the Senate.

The new national commissioner nominees are Professor Mustapha Aliu, who is to replace Professor Abdullahi Zuru as the North-west representative, and Bashir Muhammed Umar, who is to replace Professor Muhammad Adamu as the North-central representative.

The president also nominated Mrs Oluwatoyin Babalola, the resident electoral commissioner in Osun State, as the South-west national commissioner to replace Professor Cornelius Ajayi, whose tenure expires on October 24, 2026.

The two nominees for resident electoral commissioner positions are retired permanent secretary Dr Samuel Akinjide Akinleye, representing Ekiti State, and Zahradden Basiru Sanusi, from Jigawa State, who is to replace Professor Saidu Ahmed Babura.

Tinubu urged the Senate to expedite confirmation of the nominees in view of the forthcoming general election scheduled for 2027.

Ogun PDP Aspirant Threatens Legal Action

In Ogun State, governorship aspirant Olusegun Peter Topa gave INEC 48 hours to publish his name as the PDP’s duly nominated candidate for the February 2027 governorship election or face possible legal action.

In a letter dated October 14 and addressed to the INEC chairman through his lawyer, Anderson Asemota of Neplus Ultra Attorneys, Topa argued that he had fulfilled the requirements for nomination and should be included in the final list.

He said he obtained the party’s Expression of Interest and nomination forms on May 12, 2026, and participated in its governorship primary conducted on May 27, 2026.

INEC published its final list of governorship candidates on October 10 but excluded the PDP from the race in Ogun State.

Topa’s lawyer maintained that his client’s name appeared as entry number 15783 on the PDP membership register submitted to INEC in compliance with Section 77 of the Electoral Act, 2026.

He argued that the commission had a statutory obligation to publish the particulars of duly nominated candidates, subject to applicable laws and any binding court decisions.

The lawyer urged INEC to verify Topa’s membership status, examine the party’s primary and nomination records, establish the basis for the exclusion and provide a written explanation.

He further asked the commission to publish a supplementary or amended list containing Topa’s name if its records confirmed his nomination and no lawful basis existed for excluding him.

Asemota warned that his client had instructed his lawyers to consider instituting proceedings before a competent court if INEC failed to provide a substantive response within 48 hours or the omission persisted without a lawful explanation.

World.title: With New Credit Rating Agency, Africa Pushes for Fairer Risk Assessment, Lower Borrowing Costs
World.content:
• Continent pays more to borrow, says WAIFEM DG

• Experts demand transparent ratings, stronger data, joint ownership of debt analysis

• IMF warns rising debt service crowding out development spending

• W’Bank mobilises $112bn in private capital, says 59m Africans gain electricity access

Nume Ekeghe in Bangkok, Thailand

African policymakers and financial experts have called for a fairer assessment of the continent’s economies, stronger debt management capacity and greater transparency in credit rating methodologies, warning that persistent risk premiums continue to raise borrowing costs and constrain development financing.

The call comes as Africa seeks to strengthen its voice in global credit assessments following the launch of the Africa Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA) in Mauritius this month, against the backdrop of mounting debt pressures, a projected global shortfall of 800 million jobs and growing demands for infrastructure and social investment.

Also yesterday, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) warned that rising debt-service burdens were squeezing development spending, while the World Bank Group highlighted the challenge of creating jobs for a rapidly growing global workforce, with a projected shortfall of 800 million jobs over the next 10 to 15 years.

Speaking at the 2026 IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned that high and rising interest burdens, particularly in low-income countries, were leaving governments with less room to finance development.

On his part, World Bank Group President Ajay Banga, stressed the need to mobilise private capital, expand infrastructure and create jobs, disclosing that the institution mobilised $112 billion in private capital last year.

The new continental credit rating agency is expected to complement existing international credit rating agencies by incorporating more African data, expertise and perspectives into assessments of the continent’s economies. However, stakeholders say its success will depend on its independence, credible methodologies, reliable economic data and acceptance by investors.

Speaking at a panel discussion on ‘The Debt Sustainability Framework, Credit Ratings and Africa’s Risk Premium,’ held on the sidelines of the IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, the Director-General of the West African Institute for Financial and Economic Management (WAIFEM), Dr. Baba Musa, said African countries had spent decades calling for their economic realities to be assessed accurately and proportionately.

He said African countries pay more to borrow than comparable economies in other regions, arguing that prevailing perceptions and external interpretations of the continent’s economic realities often placed it at a disadvantage.

“For a rating agency, the methodology should be comparable with international standards. However, what African countries have been asking for over the past 20 years is that they should be assessed accurately, their risks communicated proportionately, and their economies evaluated fairly,” Musa said.

He stressed that the demand for fairer assessments was not a call for preferential treatment or lower standards, but for methodologies that adequately reflected the diversity, resources and economic circumstances of African countries.

“Africa’s voice should be heard and the continent should be assessed fairly, just like any other region,” he said, adding that AfCRA’s success would depend on transparency, credible methodologies and its ability to capture the actual realities of African economies.

The cost of Africa’s risk premium remains substantial. The Deputy Executive Secretary and Chief Economist of the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (ECA), Dr. Hanan Morsy, estimated that persistent risk premiums cost the continent approximately $75 billion annually in excess interest payments.

The additional borrowing costs come at a time when governments face mounting pressure to finance development, improve living standards and create jobs for rapidly growing populations.

Morsy said African countries must also take greater responsibility for presenting evidence-based accounts of their economies rather than relying on others to make their case.

“If you do not advocate for yourself, no one will. This applies to individuals as well as countries. You must make your case and ensure that it is not based on words alone but backed by evidence,” she said.

She emphasised the need for reliable data to limit the room for discretion in credit assessments, warning that countries must be prepared to provide the evidence needed to support their economic outlooks.

Morsy added that international institutions had helped countries without previous credit ratings obtain them and subsequently improve their ratings, while also supporting countries seeking investment-grade status.

The launch of AfCRA is expected to broaden the information available to investors and provide additional perspectives on African economies, reform programmes and growth prospects. However, stakeholders have cautioned that the agency’s establishment alone will not automatically reduce borrowing costs without stronger economic fundamentals and institutional credibility.

Beyond credit ratings, African policymakers called for reforms to debt sustainability assessments to ensure that the models and assumptions used by international financial institutions adequately reflect national economic conditions.

Musa welcomed aspects of the revised Debt Sustainability Framework (DSF), noting that distinguishing between external debt distress, overall public debt distress and actual debt unsustainability represented progress in assessing African countries’ debt positions.

He explained that countries experiencing liquidity pressures should not necessarily be assessed in the same way as those facing solvency problems. Indicators such as gross financing needs relative to gross domestic product and government revenue, he said, could provide a more nuanced picture of countries’ debt positions.

However, he called for African governments to have a greater role in debt sustainability assessments, arguing that countries should jointly determine the assumptions and projections used to evaluate their debt positions.

Musa warned against situations in which the IMF and World Bank relied on their own projections while African governments maintained different estimates of their economic outlooks.

Former Finance Minister of Niger Republic, Hon. Ahmat Jidoud, said the revision of the DSF should not mark the end of efforts to improve debt assessment across the continent.

He called on the IMF and World Bank to engage more closely with African countries, explain the models and assumptions underpinning the framework, and provide training to officials in finance ministries and other relevant institutions.

Jidoud also raised concerns about the treatment of domestic debt under the revised framework, particularly its implications for regional economic communities such as the West African Economic and Monetary Union and the Central African Economic and Monetary Community.

For the Chief Executive Officer of the African Legal Support Facility (ALSF), Dr. Olivier Pognon, stronger coordination and knowledge-sharing among African institutions are essential to improving the continent’s engagement with credit rating agencies and strengthening debt management.

Pognon said the ALSF was developing a capacity-building platform expected to be launched in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, at the end of November. The initiative would support debt management offices and officials involved in public borrowing and major project negotiations.

IMF Warns Debt Burdens Squeezing Development

The debate over Africa’s borrowing costs comes as the IMF warns that rising public debt and interest payments are limiting governments’ ability to finance development and respond to economic shocks.

Speaking at the Annual Meetings Plenary, Georgieva, said low-income countries faced particularly difficult conditions, with high and rising interest burdens compounded by declining official aid.

“Too many countries carry too much debt,” she said, warning that debt-service obligations were crowding out development spending.

Georgieva said governments could not rely on economic growth alone to reverse rising debt trajectories quickly enough and called for credible medium-term fiscal plans to restore stability.

“The inescapable bottom line is that preserving stability requires fiscal consolidation in most high-debt countries,” she said.

However, she cautioned that fiscal adjustments must protect vulnerable households, limit the cost to future growth and be complemented by structural reforms that improve productivity.

World Bank mobilises $112bn in private capital

Banga, meanwhile, highlighted the need to mobilise private capital, expand infrastructure and create jobs for a rapidly growing young population.

He said 1.2 billion young people were expected to enter the labour market over the next 10 to 15 years, while the global economy was projected to generate only about 400 million jobs, leaving a potential shortfall of 800 million.

“The jobs gap is a projection. It does not have to be our future,” Banga said.

He argued that closing the gap would require countries to make better use of scarce resources by combining public finance, private investment, philanthropy and technology to support development.

Banga disclosed that the World Bank Group mobilised $112 billion in private capital last year, compared with approximately $35 billion in financial year 2022. Total financing, including the institution’s own resources, exceeded $230 billion.

However, he acknowledged that attracting commercial investment remained difficult in low-income countries, where private capital mobilisation stood at roughly $3 billion.

He said the World Bank was seeking to expand financing for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises by improving access to finance, connecting smaller businesses to larger markets and simplifying regulations that constrain growth.

Banga also identified infrastructure, human capital and regulatory certainty as essential foundations for job creation, noting that businesses needed reliable electricity, water, transport and digital connections, while workers required education, healthcare and relevant skills.

On electricity access, he said the World Bank Group and the African Development Bank were working to provide electricity to 300 million people across Africa by 2030 under Mission 300.

So far, 59 million people have gained access, with the pace accelerating from 12 million in financial year 2024 to 18 million in financial year 2025 and 28 million in the latest financial year.

“But access is only part of the challenge. Homes, mines, factories, farms, and growing cities need reliable, affordable baseload power,” he said.

Stakeholders also stressed the need for responsible fiscal policies, stronger domestic resource mobilisation, improved debt management and greater coordination between African governments and international financial institutions.

World.title: Tinubu Welcomes W’Bank’s $5.79bn Plan, Dangles $78.5bn Projects Before Investors
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja



President Bola Tinubu yesterday welcomed World Bank Group’s proposed plan to mobilise about $5.79 billion in private financing for Nigeria.

He has also taken steps to attract domestic and foreign investors to Nigeria, unveiling a pipeline of 65 bankable projects seeking $78.5 billion in investment.

According to Tinubu, the investment move was aimed at strengthening the foundation for economic growth, expanding businesses and creating jobs, with agriculture and digital infrastructure among the sectors expected to benefit from increased private capital.

Tinubu, in a post on his verified X handle, @officialABAT, extended invitation to Nigerian and international investors to explore the projects, assuring them that his administration would work to resolve obstacles and facilitate the execution of viable investments.

He wrote, “We undertook our economic reforms to build a stronger foundation for investment and give more Nigerians the opportunity to earn a better living.”



According to the President, the World Bank Group’s financing mobilisation initiative is a support for the government’s efforts to attract investment and expand economic opportunities.

“I welcome the World Bank Group’s work to mobilise up to $5.79 billion in private financing for Nigeria. This partnership supports our efforts to help businesses expand and attract investment into agriculture and digital infrastructure,” Tinubu said.

The $78.5 billion project pipeline was presented by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, alongside the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, Olayemi Cardoso, at the Nigeria Investors Forum, held on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

The President charged investors to examine the proposed projects and engage directly with their sponsors through Projects Nigeria, the Federal Government’s platform for showcasing investment opportunities.

“Our administration will work with you to resolve obstacles and move viable investments into execution, creating jobs and expanding opportunities for our people,” Tinubu stated.

His appeal came as the government seeks to attract private-sector financing to support economic development, with the government positioning the project pipeline as an avenue for investors to participate in key sectors of the Nigerian economy.

The initiative is expected to complement efforts to expand productive activities, support business growth and create employment opportunities through increased investment in viable projects.

The President directed the investors to access details of the 65 projects through the Projects Nigeria portal at finance.gov.ng/projectsnigeria.

World.title: Wike Slams Atiku, Amaechi, Labels Them Political Gamblers
World.content:
.Comment on Benue’s N25bn allocation, plot by Suswam and Benue governor sparks tension



Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja and George Okoh in Makurdi



The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Nyesom Wike, has doubled down on the candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in next year’s Presidential election, Atiku Abubakar and his joint-ticket flagbearer, Rotimi Amaechi, as political gamblers and ‘kalokalo’ people.

Also, Wike’s recent reference to Benue State’s reported N25 billion monthly federal allocation and alleged plot by former Benue State Governor, Gabriel Suswam and Benue Governor, Hyacinth Alia, to frustrate his Rainbow coalition has increased tensions in Benue State over the 2027 elections.



Wike, the national leader of Rainbow Coalition, delivered the jibe yesterday at a townhall meeting at Ayama in Abua/Odual Local Government Area of Rivers State, to shore up support for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.



He cautioned the people of Rivers State against surrendering their political future to the duo, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential candidate, Mr. Peter Obi,

saying those individuals lacked vision or proven developmental records.

The FCT minister, who emphasised that the Rainbow Coalition represented a broad alignment designed to secure a decisive victory in the upcoming 2027 general elections, maintained that leadership requires concrete action and foresight rather than perpetual political trial and error.

Addressing a crowded gathering of stakeholders, Wike warned against politicians who treat presidential contests like games of chance.

“Don’t trust your destiny to political gamblers. Don’t trust your destiny to ‘kalokalo’ people,” Wike warned the crowd of stakeholders of traditional leaders, party faithful and community leaders.

He described Atiku and Obi as individuals who kept contesting for the presidency every four years, hoping to recover what they lost, without any genuine vision for the country.

Wike said, “These people are political gamblers and you cannot give your destiny to “kalokalo” people; you cannot hand over your destiny to political gamblers.

“Give a destiny to somebody who we know, who has tried all this, and he has done it.”

Noting that repeated presidential runs without a clear governance plan offer no real solutions to Nigeria’s challenges.

Drawing comparisons to international political figures, Wike argued that while leaders like Abraham Lincoln ran multiple times driven by a clear national vision, “Atiku continues to run purely out of political habit and desire to recoup his investments.”

He also defended his record as Rivers State governor, reminding the people of Abua/Odual that project delivery—not political rhetoric—should dictate their electoral choices.

He challenged Amaechi to show his contributions to the local government area, pointing to his administration’s projects in the area.

He adulated President Tinubu’s administration for stabilising critical national sectors and restoring industrial harmony in tertiary institutions, calling on Abua-Odual residents to remain steadfast with the current administration heading into 2027.

He urged residents of Abua/Odual to vote Tinubu for President, Chinda for governor, Felix Obua for Rivers West Senatorial District, and Solomon Boss for Abua-Odual-Ahoada East Federal Constituency, all under the All Progressives Congress (APC).

Meanwhile, Wike on Thursday at the maiden Idoma Hall of Fame event held in Abuja, spoke as the guest of honour.

His words have triggered a debate over the possibilities of APC chances to win the governorship and state elections in Benue State.

Wike backs the rainbow coalition candidates in Benue State, which has former Minister of Justice, Chief Mike Aondakaa, as governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the 2027 election.

He serves as FCT Minister under President Tinubu’s APC-led administration despite being a PDP member.

Within the PDP, Wike has continued to push for control and reorganisation of the party’s state and local structures.

For the APC, Wike’s activities may not be an immediate threat given his open support for the Tinubu administration. However, the scope of his influence in states like Benue ahead of 2027 remains a subject of political interest.

Former Benue State Governor, Samuel Ortom and members of the group known as the Rainbow Coalition/Strategic Alliance for Tinubu, have been in political consultations linked to Wike.

Ortom was a key member of the G-5 governors who opposed PDP presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar in 2023, a group in which Wike played a leading role.

If these consultations develop into a formal political alliance, it could reshape the contest for influence in Benue.

With 2027 approaching, speculation is growing that Wike may attempt to influence candidate selection and political alignments within the Benue PDP. Any such move by external actors is likely to become a major talking point in the state, as parties begin early positioning.

On the other hand, Governor Alia’s camp is focusing on his administration’s performance over the last three years, pointing to efforts in governance, infrastructure and service delivery as the basis for seeking a second term.

Supporters of the governor argue that Benue voters should decide the 2027 election based on performance on the ground, not on political deals struck outside the state.

As realignments intensify, the key question is whether behind-the-scenes negotiations will redefine Benue’s political landscape, or whether Governor Alia’s record will be decisive at the polls.

To give credence to Wike’s move, the Benue State Chairman of the APC, Augustine Agada, said recently that his faction of the APC had recognised and are working with Wike under the rainbow coalition and strategic alignment.

He said the coalition is working for the re-election of President Tinubu. He said the President directed that the party should return all its candidates in the 2023 election but the governor allegedly rejected the directive.

“Tinubu directed that the party should return all its candidates in the 2023 election but the governor refused to do so and orchestrated some members of the party to take the party to court.”

He added that the party is not in support of the governor and will not be working for his re-election.

World.title: JCI Ikeja Screens Over 2,000 Residents for Diseases, Offers Free Medicines
World.content:
Bennett Oghifo

The Junior Chamber International (JCI), Ikeja, has provided free health screening and medical services to more than 2,000 residents as part of its annual community health intervention.

The exercise tagged, ‘Commit to Quality Health’, held last Saturday and covered screening for blood pressure, blood sugar, malaria, tuberculosis (TB), HIV and hepatitis B, alongside dental and oral health checks and distribution of free drugs.

Speaking at the event, President of JCI Ikeja, Olubunmi Fadare, said the initiative was part of the organisation’s yearly programme aimed at taking healthcare education and basic medical services to communities.

Fadare said the programme was designed to encourage residents to take their health seriously and seek medical attention when necessary.

She said the latest exercise was the second phase of the programme organised by JCI Ikeja this year, following the first phase held to commemorate World Health Day, which reached more than 500 people.

According to her, the second phase was supported by the Crocodile Foundation through a grant secured for the project, allowing the organisation to expand its reach to more than 2,000 beneficiaries.

“This year is quite different because this is phase two of Community Quality Health. The first phase was to commemorate World Health Day, and this one, we are attending to a larger number of people,” she said.

Fadare said more than 30 medical personnel attended to beneficiaries during the exercise, with dedicated sections for tuberculosis, dental and other medical services.

She commended the Ikeja Local Government for partnering with JCI and providing the venue for the exercise, noting that such collaboration made it easier for residents to access the services.

Fadare also urged residents not to disregard free healthcare services, stressing that the fact that the services were provided at no cost did not mean they were inferior.

She said JCI had conducted a community rally across different wards ahead of the exercise to sensitise residents and encourage them to participate.

On Nigeria’s healthcare system, Fadare called for greater investment in public healthcare infrastructure and more functional medical centres with adequate doctors and other healthcare professionals.

She said expanding access to public healthcare would help reduce the challenges faced by residents seeking medical attention.

Also speaking, Executive Vice President (Southwest), JCI Nigeria, Idara Michael, said the organisation would assess the impact of the intervention after the exercise.

Michael said JCI would collect feedback from beneficiaries, analyse the outcome and identify areas that required improvement.

She noted that the community health programme had been running since 2017, adding that the organisation had continued to improve its approach based on feedback from previous editions.

“We are getting better. Standard is still the same, but efficiency and improvements, we keep getting better,” she said.

Michael said JCI would return to the community after the exercise to assess its sustainability and impact, stressing that the organisation did not simply implement projects and leave the beneficiaries.

She also called for stronger collaboration between JCI and government at the local, state and national levels.

According to her, JCI was non-political and non-partisan, but would continue to work with government and other stakeholders to influence policies and promote community development.

The Executive Chairman of Ikeja Local Government, Akeem Olalekan Dauda, who attended the programme alongside members of his cabinet, said the partnership between the council and JCI was not a one-off initiative, noting that both organisations had previously collaborated on healthcare awareness and intervention programmes within the community.

The chairman, however, expressed concern over the low turnout of children for the medical exercise.

He urged parents and guardians to take advantage of healthcare opportunities provided by the council to monitor the health and wellbeing of their children.

Dauda also commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for the autonomy granted to local governments, saying the development had strengthened the capacity of councils to deliver social services and respond more effectively to the needs of their communities.

World.title: NSIB Probes Mid-air Door Separation on Private Jet After Emergency Landing in Abuja
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) yesterday commenced an investigation into an incident involving a Challenger 604 aircraft, registration number T7-SEI, operated by Triton.

The aircraft departed Abuja for Lagos at 1612 UTC. At three nautical miles, while passing 3,500 feet, the crew declared a mayday after the aircraft’s door separated mid-air.

In a statement, the Director General and Chief Executive Officer of the NSIB, Captain Alex Badeh Jr., said the aircraft returned to Abuja and landed safely on Runway 22 at 1634 UTC, with nine people on board, comprising three crew members and six passengers.

The NSIB said the door had been recovered and secured at its wreckage hangar. The Bureau has commenced investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

It added that further updates would be provided as the investigation progresses.

According to a report on the incident, Abuja Tower established contact with the aircraft, identified as DWC052, at 1629 UTC. The crew asked the tower whether it could see that the aircraft’s door was missing.

The duty air traffic controller (DATCO) used binoculars to observe the aircraft but could not confirm the door’s status because of the aircraft’s position. The crew was subsequently advised accordingly.

At 1634 UTC, DWC052 landed safely on Runway 22. Upon landing, the aircraft’s fuselage was clearly visible to the DATCO, who observed that the door was missing.

The aircraft was then taxied to the international apron extension. At 1640 UTC, DWC052 reported that the marshaller was in sight and was subsequently guided to its parking position.

World.title: KZN school bans parents from delivering elaborate Matric gifts
World.content:
A KwaZulu-Natal school has banned parents from delivering elaborate gifts to their children on school premises. Ndukwenhle High School in Umlazi has voiced its concerns for others who cannot afford the grand gestures.

KZN SCHOOLS BAN ELABORATE MATRIC GIFTS

In a Facebook post, Ndukwenhle High School in Umlazi issued a directive to parents not to deliver matric gift hampers to their children on school premises.

The school shared: “This is because other parents do not have the means to afford such gifts for their children. We kindly ask for your understanding and support in this matter.



It added: “Let us promote equality and fairness among all our learners”.

In the comments section, the school defended its stance by adding, “Parents who can afford to do so are encouraged to gift their children. However, NO gifting will be allowed on the school premises”

The school received a positive response from the public.

Lelo Moumakwe commented: “Big up to the school 👏 by all means buy the gifts but have them delivered at home”. Emeldah Charl added: “Much respect to the school”.

Some even called for the school to impose strict regulations on Matric Dance events.

WHEN DO EXAMS BEGIN AND END?

According to the National Senior Certificate (NSC) examination timetable, matric exams began on Tuesday, 13 October, and will end on Thursday, 26 November 2026.



Results are expected to be released on an unconfirmed date in January 2027.

World.title: Bernard Parker’s wife stakes claim amid ‘baby mama’ drama?
World.content:
Weny Parker, the wife of Bernard Parker, has given the strongest hint that her marriage is still alive and thriving amid public scrutiny of his personal life.

The former Bafana Bafana and Kaizer Chiefs player has trended on social media after he posted a statement about splitting from his alleged baby mama, Kacha Stepanovic.

The 40-year-old claimed to have been in a three-year relationship with the red-haired woman. He has since denied posting the statement.



BERNARD PARKER’S WIFE WENDY SHOWS SUPPORT AMID MEDIA STORM

On her social media accounts, Wendy Parker changed her profile picture from one of herself to one with her husband, Bernard Parker.

On Facebook, she liked comments from followers – who responded to the apparent show of support – that read:

“I’m so happy to see this”

“My fav couple. May God bless you more, guys”

“This is what we know and love”

Wendy also liked another comment, seemingly calling Bernard’s baby mama “delulu”



Wendy last posted a picture with Bernard in March 2024. A few months earlier, she posted a picture with her spouse with the caption: “Me and you till the end of time”.

The couple met in the late 2000s and married in 2012. They have two sons, Skye and Storm.

BABY MAMA BRINGS THE DRAMA?

Meanwhile, Bernard Parker’s baby mama, Kacha Stepanovic, who claims he is the father of her baby girl, has made her own cryptic statement on social media

The businesswoman posted on her IG Storis: “Therapy is not enough. He needs to know people congratulated me when we broke up”.

Kacha has two older sons from her marriage to Ntukza, or Bantu Hanabe, who was a member of the hip-hop group Teargas.

World.title: Trevor Noah shades white refugees: ‘Sell their businesses, mansions…’
World.content:
Trevor Noah shared his views on the refugee resettlement programme. Images via IG.

Trevor Noah has shared his views on white South Africans who have taken up refugee status in the US under the resettlement programme.

The South African comedian commented on the controversial programme during his guest appearance at The Connecticut Forum’s 35th anniversary this week.

To date, almost 17 000 mainly Afrikaner South Africans have resettled in the US after claiming racial “persecution” in South Africa.



TREVOR NOAH ON WHITE REFUGEES

During his appearance at The Connecticut Forum, Trevor Noah was asked to share his views about the US’s refugee resettlement programme to South African racial minorities, particularly Afrikaner white people.

Speaking to US journalist Michele Norris, the Soweto-born comedian commented that the US administration, under President Donald Trump, had prioritised “rescuing” white South Africans, who claimed to face extreme violence and “genocide”.

The 42-year-old cheekily responded, “Most white South Africans are having a great time here…Many of these refugees had to sell their businesses, their farms and their mansions so that they could be ‘rescued’.

“When I saw those people, what I remember thinking was: I have seen refugees with baggage, never with luggage. It was very

Trevor Noah went on to highlight the wage gap and wealth distribution among South Africa’s racial groups. He implied that the US government had a hidden agenda in assisting South Africans.

He continued: “What’s interesting to me is how consistently the United States government has first had a concern with the oppressors, but not the oppressed. 

“Yes, crime is terrible. But you know who is being killed more than white South Africans? Black South Africans. It’s a crime linked to poverty.

“The adverse effects that any nation faces will be disproportionately felt by the people who are the poorest and most oppressed”.

HOW MANY SOUTH AFRICANS HAVE RESETTLED IN THE US?

According to the latest data released by US authorities, over 12 000 South Africans have resettled in the US as refugees in the past fiscal year.

The figure is the sum of successful applicants between October 2025 and the end of August 2026

The states receiving the biggest groups of arrivals include Florida, California, Colorado, Illinois and Iowa.

In May 2026, US President Trump issued an emergency determination increasing the refugee intake for the fiscal year to 17,500. Applicants are required to pass the relevant screening, security and medical processes and be approved for admission.

World.title: Full list of eThekwini beaches and swimming pools that are open
World.content:
Beautiful view of Umhlanga Beach in South Africa, featuring the iconic lighthouse and seaside buildings. Image: Pexels

The eThekwini Municipality has given swimmers the go-ahead at 21 beaches and opened 41 public swimming pools across Durban and surrounding areas, according to its latest status update dated 8 October.

However, the city has closed two beaches for swimming after water quality tests returned high E. coli readings.

The municipality said it updates the list whenever the status of a beach or pool changes, so beachgoers should check the latest information before heading out.



Where you can swim in Durban

Lifeguarded beaches open for swimming from 6:00 to 18:30 daily include:

Central: Wedge, Point, uShaka, Addington, South Beach, North Beach, Bay of Plenty, Battery Beach and Country Club

Wedge, Point, uShaka, Addington, South Beach, North Beach, Bay of Plenty, Battery Beach and Country Club North: Westbrook, Umdloti Main, Bronze Beach and Umhlanga Main

Westbrook, Umdloti Main, Bronze Beach and Umhlanga Main South: Toti Main, Ansteys, Brighton, Umgababa, Doonside, Winklespruit, Pipeline and Reunion

Most of these beaches recorded excellent water quality in tests conducted between 5 and 8 October. Point, uShaka, Bay of Plenty, Westbrook, Umdloti Main, Toti Main and Pipeline all came in with E. coli counts below 10, well under the excellent threshold of 130.

Country Club recorded a count of 345, which still falls within the acceptable range of 130 to 500.

Why two beaches remain closed

The municipality closed Thekwini Beach and Laguna Beach to swimming after both recorded counts well above the 500 limit indicating poor water quality.

The city stressed that visitors can still enjoy other recreational activities at closed beaches, such as walking, picnicking and fishing. Swimming, however, is not allowed until the water quality improves.

The municipality also urged beachgoers to keep the coastline clean by using bins for litter.



Public swimming pools open across eThekwini

The city has opened 41 public pools, operating from 6:00 to 18:00 on weekdays and from 9:00 to 17:00 on Sundays and public holidays. They are:

Hambanathi, Belvedere, Buffelsdale, Verulam, Stanmore, Rainham, Ntuzuma E, KwaMashu G, KwaMashu D, Durban North, Umgababa, Pipeline, Tiger Rocks, Umlazi D, Umlazi G, Isiphingo Hills, Anstey’s Beach paddling pool, Brighton Beach paddling pool, Laguna paddling pool, Austerville, Merewent, Tessoriere, Tills Crescent, Lamontville, Alex Bulley, Croftdene, Bayview, Arena Park, Bellair, Westville, Clermont, Marianridge, Nagina, Chesterville, Children’s Amusement Centre, South Beach, Rachel Finlayson, Sutton Park, Rochdale, Illovu and Balkumar Singh.

World.title: Beach plans this Saturday? Here’s when the tides will turn
World.content:
Check Saturday’s high and low tide times before planning your activities along South Africa’s coastline. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Saturday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Spring tides can cause greater changes in water levels along South Africa’s coastline.

However, tides are only part of the picture. Wind, waves and swell and the shape of the seabed can also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.



When to expect the next spring tide at the coast

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual, changing conditions along the coast.

The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing.



High tides may cover rocks and reefs, while low tides reveal more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Bernard Parker backtracks on split, infidelity claims amid club exit
World.content:
Bernard Parker backtracks on statement on his personal life. Images via Facebook

Days after dropping a bombshell about his personal life, including a confession alluding to cheating on his new baby mama, Bernard Parker has backtracked, calling for “privacy” and “discretion”

This comes as the former Bafana Bafana and Kaizer Chiefs player stepped down as head coach of TS Galaxy.

BERNARD PARKER BACKTRACKS ON BOMBSHELL CLAIMS

On Monday, 12 October, Bernard Parker dropped a bombshell statement on his official social media platforms about his personal life.



This included that he has split from his baby mama, Kacha Stepanovic, and was struggling with “personal addictions”. He also used the opportunity to apologise to the red-haired woman, alluding to infidelity in their three-year relationship. The news came as a surprise to the public, given that his last known relationship was his marriage to his wife, Wendy Parker.

A few days later, Bernard Parker did a 180 on his initial statement, effectively denying what he initially wrote.

He shared: “I am aware of statements circulating publicly concerning my personal circumstances and relationships. For clarity, any communication attributed to me should be treated as official only if it has been confirmed by me or issued through my authorised representative.

Bernard called for the public to “exercise discretion and refrain from circulating unverified information or speculation about my private life”.

He added that he was “attending to the matter privately and responsibly, with due consideration for the well-being and dignity of everyone concerned, particularly the children”

Bernard also deleted his reposts of several Instagram Reels, which spoke of lust, betrayal and a “miserable marriage”.



STEPPING DOWN AS TS GALAXY COACH

Meanwhile, Bernard Parker has been replaced by Esau Mtsweni, who steps in as TS Galaxy’s interim coach.

The surprise move was announced by club chairman Tim Suzaki, who claimed the move was football-related and not a result of Bernard’s personal life.

He told SABC Sport: “As a club, we’re also quite surprised when we saw the long statement coming from his social media account…Clubs and employers, in general, don’t get too involved in people’s personal affairs.

“You see and hear of them as and when they happen, you know.”

Suzaki alluded to Bernard Parker’s personal life “challenges”, adding: “He’s a man, he should find a way to resolve it. So that he could come back to football if he’s not within football”.

World.title: Tributes pour in for Lions player Hyron Andrews died in France
World.content:
PARIS - South African second-row forward Hyron Andrews of Johannesburg-based side the Lions was found dead at a hotel in France on Friday, on the eve of his team's Champions Cup match against La Rochelle, local authorities told AFP.

A source close to the investigation said the 31-year-old lock was found in cardiac arrest in a shower cubicle that was locked from the inside.

The public prosecutor in La Rochelle, western France, confirmed that an investigation had been opened to determine the cause of death, which occurred on the island of Ile de Re, and said that an accidental death was currently the leading line of inquiry.

An autopsy is due to be carried out, the source close to the investigation said.

"This devastating news has sent shockwaves through the international rugby community," the Lions said in a statement.

"The former Sharks and Sale Sharks lock forward was a valued member of the Lions family, and his loss will be felt profoundly by his teammates, coaches, supporters and all who had the privilege of knowing him."

Andrews had only returned to his native South Africa earlier this year after two years with English Prem side Sale Sharks. He began his career with the Sharks franchise in Durban and represented his country at Under-20 level.

"We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron. He was not only a gifted rugby player, but also a cherished member of our Lions family, having recently joined us this season," added Lions chief executive Rudolf Straeuli.

"On behalf of... everyone at the Lions, I extend our deepest sympathies to (his wife) Maighlin, their young sons Hendrix and Emerson and the entire Andrews family. We stand with them in their sorrow and will remember Hyron with great affection and respect."

Playing in 'honour of Hyron'

The Lions said Saturday's match against La Rochelle would go ahead as planned "in honour of Hyron".

It is the first time the Lions have played in the Champions Cup, which brings together the best European and South African clubs. A moment's silence will be held ahead of all Champions Cup and second-tier Challenge Cup matches this weekend in memory of Andrews.

"Hyron was a respected member of the rugby community whose contribution to the game and impact on those around him will be remembered with great fondness," said Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union.

"His untimely passing is a devastating loss, and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him.

"The thoughts and prayers of the entire South African rugby family are with Maighlin and all those mourning his loss."

Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson also paid tribute to Andrews, who played 45 times for the club after initially joining as injury cover at the end of the 2023-24 season.

"Hyron was just a brilliant guy and a brilliant teammate. He was so skilled on the field but off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with," said Sanderson.

"He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him."

The tragedy comes exactly 10 years to the day since the sudden death of former Munster coach Anthony Foley, who died in his sleep aged 42 due to a heart rhythm disorder just hours before his team were due to play against Racing 92 in Paris in the same competition.

La Rochelle coach Ronan O'Gara was a member of the Racing staff when Foley, a former Ireland international teammate, passed away in October 2016.

Bordeaux-Bègles are set to begin their bid for a record-equalling third straight Champions Cup crown later on Friday when they visit Gloucester in the tournament opener.

World.title: 'Sportswashing' or investment? Rwanda F1 stirs debate and doubts
World.content:
KIGALI - Viewed by some as "sportswashing" and by others as an overly ambitious, grandiose project, the prospect of a Formula 1 Grand Prix in Rwanda has provoked reaction at home and abroad.

The government touts the initiative as a significant "investment in Rwanda's future", slated for sometime in the early 2030s.

On Tuesday, Kigali put on a glitzy ceremony to announce the "historic" agreement between Rwanda, the organisation that owns Formula 1, and the International Automobile Federation (FIA).

A landlocked country still widely associated with a horrific genocide in 1994, Rwanda has used sports to revamp its image, attract tourists and impress investors with its organisational efficiency.

The event promises glamour, replete with champagne-quaffing celebrities, set against the backdrop of Rwanda's verdant hills and rich wildlife, all broadcast to a global audience.

Formula 1 markets itself as the third most-watched sporting event on the planet, trailing only the Olympic Games and the FIFA World Cup.

However, the project has drawn dismay from some quarters, including Amnesty International, which immediately condemned it as an act of sportswashing.

The NGO accuses Kigali of "buying into the world's biggest sports to polish its image and deflect from its appalling human rights record".

This same criticism has been levelled against Formula 1 on several previous occasions.

In its pursuit of global expansion, the sport has forged numerous partnerships with governments with questionable rights records, including China and Azerbaijan.

Sports diplomacy

Last year, Rwanda became the first African nation to successfully host the World Cycling Championships.

Through its "Visit Rwanda" campaign, Kigali also sponsors several major European football clubs, including Paris Saint-Germain (PSG), as well as the NBA's Los Angeles Clippers.

However, while President Paul Kagame is credited with a strategic vision that has driven Rwanda's economic transformation over his decades-long tenure, he has faced repeated accusations from opponents of suppressing political dissent.

Reacting to the news, Kenneth Roth, the former director of Human Rights Watch, noted on X Rwanda's "invasion via its M23 proxy of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo".

The armed M23 group, backed financially and militarily by Kigali, has forcibly seized vast swathes of the DRC.

During the Kigali ceremony, Kagame said it was an "honour" to be selected for Formula 1.

He described it as an "investment in Rwanda's future" that would bring "jobs, skills, tourism and new business to our country and our region for decades to come".

But one foreign attendee voiced concerns, telling AFP in English: "I am really hoping Rwanda is not chewing what it cannot swallow."

Formula 1 is an expensive pursuit and far wealthier nations have already seen their ambitions backfire.

The Qatar model

India and South Korea, which built circuits specifically to host Formula 1, eventually withdrew as their financial losses mounted.

European organisers, including those in France and, more recently, the Netherlands, have encountered similar setbacks.

In comparison, Rwanda, despite its economic boom, remains a low-income country with a GDP per capita barely exceeding $1,100.

It ranks 159 out of 193 countries on the United Nations' Human Development Index, although it is steadily improving.

Critics question whether the hundreds of millions of dollars required to build a modern racetrack might be better spent on healthcare or education, not to mention the tens of millions of dollars F1 Grand Prix organisers typically charge host countries for the privilege of holding the event.

A source close to the FIA said Qatar was "supporting" the Rwandan project.

The Gulf country is also building a new international airport in Bugesera, 40 kilometres (25 miles) from Kigali, near where the racetrack will be constructed.

Jean-Guy Africa, CEO of the Rwanda Development Board, pointed to the "tremendous interest" from the private sector.

"You cannot miss out on the 100,000 people who will come. From a business standpoint, you stand to benefit," he told AFP.

While several Rwandans told AFP of their pride that their country will soon host the pinnacle of motor sports, Kigali entrepreneur Amon Niyigena, took a more pragmatic view.

"The economics of hosting F1 in Rwanda will not be for everyone, but for a tiny percentage of the already rich," he said.

AFP

World.title: Real Madrid say Tebas must resign over Goebbels comparison
World.content:
MADRID - Real Madrid called on Friday for La Liga president Javier Tebas to resign after he compared the club's efforts to discredit referees to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.

Tebas said in a post on X on Friday that Real Madrid's in-house TV channel often suggested that referees attempt to prevent the club from winning.

The outspoken Spanish league chief said these tactics "recall propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels".

Tebas later attempted to clarify that he was drawing comparisons with "those propaganda techniques" and not with the ideology of the Nazis.

Madrid responded by saying in a statement that Tebas' claims were "deeply offensive (and) morally repugnant".

It added that Madrid believe he is unfit to represent Spain's leading clubs and that he should consider "immediate resignation".

Coach Jose Mourinho has also claimed that Madrid are consistently penalised by referees.

Tebas has frequently clashed with Madrid's president Florentino Perez, especially over the club's plans to join a European Super League in 2021.

World.title: NBA tells sportsbooks to ban certain bets and parlays: report
World.content:
NEW YORK - The NBA told sportsbook partners in a Friday memo to ban certain types of bets and parlays this season that gamblers used in recent wagering scandals, ESPN reported.

The prohibition includes a player prop parlay and bets on "under" for players that were part of federal gambling cases that included NBA players Terry Rozier and Jontay Porter, according to the report.

The league directed authorized gambling partners, including FanDuel and DraftKings, not to offer bets on such areas as the winner of a game's opening tip-off, players on missing specific shots and under bets for players expected to see under 12 minutes of playing time.

"There's a balance between ensuring that we are removing problematic bet types but also ensuring that we don't just move activity into the illegal market," NBA executive vice president Scott Kaufman-Ross told ESPN.

"Where we landed right now, we think, is the right balance of those two objectives."

Sportsbooks will be banned from offering lines with larger payouts on under wagers.

NBA agreements with sportsbook partners permit the league to restrict what wagers they offer.

Federal prosecutors said one bettor wagered $80,000 on the under for six statistical categories for Porter in a Toronto Raptors game during the 2023-24 campaign for a $1.1 million payout.

Porter admitted removing himself from the game to benefit bettors.

Prosecutors claim Rozier was involved in a similar situation while with Charlotte in 2023, although Rozier has pleaded not guilty and denied any wrongdoing.

In another memo to clubs, the NBA noted new integrity measures to begin this season, with former NFL star and retired FBI agent Charles Tillman leading training on sport betting rules and enhanced AI looking for unusual betting patterns involving the NBA.

The memo said the league seeks to better protect players, coaches and other personnel from threats or harassment from bettors.

World.title: US influence, AI and mistrust cloud Alberta independence vote
World.content:
TORONTO - The run-up to a referendum in Canada's Alberta region on a future independence vote has been clouded by US political influence and AI-manipulated online content, leaving experts concerned that the results will be contested no matter the outcome.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Thursday that he expected foreign governments, the "United States included", would not get involved in Canadian elections.

But the US is already on the scene.

President Donald Trump has launched a trade war and repeatedly claimed that Canada should be incorporated into the United States.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called Alberta a "natural partner," while Canada's Globe and Mail newspaper recently detailed contacts between separatist leaders in the province and US Republican operatives.

Canada's foreign influence transparency commissioner said in September his office was "aware of concerns" about non-Canadian activities around the Alberta referendum. The minority New Democratic Party (NDP) has advocated for a parliamentary debate on the issue.

"None of these things can be taken in a vacuum," NDP Member of Parliament Heather McPherson told AFP.

Close Trump allies have also inserted themselves into the online independence conversation.

Last week, tech billionaire Elon Musk posted on X after francophone Quebec's separatist party win: "They would be better off. Alberta and Saskatchewan should separate too."

Brian McQuinn, the co-director of the Centre for Artificial Intelligence, Data and Conflict at the University of Regina told AFP it "would be folly" to discount the impact this could have in Canada.

Along with Americans, McQuinn says he also observed Russian-linked activity pushing the most extreme aspects of the independence debate.

This may not directly sway voters but will at least raise the temperature, he said.

"If the fire is big and you fan it, it really gets bigger."

- AI amplification -

World.title: Four arrested in Soweto drug lab bust
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Another suspected drug lab has been found in Meadowlands, Soweto.

Four suspects have been arrested at what the SAPS calls a mandrax drug lab.

Friday's discovery follows several similar cases in recent weeks, including a multimillion-rand mandrax lab uncovered in Krugersdorp.

Gauteng Organised Crime Investigations officers are combing the Soweto scene for further evidence.
