World.title: Chelsea captain James has knee surgery
World.content:
London – Chelsea captain Reece James has undergone successful knee surgery, the Premier League club announced on Friday.

The England international has missed Chelsea’s past two league games — a 3-0 defeat by Brentford and a 5-1 win over Bournemouth.

“The 26-year-old was absent from Saturday’s 5-1 victory over Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge while medical assessments took place following the injury suffered in training,” the club said in a statement.

“Those assessments confirmed surgery would be the required course of action.

“Reece has already begun his road to recovery and will be supported by the club’s medical department at Cobham during this rehabilitation phase.”

Chelsea are sixth in the Premier League ahead of Saturday’s visit to Everton.

World.title: Asian stocks rise as tech bounces from rout, Warsh upbeat on AI
World.content:
Hong Kong – Most Asian markets bounced Friday after the previous day’s tech rout fuelled by concerns over the AI boom, which Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh said offered huge benefits to the global economy.

Seoul and Tokyo enjoyed healthy gains in early exchanges boosted by chipmakers SK hynix and Kioxia, after having been pummelled Thursday as investors bailed out of the once-dominant AI sector.

The selling had been fuelled by forecast-beating US inflation data that ramped up bets on Fed interest rate hikes, as well as concerns about the financial health of data centre operator CoreWeave owing to its huge debt pile.

The New Jersey firm — which has borrowed heavily to finance hefty purchases of pricey semiconductor chips from Nvidia — tanked 15.5 percent Wednesday in the US as yields on some of its bonds soared, reflecting heightened angst over its future.

That added to concerns about the whole AI-tech complex, but Nvidia chief Jensen Huang on Thursday lifted spirits by defending the company and its health.

“CoreWeave’s strength is improving every day,” he told Bloomberg. “I’m optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing.”

CoreWeave’s shares climbed almost six percent.

Huang’s “defence of CoreWeave’s financial position was enough to pull the NeoCloud complex off the floor, drag AI equities higher and give the broader market something resembling a pulse”, wrote SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes.

“One moment the market was pricing the possibility that the AI financing machine had started eating its own tail, the next it was listening to the high priest of the boom explain that the patient was getting stronger.

“AI Jesus had entered the trading room and, for a while at least, the machines found religion again.”

Seoul jumped more than two percent and Tokyo around 1.8 percent, though they slumped 7.6 percent and 4.9 percent respectively Thursday.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Taipei, Mumbai, Bangkok and Manila were also up.

Paris and Frankfurt opened higher but London fell.

Fed chief Warsh said Friday that AI was the “most consequential change” to the global economy in his lifetime, predicting its effects would be positive but the path forward “bumpy”.

At an event at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok he said the AI investment boom would drive prices up in the short term, but “there really is, I think, a huge benefit to the global economy, to the US economy over the horizon”.

He also reiterated his previously stated belief that the technology would “make economies and countries that put it to good use more productive”.

But he added: “The path from where we are to there is likely to be a very bumpy one, bumpy in our understanding of the technology, bumpy because we really don’t know what the market structure is going to be of these new technologies.”

Shares in Jakarta tanked more than 11 percent — its heaviest loss since 1998 — after index compiler MSCI said it was “no longer appropriate” to maintain Indonesia’s emerging-market status, fuelling fears of an exodus of foreign investment.

The US firm said earlier this year that investors had raised concerns about “ongoing opacity in shareholding structures” as well as co-ordinated trading behaviour that affected price information.

Authorities said they had carried out changes but MSCI said Friday that investors had indicated the “sufficient progress has not been observed consistently across the Indonesian equity market”, adding “it considers Indonesia’s continued classification as an Emerging Market no longer appropriate”.

World.title: Trump’s new press secretary says China lacked ‘proper’ toilets
World.content:
Washington – White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, who was appointed less than a week ago, said China lacked “proper toilets” in an interview that aired on Thursday.

Zacharia, 41, is already under scrutiny over her legal credentials, after giving an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States.

The press secretary, who previously lived in China, recalled in an interview that the perception in 2016 was that China would soon overtake the United States.

“We were all being told Hillary (Clinton) was going to win. The golden days or the glory days of America were over. That China was on the horizon,” Zacharia told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec.

“I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, ‘How is China the next country on the horizon? They don’t even have proper toilets,” she added.

There was no immediate comment from Chinese authorities.

Trump has boasted about his “great relationship” with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

During a Washington summit in September, the two leaders discussed topics ranging from AI and trade to the stalled war in Iran, and confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year.

Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday and only answered questions from three journalists.

She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative spokesperson, who stepped down in August to care for her young children.

Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit. She also said she had worked at a law firm in Beijing.

Asked about her legal background on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was then “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move with her husband to China.

Zacharia said that she did not retake the bar exam upon returning to the United States due to the birth of her first child.

World.title: Indonesian stocks dive 11% as MSCI weighs market reclassification
World.content:
Jakarta – Indonesian stocks plunged more than 11 percent Friday as index compiler MSCI said it was “no longer appropriate” to maintain the country’s emerging-market status, fuelling fears of an exodus of foreign investment.

The US firm said earlier this year that investors had raised concerns about “ongoing opacity in shareholding structures” as well as co-ordinated trading behaviour that affected price information.

Authorities in Jakarta said in April they had completed reforms, hoping to avoid the downgrade, which could deal a blow to government efforts to kickstart Southeast Asia’s biggest economy, and have a significant impact on investment decisions.

But on Friday MSCI said investors had indicated the “sufficient progress has not been observed consistently across the Indonesian equity market”.

“Despite the announced reforms, significant concerns remain around market dysfunction, including continued suspected coordinated trading behaviour and lack of evidence of meaningful enforcement.

“Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia’s continued classification as an Emerging Market no longer appropriate and is launching a consultation on a proposal to reclassify Indonesia as a Standalone Market.”

“A reclassification to Frontier Markets would not properly recognise the depth of the market problems,” it said.

A standalone classification could force investment funds tracking the MSCI’s emerging market indexes to sell Indonesian holdings.

Argentina, Lebanon and Palestine are among the markets with the designation, with none in Asia, according to Bloomberg.

The Jakarta Composite Index collapsed eight percent at the open, sparking a trading halt. When trading resumed it was down 11.1 percent, its heaviest fall since early 1998 and sitting at its lowest level since 2020.

The index has now fallen more than 40 percent since the start of the year.

– Rupiah weakens –

In reaction to the news, the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) said it “respects MSCI’s independence in assessing and determining market classification based on its proprietary methodology”.

“However, considering the various progress and reform measures that have been taken, the IDX will request further clarification from MSCI regarding the basis for the considerations and assessments behind this announcement.

“We also need to emphasise that this MSCI announcement is still part of the consultation process, with input being accepted until April 30, 2027, and does not constitute a final decision.”

The rupiah dropped about 0.8 percent against the dollar to sit at around around 18,060, having hit 18,209 in June, its weakest level on record.

Erwin Gunawan Hutapea, the Indonesian central bank’s head of monetary management and securities, said the bank would take action to ensure stability of the rupiah, which had already tumbled around eight percent this year to a record low.

“Amid rising global risk-off sentiment, which has driven US dollar strengthening and put pressure on domestic financial markets, capital outflows from domestic portfolio assets are expected to continue.

“Bank Indonesia is committed to maintaining a presence in the market to uphold Rupiah exchange rate stability in line with its fundamentals and to ensure that market mechanisms function properly.”

The central bank had carried out several rate hikes earlier in the year to shore up the rupiah, after it came under pressure over the state of Southeast Asia’s biggest economy.

The bank is due to hold its next monetary policy meeting on Wednesday.

New York-based MSCI produces international indexes used by investors as a benchmark to balance their portfolios.

It has a significant impact on investment decisions through its flagship emerging markets index, which contains 1,200 companies with a market capitalisation more than $10 trillion.

Fund managers worldwide keep a close eye on what countries are included or excluded in MSCI’s indexes as that can trigger adjustments to their portfolios.

World.title: Iraq’s parliament approves new cabinet ministers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — On Thursday, Iraq’s parliament confirmed 11 cabinet nominees and three deputy prime ministers, including Laith al-Khazali, a key member in Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq who faces US terrorist sanctions.

The nomination is a politically risky decision for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, whose administration is dealing with strained regional ties and severe economic challenges as a result of the continuing US-Israeli war against Iran.

Al-Khazali is the brother of Qais al-Khazali, the commander of Asaib Ahl al-Haq, which Washington listed as a foreign terrorist organization in 2020.

Both brothers were classified as specially designated global terrorists, and the US Treasury sanctioned them individually in 2019 for suspected participation in violence against Iraqi demonstrators.

Their US designations also included references to assaults on American troops, such as a 2007 operation that killed five US soldiers.

The parliamentary decision raises concerns about al-Khazali’s nomination and its ramifications for Baghdad’s relationship with Washington, especially as al-Zaidi wants to reinforce Iraq’s sovereignty and manage ties with neighboring nations.

Following the voting, Al-Zaidi advised the newly appointed ministers and deputy prime ministers to do their duties with competence and integrity.

The appointments come as Iraq faces a deteriorating economic crisis, with oil export interruptions and liquidity shortages putting strain on the government’s budget.

Al-Zaidi has declared a significant depreciation of the Iraqi dinar, warning that the government confronts unprecedented economic and security problems.

The presence of a US-sanctioned militia member in the government’s high leadership may hamper Baghdad’s attempts to preserve fruitful relations with Washington.

World.title: ‘Mixed feelings’: AI cracks centuries-old ciphers
World.content:
Tokyo – Napoleon Bonaparte ordered the wartime missive written in code, creating a puzzle that went unsolved for more than 200 years — until AI cracked it in a matter of hours.

Artificial intelligence is helping non-specialists unlock the secrets of historical sources, a trend described as a “turning point” in a field previously the preserve of scholars and dedicated hobbyists.

One new sleuth is Carter Church, a 27-year-old AI engineer who decrypted a 19th-century letter to one of Napoleon’s generals.

Without digital tools, the task could have taken weeks, but the latest model from ChatGPT-maker OpenAI broke the cipher in just six hours.

“What AI mostly brings is persistence,” Church told AFP, saying he felt “an unbelievable sense of satisfaction and excitement when I saw the result”.

The message from 1809 — detailing French and allied troops’ positions in two dozen lines of symbols, numbers and letters — had lain ignored in an online academic archive.

Because traditional, low-tech methods to crack ciphers are effective but time- and labour-intensive, historians “have more important problems to solve, so many ciphers like this often sit unattended”, said Church.

To find the solution, Church, who works at US cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, needed to learn “very little” about code-breaking techniques or the historical period.

He spent some evenings going over it, then consulted Japanese patent engineer Satoshi Tomokiyo, who maintains an online list of unsolved ciphers, to verify it.

“2026 will be remembered as a turning point for codebreaking of historical ciphers,” Tomokiyo wrote on his website Cryptiana, a go-to resource for the small but enthusiastic global community of amateur cryptographers.

– ‘Mixed feelings’ –

Researchers were already developing AI models to break ciphers, but the public release of state-of-the-art generalist tools has unleashed dozens of new solutions.

Although Church used OpenAI’s most powerful model, GPT-6 Astra, other people have used top offerings from rival US lab Anthropic instead.

Tomokiyo said that since mid-September, most of the ciphers on his list have been cracked using AI.

“There remain some tough problems” which could stay an enigma for years to come, because there is less relevant data available to help AI figure them out, the 58-year-old told AFP.

“I’m excited long-time problems are now solved, but on the other hand, I have mixed feelings, because AI seems to have solved these difficult problems so easily,” he said.

With technology draining the satisfaction of being first to crack a cipher, a fellow code-breaker told Tomokiyo: “I feel useless.”

AI is surpassing human abilities in pursuits from mathematics to computer programming, while threatening to alter or even eradicate many jobs.

The technology is transforming the work of historians not only by decoding documents, but also by analysing millions of medieval manuscripts or helping read ancient scrolls.

Too fragile to be unrolled without risking destruction, the Herculaneum Papyri — hundreds of papyrus scrolls carbonised in the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 AD — are now being X-rayed and analysed by AI to reveal the hidden writing inside.

Researchers in Italy announced in June the first complete virtual unrolling of a scroll, which turned out to be a treatise on ethics.

– ‘Facebook of the past’ –

AI is also being used to build a huge, searchable collection of previously inaccessible sources on Jewish history and culture by transcribing 10 million pages of Hebrew manuscripts.

“It’s gigantic. No human being could process such a quantity” of data, said project leader Daniel Stoekl Ben Ezra, of the Ecole Pratique des Hautes Etudes in Paris.

Researchers hope the databases created using the digitised text — which he likens to a kind of “huge Facebook of the past” — could help bring to light links between people, places and ideas.

And at the French capital’s Notre Dame Cathedral, an AI system has been trained to transcribe 14,600 Latin pages from the church’s medieval archives — a task not dissimilar to code-breaking.

“These are minutes drawn up by notaries who abbreviate their decisions. The script is highly administrative, very pragmatic… with rather technical vocabulary,” said historian Julie Claustre, who leads the e-NDP project.

With character recognition rates ranging between 88 and 94 percent, the project has revealed information about the cathedral’s daily life, its building work, its staff and the care of abandoned children.

Doing the same by hand would take “several decades”, said Claustre, but “it’s not just a time-saver”.

Automation enables “inquiries that were not previously possible; it transforms the conditions of research.”

World.title: Using AI to help find Mexico’s legions of missing children
World.content:
Mexico City – Veronica Rosas is one of tens of thousands of Mexican mothers looking for a child that has disappeared into a vortex of violence fueled by brutal cartel turf wars.

Now artificial intelligence may be able to help the loved ones of Mexico’s legions of disappeared.

Two new AI tools are being developed to help in the search for the more than 134,000 people being sought.

Rosas’ son, Diego, went missing at the age of 16 in the central town of Ecatepec in September 2015 after leaving his home to meet some friends.

The state prosecutor’s office said he was kidnapped by a criminal gang but have not established which group, why, or whether Diego is still alive.

“It’s been 11 years and I still don’t know where Diego is. There’s no line of investigation leading us to find out what happened to my son,” Rosas, 52, told AFP at one of the demonstrations held regularly in Mexico City to demand justice.

Cases like Diego’s have prompted two universities to develop AI tools they hope will provide answers.

Regresa (Return) was developed by Mexico’s main public university, UNAM. It uses anthropometry — human body measurements — to create an image of how the faces of minors, which remain frozen in time in missing persons posters, may have changed over time.

With investigations generally dragging on for years, these updated likenesses are a recurring demand of the families.

Countries like the United States, India and China already use facial recognition and age progression software to search for kidnapped children.

In Mexico, some prosecutors’ offices use the technology but most software relies on open-source photo databases that don’t reflect typical Mexican traits.

Regresa’s developers took a different approach.

They created their own image bank from hundreds of photos and data from 75 Mexican volunteers to make portraits that feature more typically Mexican features.

Anthropologist Ana Juarez, one of the project’s founders, explained that Regresa also uses different technology to age the children.

“Many software programs only work with facial contours or textures, or add filters that simulate wrinkles. We seek to develop a scientific approach that shows how a person grows in craniofacial terms,” she explained to AFP, referring to imagining that predicts the developments of the skull.

– Peace boxes and posters –

In Mexico, the inaction of authorities over many years has prompted many families to carry out their own investigations.

AI is also being used by an anthropologist at the private Ibero-American University to help facilitate those searches.

Emiliano Zolla is mapping the missing by gender, age and the circumstances of their disappearance, in the hope that it will help families refine their search.

Among his observations, based on data about cases in the State of Mexico, the country’s most populous, are that many of the missing are young women who disappear either going to or returning from school or work.

The use of AI could be a game-changer, Rosas said, on learning about Regresa from AFP.

“This initiative is very important because they’re not the little people who were taken back then,” she said.

Rosas has erected a makeshift mailbox bearing a picture of 16-year-old Diego on Mexico City’s main avenue to receive clues as to his whereabouts or greetings for him on his birthday.

Karla Lechuga created a search collective after the disappearance of her 19-year-old son, Jeshua Cisneros, in 2025.

Groups like hers have installed dozens of “peace boxes” in churches across the country to gather information.

They also post photos of their missing loved ones in public spaces and urge criminal groups to provide anonymous tipoffs.

“We have found some people alive, unfortunately others not,” Lechuga said.

World.title: PM Modi to visit Canada on December 11-12, Mark Carney confirms after phone call
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Canada on December 11-12, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said, as New Delhi and Ottawa seek to strengthen bilateral ties and advance cooperation in trade, energy, technology and security.

Carney confirmed the dates while speaking to visitors at a restaurant in Calgary on Thursday, saying he had âjust spokeâ to PM Modi about the upcoming visit. He said the PM Modi would travel to Toronto and Ottawa, adding, âWeâll see if we can broaden it out.â

The Indian High Commission in Ottawa subsequently confirmed the December 11-12 visit in a post on X, saying the two leaders had agreed to build on the positive momentum in bilateral relations and work towards concrete outcomes across key sectors.

The confirmation came amid renewed diplomatic engagement between the two countries, with both sides pushing to expand economic cooperation and conclude negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).

However, the ministry of external affairs had said on Friday that the dates were still under discussion.

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: âAs you are aware, foreign minister of Canada visited India a few days back.





She met with the external affairs minister (S Jaishankar) and discussed progress in bilateral ties. She also called on the Prime Minister. During the visit, the PM Modi's visit to Canada came up for discussion. The dates for the visit are presently under discussion. We will announce the visit at the appropriate time.

â

India, Canada push to conclude trade deal

PM Modi's proposed visit comes as the two countries seek to conclude negotiations on CEPA by the end of 2026, with the agreement expected to support efforts to double bilateral trade by 2030.

Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand discussed the trade pact and ways to expand cooperation during her meeting with Modi in New Delhi earlier this week. The discussions covered trade, investment, energy, education, culture, technology and security.

According to a readout issued by the Canadian government, the two leaders also discussed the Team Canada Trade Mission to India, led by Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu, as an effort to expand bilateral trade and strengthen Canada's engagement in the Indo-Pacific.

âMinister Anand and PM Modi discussed the importance of concluding a comprehensive economic partnership agreement by the end of the year and highlighted the Team Canada Trade Mission led by International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu as a tangible example of growing the economic partnership, expansion of bilateral trade and advancing Canada's broader engagements in the Indo-Pacific,â the statement read.

Following the meeting, Modi described the discussions as productive and reiterated India's commitment to strengthening ties with Canada.

âPleased to meet Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand. We had a productive discussion on further strengthening India-Canada ties in trade, technology, security, energy, education and people-to-people exchanges,â PM Modi said in a post on X.

âIndia is committed to building a constructive and forward-looking strategic partnership with Canada that delivers tangible benefits to the people of both countries,â he added.

Anand also expressed optimism about the relationship, saying the two countries had considerable scope to expand cooperation in trade, investment and security.

âCanada and India have enormous potential to shape a more prosperous future, together. I had the opportunity to meet with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi today to discuss our strategic partnership and the opportunities ahead for trade, investment and security,â she said.

âFrom Prime Minister Carney's visit earlier this year to the Team Canada Trade Mission underway, our renewed engagement reflects a growing ambition to turn shared priorities into lasting opportunities for both nations,â Anand said, adding that Canada looked forward to welcoming PM Modi in December.

Leaders seek to build on improved bilateral ties

The planned visit follows a telephone conversation between PM Modi and Carney earlier this week, during which the two leaders discussed strengthening the India-Canada strategic partnership.

PM Modi described the conversation as warm and productive, stressing the importance of closer cooperation between the two countries.

âTogether, India and Canada are contributing towards a more stable and prosperous world,â PM Modi said in a post on X.

World.title: 'Women ought to be released after sunset': Neha Bora questions night-long detentions over anti-SIR stir
World.content:
AISA president Neha Bora, who was detained during the anti-SIR protest in Delhi, questioned the overnight detention of protesters and alleged that police delayed her access to a lawyer

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora on Saturday questioned the overnight detention of protesters, over the anti-SIR stir, saying women ought to be released after sunset and alleging that police denied her access to a lawyer for hours.Bora was detained under preventive provisions on the evening of October 16 and released early Saturday after formal procedures under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act, Delhi Police said.âUnder what authority is this justified? By what law or order is it permissible to keep detainees held in custody all night long? Legally, individuals, especially women, ought to be released after sunset, yet this is not happening,â Bora said.She alleged that police demanded her personal details but did not allow her to speak to or consult a lawyer for a long time. âOur lawyers spent 5â6 hours trying to reach me. It was only after we managed to call them that they were finally allowed to meet me,â she said.Bora also accused authorities of creating chaos in Central Delhi through roadblocks and restrictions, while questioning the police response to the protests."Law and order are being flouted in every possible way. Ordinary citizens are treated as if they were hardened criminals, a practice that has persisted in this country for a long time," she said."Furthermore, there is a new narrative being pushed, one of chaos and anarchy. What kind of chaos and anarchy? The one you unleashed in Central Delhi? The people of Delhi cannot even breathe a sigh of relief; whichever route they take to get to work, they find it blocked. You are spreading chaos and anarchy across the nation. Please, spare the people of India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR, so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," she added.Calling for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumarâs impeachment and a halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, she said the move was necessary to ensure citizensâ voting rights.Meanwhile, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, who was also detained on Friday evening ahead of the âLehra Do Tirangaâ protest, is set to be produced before a special executive magistrate court.Delhi Police said action under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita was initiated against him.CJP had earlier alleged that Dipke was taken to an undisclosed location and denied access to lawyers, claiming his family and party members were unable to contact him for more than 10 hours. AISA had also said Boraâs whereabouts remained unknown for several hours before its lawyers traced her to the RK Puram police station around midnight.

World.title: SPO missing with his rifle found dead in J&K’s Kishtwar
World.content:
: A 54-year-old special police officer (SPO) in J&K, who had gone missing along with his service rifle in Kishtwar district, has been found dead, officials said.

World.title: Centre deviating from assurances, say Ladakh groups
World.content:
SRINAGAR: A day after crucial talks on autonomy between a ministry of home affairs (MHA) subcommittee and Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) in Leh, representatives of the two bodies rejected on Friday a draft govt proposal and claimed âit represents a significant departureâ from assurances made during previous meetings of the panel.

LAB and KDA urged MHA to reconsider its draft and accept a memorandum of understanding (MoU) submitted by the two bodies in âits true spirit and entiretyâ.The next meeting has been scheduled for October 22 in Delhi, according to the Ladakhi representatives.

âAmong several major concerns, the (MHA) draft fails to address the demand for a legislative assembly and constitutional safeguards under Article 371, including a provision tailored to Ladakhâs unique circumstances.

Instead, it proposes a NEFA-type arrangement that falls far short of the proposed Union Territory with a legislature, which was the minimum guarantee agreed upon in the meeting of May 22, 2026,â LAB and KDA said in a joint statement on Friday.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEFA is the acronym for the erstwhile North East Frontier Agency.

LAB and KDA -- the two major political bodies in the Union territory of Ladakh -- will submit a detailed response to the MHA on Oct 18, elaborating on their objections and reiterating their positions.





LAB and KDA asserted that their draft MoU âreflects genuine aspirations and demands consistently advocated since 2021â. âThe people of Ladakh deserve a meaningful constitutional framework that honours prior commitments and safeguards their political, cultural and democratic aspirations, rather than an arrangement that dilutes them,â the statement said.

The last such meeting on autonomy with the Centre was held on Sept 9 in New Delhi. LAB and KDA representatives attended it. Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra had then spoken of âa sui generis model under Article 371 which does not exist anywhere in the countryâ.

Ladakhi representatives have been in talks with the Centre since 2023 but the process stalled briefly after four people were killed and over 80 injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood in Leh in Sept last year.

World.title: J&K outcry & probe after senior IAS ‘abuses’ woman junior
World.content:
A video emerged showing IAS officer Kumar Rajeev Ranjan allegedly abusing J&K administrative officer Beenish Wani during a meeting (Photo credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: A purported video of a senior J&K IAS officer, Kumar Rajeev Ranjan, allegedly using abusive language against a junior woman colleague at a virtual meeting has triggered an outcry, an inquiry, an NCW notice and calls for the senior bureaucrat to be shunted out.In the video from Wednesdayâs meeting, Ranjan, secretary of labour and employment department, is heard telling Beenish Wani, a J&K Administrative Service (JKAS) officer, âshut upâ and âbloody shitâ.CM Omar Abdullah decried Ranjanâs behaviour and wrote to chief secretary (CS) Atal Dulloo for action. Omarâs father, National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah, called for Ranjanâs removal. Former CM and PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti urged Omar to take up the matter with the Centre. Peoples Conference, BJP, Congress and JKAS Association also demanded action.Amid the outrage, govt on Friday ordered an inquiry led by a woman IAS officer, Mandeep Kaur, against Ranjan with directions to submit a report within 15 days. It issued a circular asking all officials to âmaintain the highest standards of integrity, devotion to duty, discipline and conduct becoming of a public servantâ.The action came as National Commission for Women (NCW) took suo motu cognisance of the video and its chairperson, Vijaya Rahatkar, wrote to chief secretary Dulloo pressing for an impartial inquiry, to be followed by appropriate disciplinary and legal action if the allegations are established.NCW also called for safeguards against workplace harassment and professional retaliation, along with protection and support for Wani. It sought an Action Taken Report (ATR) within seven days. âEvery woman officer is entitled to a safe, respectful and dignified workplace. Abuse of authority and workplace humiliation must be addressed with utmost seriousness,â NCW said.The purported video shows Wani objecting to being called âshitâ, Ranjan asking other officers that she should be suspended, and the woman subordinate retorting âto hell with youâ.Some JKAS officers met CS Dulloo on Friday. A member of the delegation quoted Dulloo as saying govt âwould not tolerate such behaviourâ and commending Wani for standing up to Ranjan, whose labour department put out a statement dismissing the video as an AI-generated fabrication.âIâve seen the video. Prima facie, the conduct of the senior officer was not in keeping with the standards expected of a senior IAS. Unfortunately as a Union territory (UT), control over IAS officers rests with Lok Bhavan (LG Manoj Sinhaâs secretariat). But as CM, Iâve instructed CS (Dulloo) to ensure the JKAS officer (Wani) faces no retributive action,â CM Omar said.NC chief Farooq was scathing. âThe officer (Ranjan) should be removed from J&K. If he stays, he will find it very difficult to continue. If it would have happened in my time, he would not have remained for more than two minutes. I would have put him on a plane and sent him back,â Farooq said.

World.title: Higher duties at lower pay amount to workplace exploitation, says J&K HC
World.content:
The division bench found no illegality or impropriety in the single bench order and upheld its directions.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

JAMMU: Compelling an employee to discharge the responsibilities of a higher post while paying him a lower salary amounts to workplace exploitation, which is impermissible in law, Jammu & Kashmir high court ruled.A division bench comprising Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajesh Sekhri made the observations while dismissing J&K govtâs appeal against a single bench order granting substantive promotion and consequential benefits to a municipal employee.The petitioner, Ghulam Mohammad Sheikh, was engaged as a daily wager in Sopore municipal council in 1980, and his services were regularised in 1988.In his petition, Sheikh said while his similarly situated colleague, Khazir Mohammad Shah, was promoted as jamadar/sanitary supervisor in 1994, he was denied the promotion despite having been regularised in the same year.He subsequently approached the high court, which in 1999 directed the authorities to consider his claim for promotion. However, the direction was not implemented in letter and spirit.Allowing Sheikhâs petition on May 2, 2023, the single bench held that he should be deemed substantively appointed and promoted as sanitary supervisor from April 28, 2005, with all consequential benefits.Sheikh had been performing the duties of jamadar/sanitary supervisor since June 2000, initially in his own pay and grade and subsequently with charge allowance from April 28, 2005.The UT administration challenged the verdict before the division bench, contending that merely performing the duties of a higher post did not confer any right to substantive promotion or the corresponding pay scale.Rejecting the govtâs contentions, the bench said although an employee ordinarily cannot claim the pay scale of a higher post merely because he has performed its duties, an exception exists where the employee has been formally ordered to discharge the responsibilities of that post.The division bench found no illegality or impropriety in the single bench order and upheld its directions.
