World.title: With great fandom comes great cosplay: Hyderabad gears up for Comic Con 2026
World.content:
For some, it is about stepping into the shoes of a favourite superhero, even if only for a day. For others, it is the excitement of watching grown adults transform into fictional characters with astonishing attention to detail. And for a few, preparing for Comic Con has become an annual family ritual, involving months of planning, costume trials and even fitness routines.

As Hyderabad Comic Con prepares to return for a three-day celebration from December 11 to 13 at Bharat Future City, the city’s community of cosplayers, anime enthusiasts, gamers and comic book lovers has begun looking forward to another gathering of familiar characters and shared passions.

For 24-year-old Sathwik Reddy from Musheerabad, the fascination with cosplay began during the COVID-19 lockdown, when he developed an interest in dressing up as fictional characters. Since the pandemic, he has been a regular at Comic Con events, drawn as much by the creativity of fellow enthusiasts as by the experience of participating. “It is surreal to see people, grown adults, so passionately cosplay and nail it!” he said, describing the enthusiasm that keeps bringing him back.

A fascination which demands diet control and fitness

For 32-year-old Anusha Rao, Comic Con has become something of a household tradition, thanks to her husband’s enduring fascination with Spider-Man. Every year, the couple begin preparing months in advance as he plans to try out a new version of the superhero’s costume. “He is a huge Spider-Man fan and we start prepping months ahead. This also makes him maintain a good diet and stay fit, so I am happy to support this,” she chuckled.

Enthusiasm for storytelling and fictional worlds

Beyond the costumes, the convention has become a space where enthusiasts can celebrate interests that often extend well beyond childhood. From anime and manga to comic books and video games, the event brings together fans who share an enthusiasm for storytelling and fictional worlds.

Three days of fandom and gaming

Organised by NODWIN Gaming, Hyderabad Comic Con will feature cosplay, gaming tournaments, comic book creators, international guests, live music performances, stand-up comedy and interactive experience zones.

A notable addition this year will be the Hyderabad chapter of Indie Game Utsav, which will provide independent game developers an opportunity to showcase their creations to gamers and international publishers.

Comic Con to be part of Invest Telangana Global Summit

This year’s edition will also mark the first time Hyderabad Comic Con will be part of the Invest Telangana Global Summit, while continuing its association with India Joy for the third consecutive year.

Shefali Johnson, CEO of Comic Con India, said Hyderabad’s enthusiasm for storytelling made it one of the convention’s most exciting destinations. “Hyderabad is one of our most exciting Comic Con cities, with a community that brings incredible energy and enthusiasm to the show floor,” she said.

Shares visual storytelling with Telangana’s Cheriyal scroll paintings

Drawing parallels between comic books and Telangana’s traditional Cheriyal scroll paintings, she said the two forms shared a common language of visual storytelling, using images and characters to bring narratives to life.

Akshat Rathee, co-founder and Managing Director of NODWIN Gaming, said Hyderabad’s storytelling culture, ranging from Telugu cinema to traditional art forms such as Oggu Katha and Burrakatha, provided a natural connection to contemporary pop culture.

Fans discuss accessibility

While the return of Comic Con has generated interest among fans, the shift from HITEX to Bharat Future City has also prompted discussions about accessibility. On Reddit, some Hyderabad residents have questioned the distance to the new venue, with one enthusiast expressing disappointment that the longer journey could make attending difficult. Others have begun discussing tickets and plans for the December event. The event will open at 11 a.m. on all three days, with tickets available on the Comic Con India website.

World.title: Two SC men fall at BC villagers’ feet after row over burial of 90-year-old in Erode cemetery
World.content:
Allegations of caste discrimination have surfaced in Perumbali village in Madathupalayam panchayat near Perundurai in Erode district, after two members of a Scheduled Caste (SC) community reportedly fell at the feet of members of a Backward Caste (BC) community amid opposition to the burial of a deceased man in a common cemetery.

More than 100 people belonging to an SC community live in the village. They have faced difficulties burying their dead in the local cemetery owing to opposition from members of the dominant BC community and have had to take the bodies to Thingalur, about five kilometres away. Following a survey, the Perundurai Tahsildar had declared the burial ground common to all communities.

SC members threatened

On October 5, Chenni, a 90-year-old inhabitant belonging to the SC community, died of age-related ailments. When members of the SC community took his body to the cemetery, they allegedly faced opposition from members of the BC community, leading to an argument.

According to the district police, the burial was conducted under police and Revenue Department protection. During an argument between members of the two communities, members of the SC community were allegedly threatened and told not to approach the other community for any work in the future. Following this, two members of the SC community fell at the feet of members of the BC community.

Case registered

The police said a case had been registered at Thingalur police station on Thursday (October 8, 2026) night based on a complaint lodged by the Perundurai Revenue Inspector. Provisions of the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act were invoked against two persons in connection with the incident. An investigation was under way.

Incident triggers outrage

Video footage of the incident, including the alleged humiliation of the SC community members, has circulated on social media, triggering condemnation and demands for action against those responsible.

Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) State coordinator for the western zone P. Eswaran alleged that members of the BC community had violated the rights of SC people by opposing their use of the common burial ground. He said the alleged threat that they would be denied work if they used the cemetery amounted to caste oppression. He also condemned the alleged exploitation of their economic vulnerability to force them to fall at the feet of members of the other community.

Mr. Eswaran questioned the role of the police and Revenue Department officials present at the spot and demanded action against those who opposed the burial and officials who allegedly failed to prevent the humiliation.

World.title: Delhi court grants Brij Bhushan time to reply to plea against acquittal
World.content:
A Delhi Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) granted former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh time to file his reply to an appeal filed by four women grapplers against his acquittal in a sexual harassment case.

Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh had on September 28 issued notices to Mr. Singh, the State, and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar.

On Friday (October 9, 2026), the judge granted Mr. Singh time to file a reply and posted the matter for October 28.

When the Court asked the Delhi Police if it was going to file an appeal, the public prosecutor said a decision on the issue is yet to be taken, and sought 15 days to inform the Court about the decision

Judge Singh said that once the arguments commence, the proceedings will be held in camera.

Mr. Singh was in the Court when the matter was heard.

On August 3, a magisterial court acquitted Mr. Singh, a former BJP MP, in the sexual harassment case filed by six women wrestlers, including world championship medallist Vinesh Phogat, citing lack of evidence. A criminal appeal filed on September 25 assailed Mr. Singh's acquittal.

According to the wrestlers' appeal, the acquittal was unsustainable in law, founded on a "manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation" of the evidence on record, proceeded on conjectures and surmises, and "failed to apply binding and well-settled principles of law."

World.title: Drought impact: Shivamogga village bans post-marriage non-vegetarian feasts
World.content:
Residents of Harigi, a village about 30 km from Shikaripur in Shivamogga district, have resolved to ban non-vegetarian feasts at weddings - beegaroota - in view of the severe drought affecting the agrarian community.

Villagers who met earlier this week discussed the issue and announced the prohibition. The Grama Abhivruddhi Samiti (village development committee), comprising village elders, will enforce the resolution and impose penalties on violators.

Under the decision, no resident may host such a feast in the village or attend one organised elsewhere. The committee has fixed a penalty of ₹1 lakh on those who host a feast in violation of the resolution and ₹50,000 on those who attend such events as guests.

Also Read : Karnataka estimates crop loss at ₹46,324 crore as 220 taluks may be declared drought-hit

Burden of debt

Villagers said the decision followed a series of incidents in which families were left burdened with debt after hosting these events. “Until 10 years ago, we did not have the tradition of hosting elaborate feasts. It entered our village in recent years and has quickly become an integral part of the ceremony. Families of both the groom and the bride arrange feasts. Some families have spent up to ₹10 lakh on one feast,” said Shekharaj, president of the Grama Abhivruddhi Samiti.

A few families had to sell a portion of their land or take huge loans to raise the money. “The expenses increased as hosting the feast became a matter of prestige. Some people arranged three to four quintals of meat and offered lunch to over 5,000 people,” said Shanmukha Harigi, treasurer of the committee.

“We sensed this trend would ruin poor families. We had come up with a similar idea of prohibition five years ago, but there was hardly any support. Now, because of drought, people understand its implications. Our families can use the same money for other purposes that serve them in the long run,” he said.

A majority of the villagers belong to the Deevaru community, a Backward Classes community, and depend on agriculture for their livelihood. Of the 350 families in the village, all but a few are small growers cultivating paddy and maize, crops that have been badly hit by the drought. The State government has included Shikaripur among the drought-hit taluks.

“We cannot expect any returns from the fields. Areca growers are somehow managing with the available water, but they are also worried about safeguarding plants. Given this situation, we want to save our lives,” Mr. Shanmukha said.

The treasurer said that the amount collected as fine, if anybody violated the ban, would be utilised for the village temple.

Emulate them, say elders

The decision has been widely appreciated. Office-bearers of Deevaru community organisations from Soraba and Shikaripur taluks visited the village on Thursday and felicitated its prominent leaders. They urged all villages facing similar conditions to take a similar decision in the interest of poor agrarian families.

The resolution has also been well received on social media, with many describing it as worth emulating given the drought situation.

World.title: West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court mulls having tribunals first hear deleted voters seeking re-inclusion
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) orally suggested that lakhs of voters seeking inclusion in the West Bengal electoral roll deserved to be heard first, while appeals for exclusion pending before the Appellate Tribunals could be heard last.

An affidavit filed by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in the Supreme Court in September 2026 revealed that more than 22 lakh voters purged from the electoral roll during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in West Bengal, on grounds such as “logical discrepancies,” had filed appeals challenging their exclusion.

The EC affidavit had said that 16.10 lakh appeals had been filed against inclusion. The poll body had said a total of 38.31 lakh appeals were filed in the tribunals in the State.

The 19 Appellate Tribunals are struggling under a massive backlog, with 37.05 lakh of the 38.31 lakh appeals currently stuck in limbo. At the present pace, clearing the backlog will take more than 12 years, one of the petitioners, Congress leader Prasenjit Bose, has argued.

So far, the Appellate Tribunals, according to EC statistics, have disposed of only 3% of the total appeals filed, and 93% of these disposed-of appeals have resulted in the inclusion of electors in the electoral rolls.

In an oral mentioning, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Mr. Bose, and advocates Prashant Bhushan and Neha Rathi, representing five disentitled voters, said the disentitled voters in the State had already missed both the Assembly elections in May 2026 and the recent by-elections.

The lawyers said these voters should be allowed to cast their vote in the Municipal elections scheduled for November 2026, regardless of whether their appeals were pending before the tribunals.

“Over one lakh appeals were decided by the tribunals in the past six months, of which 93% have been ruled in favour of the deleted voters, ordering their re-inclusion in the voter list. Taking this fact into consideration, voters whose appeals for re-inclusion are pending should be allowed to vote in the municipal elections,” Mr. Bhushan said.

He said the Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Howrah Municipal Corporation elections were coming up soon, and that voters in these areas whose appeals were pending before the tribunals should have their cases decided on a priority basis.

“We are already working on the issue of the pending appeals. We will find a via media (middle path) solution. There are appeals by persons seeking inclusion. They will be taken first... first will be for inclusions,” Chief Justice Surya Kant said orally.

Justice Joymalya Bagchi said the tribunals were “taking time” on the appeals. He remarked that the Court had received feedback intrinsically related to issues such as the architecture of the software, “which we need to thrash out” with the EC. “You see, technology, method and fairness has to match,” Justice Bagchi said, on the working of the Appellate Tribunals in West Bengal.

“But we have missed one election, we are going to miss another,” Mr. Sankaranarayanan said. Justice Bagchi said the Court understood the predicament. “We will make appropriate interventions,” he said.

The Court said the case would most likely be listed on October 16, 2026, on a priority basis, but said October 29, 2026, was a more convenient date.

World.title: Former DMK Minister E.V. Velu, son E.V. Kumaran seek anticipatory bail in lake bed mining case
World.content:
Former Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) Minister E.V. Velu, 76, and his son E.V. Kumaran, 48, have filed anticipatory bail petitions before the Madras High Court in a case registered against them for allegedly excavating 45,72,058 cubic feet of sand from Malappambadi lake in Tiruvannamalai district to level the venue for the party’s north zone youth wing conference held on December 14, 2025.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan on Friday (October 9, 2026) accepted a request made by State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan to grant time till Tuesday (October 13) for filing written objections on behalf of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC). The judge orally advised the prosecution not to take any coercive action until then, since the first petitioner was a septuagenarian.

The petitioners had chosen to seek advance bail, through their counsel Rahul Balaji, after the judge, earlier this week, rejected their plea for ex parte interim relief in two other petitions filed by them, urging the court to quash the First Information Report (FIR) registered against them.

The DVAC registered the FIR on September 24, 2026, on the basis of a complaint lodged by Jayaram Venkatesan from the anti-corruption organisation Arappor Iyakkam. The complainant had alleged that the excavation was carried out on about eight acres of the waterbody in and around November 2025 to level land belonging to a private company of which Mr. Kumaran was one of the directors.

It was claimed that the alleged illegal excavation had resulted in a loss of ₹8.22 crore to the public exchequer. However, both petitioners claimed they were innocent and had not committed any offence as alleged by the complainant. In his petition, Mr. Velu said that there was no overt act attributed to him in the complaint and that there was no specific allegation that he had influenced any government official during his stint as Minister last year.

“The allegation that the petitioner’s son E.V. Kumaran was responsible for the alleged excavation of gravel/lake-bed material is a hypothetical allegation, the mere fact that unauthorised excavation or mining is alleged to have taken place does not, by itself, furnish any basis to attribute the commission of such offence to the petitioner or his son,” his advance bail petition read.

Pointing out that he was the Minister of State Highways, Minor Ports and Public Works departments during the previous DMK regime, Mr. Velu said that even according to the complainant, Malappambadi lake was under the control of the Revenue, Corporation, and geology and mining authorities, none of whom were under his portfolio.

World.title: 9-member SIT formed to probe Uttarakhand Minister's charges against husband
World.content:
A nine-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been constituted to investigate Women and Child Development Minister Rekha Arya's allegations of physical assault, harassment, caste-based slurs and death threats against her husband, Girdhari Lal Sahu, officials said.

A team led by Superintendent of Police (Rural) Jaya Baloni will conduct the investigation.

Speaking to PTI, Ms. Baloni said, “A nine-member SIT has been formed to investigate the incident. We will start the investigation after the Minister is released from the hospital and complete it at the earliest.”

On Thursday (October 15, 2026) evening, Ms. Arya filed an FIR against Mr. Sahu and released a video on a social media platform, accusing him of physical assault, harassment, using caste-based slurs, and issuing death threats.

The FIR was registered on October 15 at the Cantt police station in Dehradun, under relevant sections of law, including three sections of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

Amid an ongoing dispute with his wife, Mr. Sahu on Friday (October 16) released a video accusing the Minister of corruption, claiming that she possesses illegal assets worth ₹210 crore. He demanded that the Chief Minister initiate an investigation by an appropriate agency. However, he did not provide any documentary evidence to support these allegations.

He further claimed that an audio recording, shared by the Minister on Thursday (October 15) evening, was fake, AI-generated and fabricated “to sow discord within the family.” Mr. Sahu dismissed all allegations levelled against him as "baseless".

In the video, Mr. Sahu appealed to Ms. Arya to withdraw the FIR and retract her statement, maintaining that the accusations against him are false.

Meanwhile, on Friday (October 16) evening, state Congress president Ganesh Godiyal issued a video statement and said that if Ms. Arya has been a victim of harassment, then, “as a daughter of Uttarakhand, she has our sympathy.”

“However, serious allegations have been levelled today—specifically, that her husband has amassed proxy-held assets worth ₹210 crore and siphoned off rations intended for the mid-day meals of schoolchildren. Both Rekha Arya and the Chief Minister must provide a clarification regarding these accusations,” said Mr. Godiyal.

He added that given Ms. Arya is a Minister, referring to her as a "helpless woman" would be an insult to the State.

“In light of these grave allegations, and for the sake of public propriety, the Chief Minister should secure the Minister’s resignation and initiate an impartial investigation. The Ankita Bhandari case on one hand and the Rekha Arya case on the other—how long will this continue? The government must answer for the state of women in Uttarakhand and address these serious allegations,” said Mr. Godiyal.

World.title: How a Keralam teacher’s ‘portable chemistry lab’ is sparking students’ interest in experiments
World.content:
Imagine a science teacher holding two pieces of chalk in his hands to explain a chemical reaction in a high school class. As the chalk in one hand is slowly and slightly tilted while the other is held tight, he says, “Suppose these are two test tubes and we are pouring chemicals from one of them into another...”

Not many students would understand the “chemistry” behind it even after such a classroom experience, believes Abhilash Thiruvoth, a Chemistry teacher in the vocational higher secondary wing of the Government Vocational Higher Secondary School for Girls, Nadakkavu, Kozhikode, Keralam.

World.title: Pakistan rules out unconditional talks with Afghanistan
World.content:
• Demands verifiable mechanism to end terrorist attacks from Afghan soil

• FO says no formal Russian mediation initiative currently under discussion

• Warns India that any future aggression will be met with a stronger response

ISLAMABAD: The Foreign Office on Friday said that talks with Afghanistan could not be unconditional, while rejecting suggestions that Islamabad was unwilling to engage with its neighbour and saying it would welcome sincere efforts by friendly countries to help resolve the dispute.

“Pakistan is not shying away from discussions or dialogue, including with representatives of Afghanistan. Pakistan would welcome any sincere efforts by friendly countries that could help address our legitimate security concerns and promoting regional peace and stability,” Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said at the weekly media briefing.

The statement came as Russia recently renewed its readiness to mediate between the two countries, although Islamabad denied the existence of any such initiative.

“At present, I am not aware of any separate, formal Russian mediation initiative being under discussion,” Mr Khan said, adding that Pakistan remained open to engagement that produced tangible results.

Russia, the only country to have formally recognised the Taliban government, has recently renewed its offer to facilitate a settlement if both sides request its involvement.

Moscow’s special envoy for Afghanistan, Zamir Kabulov, had earlier this month made this suggestion after the latest round of the Moscow Format consultations on Oct 5 ended without a joint communiqué because of differences between Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban delegations over references to terrorist networks operating from Afghanistan.

Mr Khan said the absence of an agreed statement at the Moscow Format meeting reflected the Afghan delegation’s unwillingness to accept language on terrorist networks that had been agreed in the previous year’s document.

“The fact that no joint communiqué was issued after the Moscow Format is self-evident that Afghanistan did not accept the formulation which had been acceptable until last year particularly about presence of terrorist network in Afghanistan. This shows that there is reluctance on the part of Afghanistan that terrorism is originating from its soil,” he said.

The failure to get a joint communique highlighted the central obstacle to normalising relations, which is Pakistan’s demand for action against the Tehreek-i-Taliban Paki­stan (TTP) and other terrorist groups it says are using Afghan territory to launch attacks across the border.

The Taliban authorities have avoided taking a categorical position on the TTP and other groups, while rejecting Islamabad’s allegations that Afghanistan is being used as a base for attacks against Pakistan.

The dispute has frustrated international efforts to reduce tensions. Qatar and Turkiye last October helped broker a ceasefire, but subsequent round of talks failed to reach a lasting settlement. Saudi Arabia separately hosted discussions, while China held talks between the two sides in Urumqi in April. None of these efforts could resolve the disagreement over terrorist groups and the measures needed to prevent cross border attacks.

Pakistan’s position, Mr Khan said, was that dialogue would need to be backed by an arrangement that could verify whether terrorist activity against the country had stopped.

“The talks will not be unconditional. Pakistan has been raising the issue of terrorism emanating from Afghanistan at different forums. Unfortunately, the Taliban regime has been taking one step forward and one step backward,” Mr Khan emphasised.

“Pakistan has only one demand that there should be a verifiable mechanism to ensure complete cessation of terrorist activities emanating from Afghan soil against Pakistan,” he said.

‘Stronger response’

Mr Khan reminded India of the response it faced during last year’s military confrontation and warned that any future aggression would be met with an even stronger response.

FO reaction came after Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh a day earlier threatened a bigger strike in the event of any future terrorist attacks.

Singh, while speaking at National Defence Conclave 2026 in Delhi, recalled Operation Sindoor and said that it marked a decisive response to terrorism. He also referred to earlier Indian military operations.

“We reject and condemn the Indian Defence Minister’s provocative remarks entailing a threat of Indian aggression against Pakistan. Such reckless statements reflect India’s hegemonistic mindset and the risks its belligerent posture poses to regional peace and stability in South Asia,” Mr Khan said.

“We wish to remind India of the consequences of its military aggression in May last year, when Pakistan demonstrated both its capability and resolve to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity and gave a fitting reply to Indian aggression,” the FO spokesperson said.

Mr Khan urged New Delhi to draw lessons from the previous confrontation and avoid further escalation.

“India should draw an appropriate lesson from the last year’s experience and abandon its belligerent posture and dangerous rhetoric and act with responsibility for lasting peace in the region,” he said.

Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs3.93 per litre
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3.93 per litre, but left that of high-speed diesel (HSD) unchanged at Rs396.96.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs386.30 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable from Oct 17 (Saturday) to Oct 19 (Monday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Imran being forced into Benazir, Nawaz-style deal, claims Achakzai
World.content:
• Demands authorities disclose whereabouts of Sohail Afridi

• Mengal says those claiming to be framers of Constitution are ‘trampling it’

• TTAP alliance challenges governor’s rule, emergency before Peshawar High Court

PESHAWAR: PTI fou­nder Imran Khan is being forced into an agreement, similar to those given to former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto, Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai claimed on Friday.

The opposition leader was referring to the arrangements whereby the two former PMs went into self-imposed exile following their respective ousters.

Mr Sharif, who was ousted and imprisoned following a military coup by then-army chief Pervez Musharraf, left the country in 2000 following a deal negotiated by Saudi and Lebanese leaders.

Benazir, meanwhile, voluntarily went into self-exile after her party lost the 1997 general elections following her dismissal by then-president Farooq Leg­hari. At the time, her husband Asif Zardari was imprisoned over corruption charges, and was finally released in 2004.

“The same is happening today with the PML-N and PPP in government,” Mr Achakzai said at a news conference at the Peshawar High Court (PHC).

He was accompanied by Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) leaders Sardar Akhtar Mengal and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas.

He said they were in contact with all opposition parties and would soon convene a multi-party conference. Resigning from the assemblies was also an option, he said, adding that they had submitted their demands in response to the offer of negotiations.

“Nowhere in the world is a prisoner denied meetings,” he said, calling for the withdrawal of the “wrong amen­dment”, empow­erment of parliament and the formation of an independent commission to ensure transparent elections.

He said no problem could be resolved until parliament was empowered. Expressing concern over the whereabouts of the KP chief minister and other lawmakers, he demanded that the authorities disclose the chief minister’s whereabouts, calling it their constitutional right to know.

“We stand with the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The people of this province have the first right over its minerals. Regardless of political affiliation, everyone must unite for the homeland,” he said, adding that they would be safer if the country survived.

Mr Mengal said those claiming to be the framers of the Constitution were trampling on it. He questioned the imposition of governor’s rule in KP on the grounds of terrorism, asking whether military operations had improved or worsened conditions in Balochistan.

He said KP’s elected chief minister had been removed, while the provincial assembly speaker and a minister were missing. Those who had won the general elections on Form 47 had become members of the National Assembly, he alleged, adding that the system could not continue this way.

Raja Nasir Abbas, the opposition leader in the Senate, said lawlessness had reached its peak. “You cannot run a country, yet you have occupied a province,” he told reporters, adding that a cabinet member had himself acknowledged that the system had collapsed.

TTAP challenges governor’s rule

Meanwhile on Friday, TTAP leaders challenged the proclamation of emergency and imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa before the

PHC, seeking to have the measures declared unconstitutional and illegal.

The constitutional petition was jointly filed by TTAP Chairman Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Vice Chairman Senator Raja Nasir Abbas, Balochistan National Party-Mengal chief Sardar Akhtar Mengal and Sindh Taraqi Pasand Party leader Syed Zainul Abideen through Advocates Muazzam Butt and Baseem Ahmad Siddiqui.

The court was requested to declare the Oct 11 proclamation of emergency, issued under Articles 232(1) and 234 of the Constitution, unconstitutional and without lawful authority, arguing that the required constitutional conditions had not been met or that the measures exceeded the powers conferred by the Constitution.

They challenged the purported transfer of the KP Assembly’s legislative powers to parliament and the displacement of the elected chief minister and provincial cabinet. They also sought the annulment of executive orders and notifications that depended on the validity of the proclamation.

The petitioners also challenged the establishment of the purported KP Advisory Council and Area Development Secretariat, arguing that these bodies could not exercise powers beyond those conferred by the Constitution or replace established provincial institutions.

They questioned any purported suspension of constitutional provisions, including Article 175(3), unless expressly authorised by the Constitution.

The petitioners sought annulment of the Oct 11 notification concerning the deployment of armed forces in the province to the extent where it violated Article 245, failed to meet constitutional requirements or exceeded the scope of the provision.

They also sought directions to ensure that elected representatives and constitutionally established institutions in KP were not unlawfully prevented from performing their functions and that no elected representative was detained or restrained except in accordance with the Constitution.

Pending a final decision, they sought interim relief to suspend or restrain the impugned measures to prevent the displacement of elected institutions, transfer of legislative authority, creation of parallel executive structures or other irreparable harm, subject to the court’s assessment of constitutional requirements and public safety.

Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

World.title: ‘Pakistan among 10 states bearing brunt of hunger crisis’
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan is among the 10 countries bearing the brunt of the global hunger crisis, with climate-related disasters, economic hardship, displacement and shrinking humanitarian funding pushing vulnerable communities deeper into food insecurity, according to a new report released by international humanitarian organisation Action Against Hunger.

The report, Ten Largest Global Food Crises, released on Friday in connection with World Food Day, warns that an estimated 10.6 million people in Pakistan will require humanitarian assistance in 2026, despite ongoing recovery efforts and improvements in some macroeconomic indicators.

Globally, approximately 177 million people live in the 10 countries where hunger is most concentrated, while acute hunger has doubled over the past decade, affecting 266 million people across 47 countries, says the report.

The countries facing the largest food crises are Nigeria, Congo, Sudan, Yemen, Afghan­istan, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Pakistan, South Sudan and Syria.

Report sees 10.6m Pakistanis needing humanitarian assistance in 2026

In Pakistan, persistent poverty, high food inflation, rising living costs, limited employment opportunities and declining household incomes continue to erode families’ purchasing power. Unfavourable agricultural prices and broader economic instability have further undermined livelihoods, leaving millions struggling to afford adequate food.

As humanitarian needs outstrip available resources, vulnerable households are increasingly resorting to damaging coping strategies, including cutting food consumption, selling productive assets and withdrawing children from school to cope with financial pressures.

The report cautions that these measures may provide temporary relief but can deepen poverty, undermine children’s education and nutrition, and weaken families’ ability to recover from future shocks.

Limited access to healthcare, nutrition services, clean water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), and social protection is compounding the crisis, particularly in rural and disaster-affected areas. Persistent poverty and acute malnutrition remain major drivers of humanitarian needs, while cuts to support services and livelihood programmes are further eroding community resilience.

Pakistan’s exposure to climate-related disasters remains a major source of food insecurity. Recurrent floods, droughts, heatwaves, glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) and increasingly erratic monsoon rainfall have damaged infrastructure, reduced agricultural production and weakened livestock-dependent livelihoods.

Crop losses and prolonged dry spells have also increased households’ reliance on markets for food at a time when many families have limited purchasing power. Several districts are experiencing prolonged drought conditions, adding to concerns about agricultural output and rural incomes.

The report warns that seasonal hardships can intensify these pressures. The lean season from December 2025 to March 2026, characterised in some areas by extended winter conditions and heavy snowfall, was identified as a period likely to worsen food insecurity by restricting access to markets and essential resources.

Insecurity and regional tensions are adding another layer of pressure to Pakistan’s already fragile food security situation.

According to the report, localised insecurity in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan continues to disrupt livelihoods, restrict access to markets and hamper humanitarian operations.

Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

World.title: SC questions ‘lofty expectations’ in criminal cases
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court has taken exception to a prevalent practice in criminal trials which, it said, defied normal human capability and natural perception, and observed that eyewitness accounts should reflect genuine human observation rather than physically impossible details concerning firearm incidents.

“To expect mathematical precision regarding the number of firearm shots or the exact location of injuries from eyewitnesses exposed to a horrific event is both unnatural and impractical,” observed Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim in a judgement he authored.

Justice Ibrahim was a member of a three-judge SC bench headed by Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, which took up criminal appeals filed by Muhammad Azhar and the state challenging a Sept 13, 2021, Lahore High Court, Bahawalpur, ruling.

The SC, however, rejected the criminal appeal in the 2017 murder case, upholding Muhammad Azhar’s conviction for killing Sakhian Bibi.

Expecting mathematical precision from eyewitnesses exposed to traumatic events is ‘unnatural and impractical’, Justice Ibrahim holds

“In criminal jurisprudence, human behaviour should not be subjected to a fixed formula, nor should every witness be expected to react to, observe or retain events in an identical manner,” the judgement said.

The incident occurred on Jan 11, 2017, when the appellant allegedly entered the victim’s home armed with a .30-bore pistol, seeking the complainant’s uncle in connection with ongoing civil litigation. When the victim said her uncle was not present, the petitioner opened fire, discharging five shots that struck her chest, abdomen and right arm.

The additional sessions judge, Minch­inabad, convicted the petitioner and sentenced him to death, with Rs200,000 in compensation payable to the legal heirs. The LHC, Bahawalpur, later commuted the death sentence to life imprisonment, prompting both the petitioner’s appeal and the state’s petition for enhancement of the sentence.

“We frequently observe prosecution witnesses deposing with microscopic precision, as if watching events in slow motion, describing the exact trajectory and anatomical landing site of each individual bullet discharged from a firearm,” the judgement observed. It is humanly impossible for an eyewitness exposed to the sudden terror and high stress of a deadly attack to track a high-velocity bullet in mid-air and confirm precisely where each shot strikes the victim’s body, it noted.

The judge emphasised that every individual reacts differently to a sudden traumatic situation: while one person may observe details, another may freeze or lose awareness of the occurrence. In a sudden traumatic event, when multiple gunshots ring out within a few seconds and a mother is murdered in cold blood before her son’s eyes, a minor divergence regarding the exact number of firearm shots or the precise entry point of each bullet is evidence of natural and reasonable human limitations, he observed.

It is common knowledge that most individuals are not frequently exposed to dangerous, life-threatening situations, and the sudden brandishing of a weapon induces an atmosphere of shock and fear, according to the judgement.

In such stressful encounters, human cognitive and perceptual capacities are severely impaired, the judgement said. To substantiate this point, it cited renowned cognitive psychologist Elizabeth Loftus, who had stated that a witness confronted by an assailant brandishing a firearm involuntarily fixes their attention almost exclusively on the weapon itself. This cognitive phenomenon, known as “attentional tunnelling”, limits the observer’s capacity to process or recall surrounding details, the judgement said.

Trial courts should bear these limitations in mind when scrutinising eyewitness accounts claiming microscopic accuracy despite the stressful circumstances, Justice Ibrahim observed.

The judgement expected lower courts to assess witnesses in the light of the circumstances of each case, observing that, under the golden principles of criminal jurisprudence, no piece of evidence should be considered in isolation; rather, all evidence should be evaluated cumulatively alongside other available evidence.

World.title: Terrorism has no link with Baloch values, says Bugti
World.content:
QUETTA: Condemning a recent terrorist attack in Dasht Goran, Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti said on Friday that the government had always maintained that such acts have nothing to do with Baloch values, rather were purely terrorism.

He was responding to points raised by lawmakers on various issues in the Balochistan Assembly.

Earlier, MPA Mir Jahanzeb Mengal, speaking on a point of order, said that “Fitna al-Hindustan” had attacked the house of Mir Qambar Khan Mengal in Dasht Goran at 6am. He said the firing continued until 4pm, leaving Ahmed Nawaz Mengal dead and another person injured.

“This is my house, and my mother and sisters are there. This is not Balochiyat. If anyone is so keen on fighting, let them specify the place, field and time. The Balochistan chief minister should take notice of the incident,” he said.

Condemns Dasht Goran attack; directs district administrations to inspect school and college buildings in Balochistan

CM Bugti said the people of the province were increasingly realising that the Baloch were being pushed into a futile conflict. “What kind of tradition allows the killing of passengers and unarmed people?” he asked.

Asma Jattak case

Then, speaking about the high-profile Asma Jattak case, he said the government had been in contact with her family.

“I have said before that the matter is sensitive and cannot be discussed on the floor of the assembly,” he said.

The case he was referring to revolves around the murder of Ms Jattak’s father in August this year. The woman in question was abducted in 2025. After being freed, she levelled allegations against an influential individual, accusing him of threatening her family. The same day, her father was shot dead outside their residence.

Referring to remarks by lawmakers during a previous sitting, the chief minister said it was inappropriate to name an individual, whose father had also served as the provincial chief minister, and allege on the assembly floor that those responsible for the killing of Asma Jattak’s father were present in the house.

“I have reports from the security agencies, and the information provided by the member concerned is incorrect,” he said.

School safety

Referring to the recent school roof collapse incident in Peshawar where several children lost their lives, former chief minister Dr Abdul Malik Baloch urged the chief minister to direct the Education Department, the Communications and Works (C&W) Department and local councillors to inspect all government and private school buildings across Balochistan.

He said officials should visit schools in every area and ensure that any building found to be dilapidated was closed until it could be made safe.

In response, the chief minister said he had directed authorities to inspect the buildings of all schools and colleges across the province.

Speaker Abdul Khaliq Khan Achak­­zai noted that because madressahs accommodate children, their buildings also require strict safety inspections.

Published in Dawn, October 17th, 2026

World.title: Millions may be forced to move as climate change hits South Asia: UN
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Climate change is threatening livelihoods and forcing people from their homes across South Asia, but technology and government action could help limit the damage, the UN migration chief said on Friday.

Rising seas, flooding and drought threaten homes and farmland, Amy Pope, director general of the International Organisation for Migration (IOM), said during a visit to New Delhi.

In the Himalayas, she pointed to Nepal’s Aug 26 disaster, when a mountain and glacier collapse triggered deadly flooding, where IOM sent humanitarian aid to help.

In a worst-case scenario, up to 40.5 million people in South Asia may be forced to move by 2050, according to IOM.

Rising seas, flooding, drought threaten homes and farmland, warns IOM chief

“When they can’t produce food, when they can’t feed their livestock, it increases the likelihood of displacement,” said Pope. “The first adaptation is often for people to move.”

Pope said climate change was also accelerating urbanisation in India.

“As people seek shelter from heat, they’re going into urban centres,” she said.

Migration as a tool

The risks are particularly acute in South Asia, where a vast population and limited resources leave many communities vulnerable.

“There’s a lack of urgency globally about the risks that vulnerable communities are facing,” Amy Pope said, warning that funding to help residents prepare for climate change remained inadequate.

“The cost of a humanitarian disaster is in the billions. The cost of investing in some of the resilience measures can be far less,” she said.

Better data and artificial intelligence could help governments identify communities at risk before disaster strikes, Pope added.

“With the advancements in AI forecasting, you can now better anticipate those communities that are at high risk of displacement,” the IOM chief said.

By combining weather forecasts with information about local livelihoods, authorities can identify which communities most need help.

“If you know a community is at risk, we don’t need to wait until they’re displaced to respond,” she said.

Measures could include improving farming methods, training people for other jobs and, where necessary, relocating communities repeatedly hit by floods or drought.

Finding the money for such programmes is a major obstacle, Pope said, with governments often struggling to navigate the systems available to fund climate adaptation.

India’s investments in early-warning systems, disaster response and technology offer grounds for optimism, she said. But no government can meet the scale of the challenge alone.

International migration can also help people earn a living while filling labour shortages abroad.

However, Pope warned that growing demand for workers must be matched by safe, legal routes to employment.

World.title: Zelensky smiles on being asked whether Trump  is scapegoating him
World.content:
BRUSSELS: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zele­­nsky gave a knowing smile and stayed mum on Friday when asked if the US president was scapegoating him for troubles in the US.

“This is my answer,” Zelensky said, as journalists broke into laughter at a press conference in Brussels after he met EU leaders.

Zelensky had been asked if Donald Trump was lashing out at the Ukrainian leader as a way to deflect from his own political strife ahead of next month’s midterm elections as he is bogged down with Iran and diesel prices have soared.

The question came after Trump said he found it easier to deal with Russian President Vla­dimir Putin than Zelensky as ties have soured with Kyiv.

“Yesterday was a thousand drones in Ukraine, a thousand, but the American side said that it is difficult to speak with Zelensky, it’s less difficult to manage with Putin,” Zelensky said.
