However, according to Gergerlioğlu, a lawmaker from Turkey’s ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP), who attended the meeting, chose to remain silent.

Araz Aliyev believes Ankara’s reaction was inevitable. In his view, under Erdoğan, Turkey presents itself as a defender of “moderate Islam” and Muslims, while religious voters form one of the ruling party’s main support bases. “In this situation, Baku’s decision could not go unanswered,” he says.

Javid Agha, meanwhile, points out that Leyla Şahin Usta was among those whom Azerbaijan’s ruling New Azerbaijan Party (YAP) criticised in its statement. In the late 1990s, a headscarf ban prevented her from continuing her studies in Istanbul. Şahin Usta later lost her case against Turkey at the European Court of Human Rights and completed her education in Vienna.

“These bans did not stop her. Today, she is among those who govern Turkey. The authors of the statement should at least have familiarised themselves with her biography,” Agha says.

Sheikh-ul-Islam: “Consultations could have taken place, but they did not”

Allahshukur Pashazade, chairman of the Caucasus Muslims Board, has also commented on the situation. In an interview with Real TV, he acknowledged that the authorities had not consulted the religious organisation he heads before making the decision:

“I deeply regret that consultations could have taken place on this issue in advance, but they did not.”

At the same time, Pashazade supported the government’s position. He said the school uniform regulations do not mention the word “hijab” and that the country has no ban on wearing it. Children can study in hijabs at madrasas, he added, “but a different decision was taken regarding state schools”.

The Sheikh-ul-Islam stressed that “religion is separate from the state, and school is separate from religion”. He also accused certain “internal and external forces” of politicising the issue and trying to turn citizens against the state.

Araz Aliyev sees Pashazade’s statement as evidence that the authorities made the decision hastily:

“If the decision had been carefully considered and prepared over many years, the authorities should have consulted someone. It appears they made the decision in haste.”

For more on the legal aspects of the hijab ban, protests at schools and detentions, see JAMnews’ earlier report.

How will relations develop?

None of the experts interviewed expects Azerbaijan and Turkey to break off their alliance. However, they all believe the chill between the two countries will persist for some time.

Araz Aliyev believes the tensions will remain at the political level and gradually ease:

“Turkey needs Azerbaijan, while Azerbaijan needs Turkey even more in terms of national security, the economy and defence. Companies close to the leadership in both countries may face pressure from one another, but I do not believe their alliance will be threatened. After some time, we will hear declarations of brotherhood again.”

He notes that the two countries have weathered similar crises in the past. In particular, tensions in the late 2000s, when Turkey and Armenia were discussing protocols to normalise relations, led to Turkish flags being taken down in Baku. Aliyev believes the summit of the Organisation of Turkic States, which is expected to take place in Turkey at the end of the month, could indicate the direction in which relations between Baku and Ankara will develop.

Gergerlioğlu also does not expect Erdoğan to distance himself from Baku solely over the hijab issue. He says Ankara places much greater importance on revenue from the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline, Turkey’s ambition to play a leading role in the “Turkic world” and the support of its nationalist-conservative electorate.

“Behind closed doors, they will probably say politely: ‘Wouldn’t it have been better not to introduce such a ban?’ However, if Aliyev begins openly supporting Israel, Turkey will also start signalling its discontent with the relationship more openly.”

The MP also points to declining electoral support for the ruling party. He claims that some voters dissatisfied with the AKP’s “two-faced” policy towards Israel backed the New Welfare Party in the last election. In his view, the hijab issue could deepen this discontent further.

Javid Agha reaches a similar conclusion. He believes that no matter how often Erdoğan repeats the slogan “one nation, two states”, he will have to take into account the views of the religious-conservative electorate that forms the foundation of his political support and adjust his position accordingly.

Fidan’s statements in Baku also offer insight into this diplomatic strategy. Ankara does not deny that problems exist, but seeks to move discussions about them out of the public arena and into closed-door diplomatic channels. So far, however, there are no signs that Baku intends to make concessions either on the hijab issue or on its relations with Israel.

Strained relations between Turkey and Azerbaijan

World.title: Millions spent on Patriarch’s funeral: scandal involving Georgia’s former culture minister Tinatin Rukhadze
World.content:
Scandal involving former officials in Georgia

On 14 October 2026, Davit Okitashvili, a supporter of the Georgian Dream party, publicly accused former Culture Minister Tinatin Rukhadze of misusing funds allocated for the funeral of the Patriarch of Georgia and called on the prosecutor’s office to launch an investigation. Okitashvili also criticised former State Security Service chief Mamuka Mdinaradze, whom he described as Rukhadze’s political patron.

Other Georgian Dream supporters also responded to Okitashvili’s allegations. Opposition figures believe such attacks on former senior officials may be intended to pave the way for their arrests.

How much did the Patriarch’s funeral cost?

Patriarch Ilia II was buried on 22 March 2026. The government allocated a total of 5.59 million lari to organise the funeral, distributing the funds among six government agencies. The largest share — 3 million lari — went to the Ministry of Culture, which Tinatin Rukhadze headed at the time.

It later emerged that the authorities had not spent more than half of the allocated funds. On 8 May, the government revised the funding to reflect actual expenditure, reducing the total to 2.56 million lari.

Georgian minister quits politics shortly after ex-PM’s accusations

From ‘crown prince’ to prisoner: Irakli Garibashvili’s break with Georgia’s ruling party

Patriarch’s funeral: farewell ceremony of unprecedented scale in Tbilisi. Photos/videos

The Ministry of Culture spent just 722,600 lari of the 3 million lari originally allocated to it. The remaining 2.28 million lari went unspent.

However, it remains unclear exactly how the ministry spent the 722,600 lari: who received the money, what services they provided and how transparently the ministry selected contractors.

September: first questions and the prime minister’s response

Questions about spending on the Patriarch’s funeral emerged in September, following an investigative report by the Pirveli television channel.

Acting Culture Minister Mikheil Kiknadze initially said that the audit documents reflected the shortcomings investigators had identified. However, he later added: “I did not say that there had been any violations.”

Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze also commented on the issue on 14 September. He said the Ministry of Culture had spent only 722,000 lari of the 3 million lari allocated to it.

“If anyone had wanted to steal the money, they could easily have taken all three million,” Kobakhidze said.

He also made the following promise:

“This is preliminary information. I will examine the matter in greater detail and provide the public with a detailed account.”

The Patriarchate defends Rukhadze

On 16 September, Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze, head of the Patriarchate’s public relations service, issued a statement.

He said the Patriarchate had known from the outset that a significant portion of the money allocated for the funeral would remain unspent.

“During that period, we were in frequent contact with Ms Tika Rukhadze, and we knew from her that most organisations and individuals who provided various services had declined any remuneration or payment,” Jaghmaidze wrote.

He expressed hope that people would stop using the Patriarch’s name as a pretext for unfounded accusations and slander.

What links Tika Rukhadze to Tikhart?

According to Transparency International Georgia, Tinatin Rukhadze earned 410,000 lari as a consultant for Tikhart, an event management company, in the two years before she became culture minister.

The organisation also reports that Tikhart secured government contracts worth a total of 3.8 million lari through direct procurement, bypassing competitive tenders.

These circumstances raise questions about whether the company also received payment for organising the Patriarch’s funeral. However, no publicly available information confirms that it did.

Transparency International Georgia has called on the Ministry of Culture to disclose who received the 722,600 lari spent on the funeral and specify which services they provided.

Another problem is that the government does not have to disclose procurement information for purchases financed through the government’s reserve fund. This makes it harder for the public to scrutinise how the authorities spend public money.

The minister’s resignation and a new political climate

Tinatin Rukhadze became culture minister in October 2024. On 28 July 2026, she left the post, citing health reasons. No evidence has established a link between her resignation and the allegations concerning funeral expenditure.

On 15 September, Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze appointed Maia Bitadze, a Georgian Dream MP, as culture minister, specifically praising her integrity.

Around the same time, Mamuka Mdinaradze also left his political post as head of the State Security Service. Rukhadze and Mdinaradze subsequently became targets of coordinated public attacks.

October: accusations from a Georgian Dream supporter

On 14 October, Davit Okitashvili, president of the Georgian Chamber of Culture and an active Georgian Dream supporter, publicly accused Tinatin Rukhadze of obstructing his projects and damaging his reputation. He also described Mamuka Mdinaradze as the former minister’s patron.

Okitashvili raised questions about the cost of the Patriarch’s funeral and called on the prosecutor’s office and the State Audit Office to investigate the spending. In a post, he asked Rukhadze:

“Ms Tika, where did the millions go?!”

Other Georgian Dream representatives supported Okitashvili’s post, including party activist and MP Dimitri Samkharadze.

What does Mamuka Mdinaradze have to do with it?

Okitashvili did not limit his attacks to the former culture minister.

He claimed that Mamuka Mdinaradze had acted as Rukhadze’s political patron. According to Okitashvili, Mdinaradze helped secure her appointment as minister, and she subsequently acted under his influence.

In an interview with Palitranews on 15 October, Okitashvili repeated these allegations. He also claimed that both Rukhadze and Mdinaradze had betrayed Georgian Dream.

However, he noted that the prosecutor’s office had not contacted him.

Georgian Dream representatives also responded to Okitashvili’s accusations.

MP Tengiz Sharmanashvili said the prosecutor’s office should ask Okitashvili what evidence he had. If his claims proved credible, investigators should question those involved, including Rukhadze and Mdinaradze.

Opposition warns of possible arrests

The opposition also reacted to the October developments.

Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Coalition for Change, said Okitashvili’s statements might be intended to prepare the public for the possible arrests of Tinatin Rukhadze and Mamuka Mdinaradze.

Gvaramia suggested that Bidzina Ivanishvili could be behind the process.

Ana Tsitlidze, a representative of the United National Movement, accused Rukhadze and Bakur Bakuradze, the former director general of Rustavi 2, of embezzling funds allocated for the Patriarch’s funeral. She also suggested that authorities might arrest Mamuka Mdinaradze.

Former MP Eka Beselia suspected that Okitashvili’s statement might form part of a pre-planned process. She said that if an investigation began immediately after his statement, it would confirm her suspicions.

World.title: ‘Deadly consequences’: How lack of proper prison in Abkhazia leads to further crimes
World.content:
The recent murder of a Russian tourist has exposed problems with prison sentences in Abkhazia. Edgar Abukhba, who stands accused of murdering Amina Bikbova, received a nine-year sentence for a previous serious crime. In practice, however, he served only half that time. This proved fatal for his next victim.

Amina’s murder prompted Abkhazian society to take a closer look at how courts enforce their rulings. It emerged that in Abkhazia, a sentence tells you very little about how long someone will actually spend in prison. The republic has no proper prison, and a complicated system of “penitentiary arithmetic” determines how much time a person spends behind bars. Even those who apply the rules struggle to make sense of them.

One last coffee

Amina Bikbova’s family had a rule: call her mother every evening. The 26-year-old followed it without fail when she travelled to Abkhazia with her friend Adila for a holiday in September 2026. But one evening, she did not call and failed to answer her phone either. The next day, her phone remained silent. Her family then realised that something serious had happened.

Amina Bikbova

The circumstances surrounding Amina’s final day are known from accounts given by her family and witness testimony reported by Abkhazian and Russian media. Amina and Adila met Edgar Abukhba, a 25-year-old fruit seller. A couple of days later, he invited Amina for coffee. Adila says she tried to talk her friend out of going, but failed. Amina went to meet Edgar and never returned.

During his initial questioning, he denied any wrongdoing. He claimed that he and Amina had simply had coffee, after which she got into someone’s car and drove away. Investigators quickly disproved this account, and Edgar admitted that they had argued, that he had strangled Amina and left her body in bushes beside the road.

A familiar name

Edgar Abukhba

For Abkhazians who follow local crime reports, the surname Abukhba sounded familiar. In July 2019, a 24-year-old Russian tourist suffered a brutal attack in central Sukhum. Her assailants beat, raped and robbed her. Everyone familiar with the case said they had rarely encountered such brutality. Authorities arrested Edgar Abukhba on suspicion of the crime. The case took more than two years to reach court, and in 2021 a judge sentenced him to nine years in prison.

If the nine-year sentence is counted from 2019, when Abukhba entered pre-trial detention, he should not have been released before 2028. Yet by the summer of 2026, he was already selling fruit in Gagra.

Sentences without a prison

Court rulings specify the regime under which a convicted person must serve their sentence, and this affects the time they spend in prison. But Abkhazia has no prison colony with different security regimes, which creates confusion. Officials recalculate sentences differently depending on how much time a prisoner has spent under various conditions. The final figure depends on the coefficient they apply and can differ significantly from the court’s verdict.

Got that? No, of course not. For anyone unfamiliar with the system, it is almost impossible to understand. Even staff at the relevant institutions struggle to explain on the spot how they calculate a particular sentence, how long a specific prisoner will serve and when they will be released.

Perhaps this explains why a man who, on paper, received a nine-year prison sentence attacked another woman long before that term had expired.

Leniency vs prudence

There is another legal complication in Edgar Abukhba’s case. He was still a minor when he committed his first crime, and under Abkhazian law, courts must not take juvenile convictions into account in the future.

There are two opposing views on this rule.

The logic of juvenile justice holds that a teenager’s actions should not determine the rest of their life. But this approach conflicts with public safety concerns, which suggest that authorities cannot simply ignore a proven threat posed by an individual.

Many countries face this dilemma, but they also assess risks before releasing offenders and supervise them afterwards. They may also restrict where former prisoners can work or live and impose other measures. Abkhazia, however, has no such safeguards in place.

A tarnished reputation

Cynical as it may sound, Abkhazia’s tourism sector — and, consequently, its budget — can also be counted among the “victims” of this tragedy.

Abkhazia effectively lives off Russian tourists, who provide the republic’s main source of income. Its reputation as a safe holiday destination is vital to its survival. Now, Amina Bikbova’s murder has left a major black mark on that reputation. This is particularly troubling because it is not the first attack on tourists.

Tourists may forgive reckless taxi drivers or poor service. But they are unlikely to accept the idea that killers who have not served their full sentences can freely walk the streets in search of new victims.

Many Abkhazian lawyers believe the authorities should publish a breakdown of Edgar Abukhba’s first sentence, including the coefficients they applied and his release date. In other words, they should at least explain why he regained his freedom so quickly. Perhaps the authorities should also review the system for calculating prison sentences. Better still, they should finally build a proper prison colony so that no one has to perform these calculations in the first place.

The public, meanwhile, wants an open trial in this case. People are waiting for an explanation of how this mysterious coefficient can allow rapists and murderers to walk free earlier than petty thieves.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

World.title: Chronicles of Victory: First VP Mehriban Aliyeva shares post in connection with terror committed by Armenia in Ganja on October 17, 2020 (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. The Azerbaijani Army launched a counter-offensive operation, later called the "Iron Fist," on September 27, 2020, in response to the large-scale provocation of the Armenian armed forces along the frontline.The 44-day second Karabakh war ended with the liberation of Azerbaijan’s territories from nearly 30-year Armenian occupation and the restoration of territorial integrity.

On October 17, 2020, First Vice-President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Mehriban Aliyeva made a post on her official Instagram page in connection with the terror committed by the Armenian side in Ganja.

Trend presents the post:

"How one can be an insane beast to give another order on missile attack of civilian quarters of the sleeping city where there is no any military infrastructure?

Perfidious attack on Ganja done in the night is not only the evidence of fascist nature of the Armenian authorities and their lack of principles, but unveils also the total helplessness of the aggressor in front of the Azerbaijani Army.

Targeted attacks against peaceful citizens are the crime against humanity. And, to remain indifferent means to be the accomplice of this crime!

I express my deep condolences to the families and beloved ones of those killed in the aftermath of this tragedy, and I wish the soonest recovery to all injured ones.

May Allah bless our people, our Motherland and our President! Karabakh is Azerbaijan!"

World.title: Chronicles of Victory: President Ilham Aliyev addresses nation on October 17, 2020 (PHOTO/VIDEO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. The Azerbaijani Army launched a counter-offensive operation, later called the "Iron Fist," on September 27, 2020, in response to the large-scale provocation of the Armenian armed forces along the frontline.The 44-day second Karabakh war ended with the liberation of Azerbaijan’s territories from nearly 30-year Armenian occupation and the restoration of territorial integrity.

President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev has addressed the nation.

Trend presents the address.

Nationwide address of President Ilham Aliyev: Dear fellow compatriots!

Today, the fascist leadership of Armenia committed yet another war crime. The cities of Ganja and Mingachevir came under rocket fire. As a result of this cowardly shelling, our compatriots have been killed and wounded. May Allah rest all our martyrs in peace and send healing to our wounded compatriots!

This once again shows the fascist nature of the Armenian leadership. This is not the first time our cities have come under fire. Armenia fires on Tartar, Aghdam, Goranboy, Aghjabadi, and other cities practically every day. As a result of this fire, our citizens have been killed and wounded, and more than 2,000 houses have been destroyed or seriously damaged. However, these cowardly actions cannot break the will of the Azerbaijani people.

Armenian leadership is committing a war crime. Shooting at civilians, including firing missiles, is a war crime, and they must and will bear responsibility for this crime. We are giving their answer on the battlefield. We are avenging and will continue to avenge the deaths of our martyrs and innocent civilians on the battlefield. We have never fought or will ever wage a war against the civilian population. We are not Armenians. We have our own way, we have our own cause, and all the Azerbaijani people are united around this cause. All the Azerbaijani people are showing solidarity and patriotism.

The victorious Azerbaijani Army is driving and will continue to drive the enemies away from our lands in the ongoing battles. I said that if they do not leave our lands of their own free will, we will chase them away like dogs, and we are doing that. Every day, the victorious Azerbaijani Army liberates new strategic locations, new heights, and new settlements from the occupiers. Our revenge takes place on the battlefield.

These days, from 27 September to the present, a crushing blow has been dealt to Armenia's military potential. I just want to bring some figures to the attention of our citizens. I must say that the list I will provide is incomplete. An even larger amount of enemy equipment has been destroyed, and, of course, it is impossible to calculate it accurately during the battle. However, the figures I will quote show explicitly that we have gained a complete advantage on the battlefield and have almost completely destroyed the military-technical potential of Armenia. The question is, where do so many weapons and so much equipment come from to Armenia? Armenia's military budget is well known. Armenia's state budget is also well known. Armenia is a bankrupt country. The country's foreign debt accounts for 60–70 percent of the country's gross domestic product. The country's foreign exchange reserves are only $1.5 billion, which are bank reserves. That is, it is not free funds. What money are they getting these weapons and equipment with? The equipment we have destroyed and taken as booty so far is worth at least $2 billion. But there is still more in their hands – in the occupied territories and in the territory of Armenia. The question is who is arming them. In some cases, we are criticized that we are arming ourselves; we are buying weapons, and this can allegedly aggravate the situation and turn it in an unacceptable direction. The question is what about Armenia’s armament. Where do so many weapons and hardware come from in this poor country? Today, they are smuggling weapons and equipment using some smuggling schemes. And they are very dangerous and very destructive weapons. Therefore, we want answers to these questions, and I am sure we will get them.

I would like to bring to the attention of my people some of the Armenian equipment the Azerbaijani Army has destroyed in recent days. Thus, the list of the destroyed Armenian equipment includes: 234 tanks have been destroyed, 36 tanks have been taken as military booty, 49 infantry fighting vehicles have been destroyed, 24 have been taken as military booty, 16 self-propelled artillery pieces have been destroyed, 190 cannons of various calibers, two "Hurricane" systems, one TOS flamethrower, two "Elbrus" operational tactical missile complexes, one "Tochka-U," 35 "OSA" anti-aircraft missile systems, three "TOR" anti-aircraft missile complexes, five "KUB" and "KRUG" anti-aircraft missile complexes, nine radio-electronic combat systems, two S-300 anti-aircraft missile systems, 196 trucks have been destroyed, and 98 have been taken as booty. Anyone, any specialist, can calculate the price of this equipment from open media. We must, and we will find answers to these questions.

The glorious Azerbaijani Army is successfully continuing its salvation mission. In recent days, I have informed my people and announced the names of the newly liberated villages. Today, with a feeling of great satisfaction and joy, I want to convey to my dear people the names of more settlements that have been liberated. The following settlements of Fuzuli district have been liberated from the occupiers – Gochahmadli village, Chiman village, Juvarli village, Pirahmadli village, Musabayli village, Ishigli village, Dadali village, and Fuzuli city. The city of Fuzuli has been liberated from the occupiers; Fuzuli is ours, and Karabakh is Azerbaijan!

I heartily congratulate all the people of Azerbaijan on this occasion. I heartily congratulate the people of Fuzuli on this occasion. Many years of longing for native land are coming to an end. We are honorably fulfilling our mission, restoring and will restore the territorial integrity of our country. The battles for Fuzuli were very hard. Time will pass, and books and papers will be written about these battles. It was a battle that required great professionalism, skill, courage, and self-sacrifice. Because during these 30 years, the enemy has built such a strong fortification on the line of contact that some people thought that it was impossible to liberate the city of Fuzuli from occupation. Even the most well-known military experts were of the opinion that it would take months to capture Fuzuli and free it from occupation, and whether the operation would be successful was still in question. However, the victorious Azerbaijani Army was able to cope with this glorious mission, and most of the villages of Fuzuli district and the city of Fuzuli have been liberated from the enemy in a short time. When we talk about the city of Fuzuli, of course, we should all know that there is nothing left of the city, no monuments, not a single safe building. For 30 years, it was in the hands of wild beasts, in the hands of predators, in the hands of jackals. All the buildings have been demolished, our religious sites have been demolished, everything has been looted, the roofs of the houses, the windows, the belongings – everything. It was as if a wild tribe had taken over the city. The remains of the city of Fuzuli are a manifestation of Armenian fascism and a witness to Armenian fascism.

We will return to Fuzuli, we will rebuild and landscape all the villages. Life will return to those villages. Just like in the past when the Azerbaijani Army liberated 22 villages of Fuzuli district, including Horadiz settlement, under the leadership of the great leader. Look at how beautiful this place is now. Horadiz settlement has become a very prosperous and modern town. Fuzuli people live in liberated villages. I can say that about half of the population of Fuzuli has been settled in the villages liberated so far, but more villages inhabited by Fuzuli people have been liberated today. Life will return there; they will return there, they will live there; they will visit the graves of their ancestors. The call to prayer will be heard in the mosques to be restored there. We are fulfilling our glorious mission. I am confident that the glorious Azerbaijani Army will continue to drive the invaders away from our lands.

The Fuzuli operation is quite symbolic. Azerbaijan has regained its historical and ancient settlement and ensured the return of tens of thousands of people to these places. At the same time, from a strategic point of view, the splitting of several lines of defense on the line of contact with Fuzuli gives us another strategic advantage. Because our armed forces located in the direction of Fuzuli have been fighting there these days. Of course, it is not a secret now where we were able to enter Fuzuli from. As a result of tremendous military professionalism and courage, we were able to liberate Fuzuli from the occupiers. Before that, the city of Jabrayil was liberated from the invaders. Before that, Hadrut was liberated from the occupiers. Many villages of Khojavand and Jabrayil districts, including Fuzuli district, were liberated from occupation. Only after that were we able to liberate the city of Fuzuli from the occupiers.

In the latest stage, the enemy has dropped his guns and fled. Today, I can say with full responsibility that the Fuzuli operation will be included in military books. In fact, not only the Fuzuli operation but also other operations. According to the information I have today, military experts are already clearly saying that the Azerbaijani Army is an army with great combat capability and technical support.

It is a historic day today. The date of October 17 will remain forever, not only in the memory of the Fuzuli people but also in the history of the Azerbaijani state. Today, we, all the people of Azerbaijan, are writing the brightest page of our people and our state together. Today, we are writing this glorious history of solidarity, mutual support, and unity. We are lucky to live in these moments. Unfortunately, tens of thousands of our refugees and IDPs who were looking forward to these moments did not live to see these days. But I am sure that their spirit is happy today because their native lands have been liberated from the occupiers.

Despite the fact that the cowardly, treacherous, and vile enemy commits war crimes, fires on the civilian population, and kills children as a result of today’s shooting, I want to say again that we must not take revenge on civilians. We are taking revenge on the battlefield. The blood of our martyrs and civilians does not and will not remain unavenged. I warn the fascist leadership of Armenia again – leave the remaining lands of your own accord. We will throw you out of there anyway. There will be no trace of them left on those lands. We will drive them out of our lands to the end. Let them leave of their own accord!

He did not want to give up Fuzuli, even though he understood perfectly well that he would not be able to keep it. He did not want to give up Jabrayil. Yesterday, the day before yesterday, and today, successful operations were carried out in the direction of Jabrayil and strategic heights were taken. I do not want to say anything about that yet. I do not want to get ahead of the events. But the victorious Azerbaijani Army is achieving and will continue to achieve its goals; our territorial integrity is being restored and will be fully restored. No force can stop us. No force can stand against the will of the Azerbaijani people. Everyone should know this. No one can stand in front of us. Let the predatory Armenian state vacate our lands. After that, a ceasefire will be ensured. A ceasefire was declared, but Ganja was bombed a day later. And which part of it? A residential settlement. Where did they hit today? Again, a residential area. When did they shoot? At night, so that more people die.

This is a crime against humanity. If the international community does not want to bring Armenia to justice for the crimes it has committed – just as no one has brought them to justice for the Khojaly genocide – we will bring them to justice ourselves. We will punish them, and our punishment will be just. They deserve the most severe punishment. The military-political leadership of Armenia is criminal, and we will punish these criminals.

The prime minister of Armenia who said that "Karabakh is Armenia." What happened? Why aren’t you saying that "Karabakh is Armenia" now? Come to Fuzuli, where you were exploiting our land. Come to Jabrayil, come to Hadrut, come to other liberated places, and say that "Karabakh is Armenia.". You are sitting there in Yerevan, making statements from there, annoying world leaders – there is no one left you didn’t phone.

Why aren’t you saying that "Karabakh is Armenia"? You are afraid, and you should be. But why were you so brave when you insulted the Azerbaijani people by saying that "Karabakh is Armenia, full stop"? Who did you rely on? Didn’t you know that one day you will be held accountable for your actions? The day has come and is coming. Bringing Armenians from Lebanon and other countries to Shusha is a war crime that contradicts the Geneva Convention. They do it demonstratively; they show it on TV; they show Armenians coming to live and work in our ancient land. Let's see now who will come to settle in Shusha. You were building a new road with Armenia from Jabrayil. Why? You have illegally occupied that region, our Araz region, in order to settle Armenians there? You wanted to make us face facts? What was the purpose of bringing Armenians from abroad and settling them there in various ways, including through deception because Armenia has a small population? The goal is to keep our historical lands under eternal occupation to ensure eternal occupation and Armenianize our lands. Look, they gave Fuzuli an ugly name. Let this name be a curse to you. This name will go to hell. This name no longer exists. There is no Madagiz – it is Sugovushan. We will restore our other historical names. You wanted to move the parliament of your "entity" to Shusha. Go ahead and do it now! Where is the place where you conducted the "swearing-in ceremony" of the leader of that fake gang? We have destroyed it, completely destroyed it. You put forward seven conditions to us. You were speaking to us in the language of ultimatum. Let's see what your conditions are now. What happened? You cling to people, fall at their feet, begging for help in stopping Azerbaijan. Tell Azerbaijan to stop. Get out of our land, and we will stop! Get the hell out of our lands! I have said this before and do not hide anything. The people of Azerbaijan know this, and the international community is saying this too. I say this every day – get out and say that you will leave here tomorrow, and we will stop. We do not need to shed blood. We need land. We will get this land by any means. Let everyone know this. The history of the last days shows this.

It is proving too costly for you, for the Armenian leadership, to insult the Azerbaijani people. Too costly. The Armenian people must finally bring the leaders of this criminal regime to justice. Rallies are already being organized in military conscription offices in Armenia. Mothers are blocking the roads and preventing their children from dying in another country. I also appealed to the Armenian people, and I am appealing to them again: Do not let your children go! What are they doing in our lands? Live in your own country. We have nothing to do with you. Go and live in your own country; do whatever you want but leave our lands. I am confident that the Armenian people will also bring the leaders of their criminal junta to justice. We are on the path of truth; we are on the path of justice. We are right, we are fighting in our own land, we are giving martyrs on our own land. Ours is a holy war!

We have shown our strength on the battlefield, both to the enemy and to the whole world. The strength we are showing on the battlefield is underpinned by the will of the Azerbaijani people, their talent, and our success.

I want to say again that we are lucky people. Our generation is happy to be witnessing these happy days. I consider myself lucky to convey this good news to my people. As the Commander-in-Chief, I lead all the work and want to assure the people of Azerbaijan that I will continue to do my best to protect the national interests of our country and our people. No threat and no pressure can affect my will. Ours is the cause of truth. We are fighting on our own land and restoring our territorial integrity.

Long live the Azerbaijani Army! Long live the people of Azerbaijan! Karabakh is Azerbaijan!

World.title: Turkmenistan’s trade turnover growth slows to 13.2% in Jan-Sep 2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. The growth rate of trade turnover under Turkmenistan’s Ministry of Trade and Foreign Economic Relations slowed to 13.2% in January-September 2026 compared with the same period of 2025.

This was announced in a statement issued by the press service of the Turkmen government following Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Nokerkuly Atagulyyev’s report on the country’s economic performance for January-September at a government meeting chaired by President Serdar Berdimuhamedov yesterday.

Trend’s calculations based on official government data show that the trade turnover growth rate declined by 5.2 percentage points in January-September 2026 compared with the same period of 2025.

At the same time, the 2026 figure remained 11.1 percentage points above the 2.1% growth recorded in January-September 2024.

The growth rate of textile production stood at 6.4% in January-September 2026. Production of cotton yarn increased by 2.3%, cotton fabrics by 0.9%, garments and knitwear by 2.6%, and leather products by 0.5%.

The Turkmenhaly state association recorded a 7.6% increase in total revenue during the reporting period.

The State Commodity and Raw Materials Exchange held 222 trading sessions during January-September, registering 23,460 contracts.

Meanwhile, the Chamber of Commerce and Industry recorded a 7.3% increase in the volume of work carried out during the period, while hosting 18 exhibitions and 10 conferences.

President Serdar Berdimuhamedov instructed the government to ensure the efficient use of production facilities in the trade sector and continue the modernization of textile enterprises.

World.title: Iran's Imam Khomeini Port handles $1.5B in exports in six months
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. During the first six months of the current Iranian year (March 21–Sept. 22, 2026), 4.1 million tons of products worth $1.5 billion were exported through Imam Khomeini Port in Iran's southwestern Khuzestan Province.

According to Trend's analysis based on data from the Iranian Customs Administration, exports through Imam Khomeini Port decreased by 33% in value and 41% in weight during the six months compared with the same period of the previous Iranian year (March 21–Sept. 22, 2025).

During the six months, 6.4 million tons of products worth $2.9 billion were imported into the country through Imam Khomeini Port. Imports increased by 16% in value but decreased by 34% in weight compared with the same period of the previous year.

During the reporting period, 204,000 tons of products were transited through Imam Khomeini Port, up 268% compared with the same period of the previous year.

Customs revenues at Imam Khomeini Port totaled 292 trillion rials, or approximately $164 million, during the six months, increasing by 318% compared with the same period of the previous year.

During the first nine months of the previous Iranian year (March 21–Dec. 22, 2025), non-oil exports through Imam Khomeini Port totaled 9.73 million tons worth $3.29 billion. During the same period, 12.8 million tons of products worth $5.32 billion were imported through the port.

Imam Khomeini Port has an annual capacity to load and unload 60 million tons of oil and non-oil products. The port has previously been described as one of Iran's major strategic ports and a key entry point for essential goods.

World.title: ChatGPT maintains lead in Azerbaijan's AI chatbot market
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 9. ChatGPT maintained its leading position in Azerbaijan's artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot market in September 2026, with a market share of 86.3%, according to Trend's calculations based on data from StatCounter Global Stats.

ChatGPT's share increased by 2.69 percentage points from August.

Google Gemini ranked second with a 10.28% share, down 1.17 percentage points from the previous month.

Perplexity accounted for 2.34% of the market, followed by Claude at 0.83% and Microsoft Copilot at 0.24%.

Thus, ChatGPT continued to significantly outperform its closest competitors in Azerbaijan's AI chatbot market.

Meanwhile, OpenAI has begun the global rollout of GPT-6 in ChatGPT, accompanied by a new Intelligent UI feature that allows the chatbot to combine text, visuals, and interactive elements in its responses. The feature can include interactive charts, buttons, forms, diagrams, calculators and other tools.

OpenAI says GPT-6 can automatically select the most appropriate format for a response depending on the task. For example, it can use an interactive diagram to explain a complex topic or generate a calculator for a specific task.

OpenAI has also announced a new visual advertising format for ChatGPT. The company plans to begin testing the format later in October among Free and Go users in the US. OpenAI says the ads will be clearly separated from ChatGPT's responses and will not influence the answers generated by the chatbot.

World.title: Kazakhstan's goods exports rise 27.1% to $48.5B in H1 2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. Kazakhstan’s exports under balance-of-payments statistics increased by 27.1% year-on-year to $48.5 billion in the first half of 2026.

This was reported in a press release published by Kazakhstan’s Ministry of National Economy, citing data from the National Bank of Kazakhstan.

"Positive growth was recorded across more than 80% of commodity categories," the ministry said.

According to the ministry, citing the country’s Bureau of National Statistics, exports of copper and copper cathodes increased by 58%, while shipments of copper ores and concentrates rose by 42.9%. Uranium exports grew by 15.1%, and wheat exports increased by 28.2% in 6 months. Sulfur exports rose 2.9-fold, while silver exports increased 2.4-fold.

Amid 9% growth in manufacturing, non-resource exports increased by 19.5% to $18.6 billion.

The ministry also reported continued growth in January–July 2026, with exports increasing by 15.8% year-on-year to $50.9 billion.

Kazakhstan’s trade surplus reached $14 billion, exceeding the year-earlier figure by $5.4 billion, the ministry said.

According to Trend’s calculations, the trade surplus increased by 62.8% year-on-year.

The report says that agricultural exports rose by 34.8%, from $3.7 billion to $5 billion. The main contributors in 7 months were wheat, up 25.5%; sunflower oil, up 49.1%; animal feed, up 68.2%; flax seeds, which more than doubled; and flour, up 37.1%. These products accounted for around 60% of agricultural exports, according to the ministry.

World.title: Uzbekistan escrow transactions rise 3.8% to 34,659 in September
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. Uzbekistan processed 34,659 real estate and vehicle transactions through escrow accounts in September 2026, up 3.8% from August, according to the country’s Central Bank.

Real estate transactions accounted for 16,711 of the total, an increase of 1,126, or 7.2%, from the previous month. Vehicle sales accounted for the remaining 17,948 transactions.

Real estate transactions drove most of the monthly increase, while vehicle sales remained the larger segment by transaction count.

Tashkent recorded the highest number of transactions among Uzbekistan’s regions, at 10,711, followed by Fergana region with 3,363, Samarkand region with 3,131 and Namangan region with 2,404. The capital accounted for 30.9% of all completed transactions, while the other regions contributed 69.1%.

As of September 30, another 4,354 transactions were still being finalized, according to the Central Bank.

In August, Uzbekistan recorded 33,392 transactions through escrow accounts, including 15,585 real estate deals and 17,807 vehicle sales. September’s total was 1,267 higher, with real estate transactions accounting for approximately 88.9% of the net monthly increase.

Uzbekistan introduced a new procedure requiring noncash settlements for covered real estate and vehicle transactions from April 1, 2026. Under the procedure, banks provide electronic payment information that notaries use to verify settlements before finalizing contracts. Escrow accounts can be used to hold funds until the transaction is completed.

According to Trend’s calculations, real estate accounted for 48.2% of September’s completed transactions, while vehicle sales made up 51.8%. The four leading areas — Tashkent, Fergana, Samarkand and Namangan — together accounted for 56.6% of the national total. The 4,354 transactions still being finalized at the end of September were equivalent to 12.6% of the number completed during the month.

World.title: Azerbaijani weightlifter wins three bronze medals at European Championships
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 17. Azerbaijani weightlifter Gasim Ismayilov has delivered a successful performance at the European Weightlifting Championships for U23 and junior athletes, held in the Albanian city of Durres.

Competing in the 75 kg weight category, Gasim Ismayilov finished third in the snatch with a result of 139 kg.

The athlete also performed successfully in the clean and jerk, lifting 175 kg to claim another bronze medal.

Thus, with a total of 314 kg across both events, Gasim Ismayilov secured another bronze medal at the European Championships.

World.title: New menopause guidelines designed to cut through misinformation
World.content:
Hot Flushes. Night sweats. Vaginal dryness. Painful sex. A frequent need to wee.

Menopause marks the end of a woman's reproductive years and is associated with a range of symptoms that can affect their quality of life.

There's a lot of information and misinformation about the best treatments to help ease the severity of symptoms.

In a bid to make things easier, the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG) has developed a new set of clinical guidelines.

Loading...

The guidelines clarify when to use menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) over other medicines and what options are available for those with a history of breast cancer.

RANZCOG guideline development group chair Catriona Melville said they wanted to "cut through the noise" and provide clear, evidence-based recommendations for clinicians to discuss with their patients.

"If your clinician is not clear about where the evidence lies and what's safe and what isn't safe, and what's recommended and what isn't recommended, then they're not in a position to have that patient-centred discussion about what the available [treatment] options are," she said.

What do the guidelines cover?

The new guidelines provide evidence-based advice for managing the symptoms of menopause, which begins 12 months after a woman's last period.

The guidelines cover vasomotor symptoms (such as hot flushes and night sweats) and genito-urinary symptoms (such as vaginal dryness and the frequent need to urinate) of menopause in women 40 years and above.

They do not cover the management of bone density, joint pain, libido, depression or anxiety.

Experts sceptical about menopause 'cliff-like' decline A new international study suggests menopause-related changes to the body are sudden and "cliff-like", but Australian experts urge caution interpreting the results.

Magdalena Simonis, a practising GP and women's health expert from the University of Melbourne, said not all women experienced the same type or severity of symptoms.

While she was not involved in developing the guidelines, she said they reinforced the need for clinicians to treat the whole person in front of them, not just the symptom.

"We should also be looking at lifestyle and other risk factors around the time of the menopause," Dr Simonis said.

"This is a really important time to talk about [cholesterol] lipid control, bone density management and lifestyle activities.

"Looking at family history of other cancers, breast screening, cervical screening and having that conversation around chronic conditions."

How do the guidelines work?

The guidelines list a range of possible treatment options for different menopausal symptoms, including menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), acupuncture and hypnosis, ranking available evidence on a scale of very low to high.

The guidelines recommend that women taking MHT have an annual review with their doctor.

But there's not enough evidence that weight loss or physical activity alone will improve hot flushes or night sweats, or that hypnosis will improve sleep.

Dr Melville, a specialist gynaecologist and sub-specialist in sexual and reproductive health, said the new guidelines would hopefully make it easier for clinicians and patients to understand their options.

For example, women with a history of breast cancer can be offered vaginal oestrogen to ease menopausal symptoms.

Although RANZCOG had previously released statements about managing menopausal symptoms, Dr Melville said these were their first evidence-based guidelines.

How will it improve patient care?

Women should receive the same standardised recommendations no matter who they see or where they live if clinicians across Australia use the same guidelines.

Women cut HRT patches in half amid ongoing shortage Supplies of some HRT patches may not return to normal until at least the end of the year.

Jean Hailes for Women's Health chief executive Sarah White, who was not involved with the guidelines, said this was important because clinicians wanted to give their patients the very best support, but there was a lot of online misinformation to wade through.

"It really will help the health professional to have these new guidelines sitting in front of them so that they can talk them through and reassure women that they are getting the very best advice," she said.

The guidelines also encourage clinicians to ask women approaching menopause if they experience any "troublesome" symptoms, especially if patients are First Nations, Māori and Pacific Islander women and others who may experience barriers to treatment.

This will make it easier for women to get help, even if they find it hard to ask.

Won't there be new national guidelines soon?

The Australian government has funded separate perimenopause and menopause guidelines expected to be released next year.

These guidelines, which RANZCOG is contributing to, will be continually updated as new evidence emerges.

Dr Simonis welcomed the spotlight on the health of menopausal women.

She encouraged anyone experiencing troublesome symptoms to book an appointment with their GP and advised women approaching mid-life to schedule a check-up.

"Menopause is not a stage to be afraid of or to dread; it's a natural phase of life," she said.

World.title: Famous Larrimah pub shuts after bikies visit sister venue on 'charity run'
World.content:
The owner of the Northern Territory's famous Larrimah Pink Panther Hotel and the Stuarts Well Roadhouse has shuttered both businesses following a police raid regarding "a visit" by the Outlaws bikie gang this week.

In a statement released yesterday, an NT Police spokesperson said investigators had searched the Stuarts Well Roadhouse "and an adjoining property" after a tip-off alleging breaches of the venue's liquor licence.

They said officers searched the property on Wednesday and allegedly found an unsecured firearm and ammunition, 214 packs of illegal cigarettes, six unlawfully imported OC spray canisters and $3,800 in cash.

Police allege a search of the Stuarts Well Roadhouse and "an adjoining property" resulted in the seizure of an unsecured firearm and ammunition along with 214 packs of cigarettes. (Supplied: NT Police)

Police charged a 59-year-old man with unlawfully possessing a Schedule 8 drug and a 33-year-old man with breaching his firearms licence conditions.

They also charged a 71-year-old man with manufacturing, selling or purchasing a prohibited weapon, with all three due to face the Alice Springs Local Court in January next year.

The spokesperson said the alleged liquor licence breaches had been referred to Licensing NT.

'Corrupt cops', government 'harassment'

Following the raid, the owner of both venues, Laura Ragless, took to social media to announce they were each "officially closed".

"Don’t bother coming the government harassment and all has taken its toll sorry," she wrote.

"We will always respect our supporters but no longer can take the government harassment the convicts running this country."

Stuarts Well Roadhouse owner Laura Ragless has labelled charges laid following a raid on the business as "trumped up". (ABC News: Hamish Harty)

On Tuesday, Ms Ragless posted pictures to the Stuarts Well Roadhouse Facebook page showing members of the Outlaws motorcycle gang attending the pub on the Stuart Highway south of Alice Springs.

"A little rain and wind can’t stop these legends from hitting the road," she wrote.

"Great to see the crew rolling into our roadhouse today!

"Thanks for stopping by, guys. Ride safe and enjoy the journey!"

In a separate post on Wednesday, Ms Ragless denied any wrongdoing and suggested the Outlaws had been on a "charity run".

"Accused of illegally selling cigarettes and gun charges when I don’t even have guns anymore," she wrote.

"And to top it off Stuart’s well [sic] locked down by corrupt cops that can’t even produce a warrant enough is enough."

In another post this morning, Ms Ragless claimed the charges were "trumped up" and the tobacco products were "personal cigarettes not sold in or around the roadhouse".

Under NT law, licensees and staff are required to direct outlaw motorcycle gang members to leave the premises if they refuse to remove "any clothing or items that identify their club".

'No animal welfare concerns'

In a statement, a spokesperson for the Department of Agriculture and Fisheries told the ABC animal welfare officers had conducted an unannounced inspection of the Larrimah Hotel on Thursday after receiving "reports regarding animals".

"No animal welfare concerns were identified pursuant to the Animal Protection Act 2018 at the time of the inspection," they said.

Larrimah Pink Panther Hotel owner Laura Ragless says she closed the pub by choice. (ABC News: Neda Vanovac)

"The Animal Welfare Branch assesses all reports received and undertakes enquiries where appropriate.

"It will continue to monitor and assess information in accordance with its normal operational processes."

Ms Ragless also took to Facebook on Wednesday to defend her treatment of the business's resident saltwater crocodile, Sneaky Sam.

Sneaky Sam has been the Larrimah Pink Panther Hotel's resident croc for years. (ABC News: Neda Vanovac)

"No one shut me down it was my choice and how about you google crocs they can only snap not chew so Sam leaves his food for later," she wrote in response to a customer.

" Would you like national parks and wildlife numbers I can give them to you that [sic] god you only had one beer. "

The Larrimah Pink Panther Hotel sells merchandise referencing the 2017 disappearance of local man Paddy Moriarty. (ABC News)

The Pink Panther Hotel on the Stuart Highway between Katherine and Daly Waters made global headlines following the disappearance of local man Paddy Moriarty in 2017, years before Ms Ragless took over.

The still-unsolved mystery has been the subject a hit podcast, a book and a HBO documentary film, with Ms Ragless now selling merchandise from the pub featuring Mr Moriarty's likeness.

World.title: Dogs captured after attack on Brisbane man
World.content:
Two dogs have been captured after a man was attacked in Brisbane's north overnight.

Emergency services were called to Kittyhawk Drive in Chermside just after 6pm on Friday evening after reports a man had been attacked by dogs.

They found a 37-year-old man with serious injuries to both arms, and two dogs fled the scene.

The man was taken to the Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital in a stable condition.

Police located and captured one of the dogs nearby a short time later with the assistance of a police helicopter.

The other dog remained at large overnight but was located and captured by police at an address in Wavell Heights this morning.

A spokesperson for Brisbane City Council said both dogs were registered at the same address and had not previously been declared dangerous.

"Both dogs involved are now in council possession and a decision on their future will be made as soon as possible," the spokesperson said.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with the victim of last night's horrific dog attack."

World.title: Breaking: Mexican court sentences three men over murders of Jake and Callum Robinson
World.content:
Three men have been sentenced to more than 150 years in prison for killing Perth brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend Carter Rhoad two years ago.

The three victims were killed during a surfing trip in Mexico's Baja California region in April 2024.

Jesús Gerardo, known as "El Kekas", Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús, whose full names were withheld for legal reasons, were found guilty of aggravated homicide and several related offences in a judge-only trial last week.

The prosecution told the trial that the victims were murdered during a robbery gone wrong, although the defence had attempted to argue there was not enough evidence to prove the case.

Ángel Jesús has been in custody in a local jail. (Supplied)

Judge Raul Hernandez Arellano sentenced each man to 158 years and 9 months in prison, saying the characteristics of the attack constituted a serious crime.

He told a court in Ensenada, Mexico, that their crimes were made worse by the fact the tourists were unarmed and attacked at a remote location at night.

He said the three men had time to think through the crime and proceeded anyway.

Jesús Gerardo, alias El Kekas, had a reputation as a violent hit man, the trial heard. (Supplied: Mexican police handout)

Irineo Francisco has links to the Sinaloa cartel, according to court documents. (Supplied)

The men were also ordered to pay 1,980,728 pesos ($45,000) for the murders of the brothers, and 549,550 pesos for the murder of Mr Rhoad.

In an emotional address, Mr Rhoad's mother, Page, thanked the judge.

She told the court that while nothing could recover her son, she was glad no other families would be victims of these men's crimes.

The defence team have indicated their intention to appeal the sentence and have 10 days to do so.

International attention in surfer case

In 2024, Jake, 31, travelled to California to see Callum, 32, before they travelled south to Mexico.

Jake was a doctor who was due to start a new job at a Geelong hospital after returning to Australia, while Callum was a talented lacrosse player who had moved to the US to pursue the sport.

The pair had initially been reported missing by friends and family members when they were unable to contact them and learned they had failed to check into their accommodation as planned.

Callum and Jake Robinson disappeared while camping on Mexico's west coast. (Instagram: @Callum10Robinson)

The bodies of the two men, along with Mr Rhoad's, were later found at the bottom of a well along Mexico's Pacific coast.

The case made international headlines and has shone a light on crimes against tourists in Mexico.

World.title: Wildfires rage in Southern California, burn homes
World.content:
Firefighters in Southern California say a fast-moving wildfire has ripped through at least six homes, engulfing expensive coastal properties and prompting thousands to evacuate.

TV footage showed homes engulfed in flames in San Juan Capistrano in Orange County on Friday, local time.

Firefighters doused two-storey suburban homes with flames leaping out of their roofs. Black smoke billowed over tennis courts and backyard swimming pools.

Over 500 firefighters were battling the blaze that had grown to nearly 2 square kilometres, said Captain Steve Concialdi, a spokesman with the Orange County Fire Authority.

A firefighter works to douse a blaze in San Juan Capistrano. (AP: Jae C. Hong)

"We're doing everything we can to protect structures," he told KTLA-TV.

An evacuation shelter has opened in each city.

The Norte fire started in the coastal city of San Clemente and wind drove it into San Juan Capistrano.

It was one of several fires in the region hit by dry, warm gusts known as Santa Anas, which blow from the interior and toward the coast.

The strongest winds were expected through Friday afternoon but conditions that increase the fire risk were expected to last through Saturday night.

Tens of thousands of people in the state are without power after their electricity was turned off.

A separate fire shut down a section of Interstate 5 that is a major artery connecting Orange County to San Diego, adding hours to commutes throughout Southern California.

The coastal cities are surrounded by hillsides.

San Juan Capistrano, a city of 35,000, is known for horse trails and the historic Mission San Juan Capistrano. San Clemente, which is home to 62,000 people, is known as a "Spanish village by the sea" and is popular with beachgoers and surfers.

A resident grabs a garden hose in an effort to help with a wildfire spreading in his neighbourhood, in San Juan Capistrano. (AP: Jae C. Hong)

Thousands were being asked to evacuate, said Victor Cabral, a San Clemente council member.

"The fire is right up on the city," he said.

"It's on the perimeter of our homes on the north end."

Nine schools were also closed on Friday in San Juan Capistrano, the Capistrano Unified School District said.

Howard Hart, a local council member, said he and his wife doused their roof with water and moved propane tanks away from their home before they evacuated on Friday with a to-go bag.

Laura Hart has not had to evacuate due to fire in the more than five decades she has lived in the community, she said.

"This doesn't usually happen to us, we usually see it on the news," she said.

"We always pray to God it's not us, but yeah, it was today."

Santa Ana winds hit

The Bryson Fire that sparked on Thursday, local time, in Malibu had died down significantly by Friday and firefighters were focused on mop-up and containment, officials said.

The blaze prompted evacuation orders and warnings for a swath of the Santa Monica Mountains that covered more than 12,000 people.

Winds from 32km/h to 56km/h were expected on Friday, with gusts forecast to reach 80km/h to 112km/h in some areas, the National Weather Service said.

A firefighting helicopter drops water as the Bryson Fire, burns in the hills east of Malibu. (Reuters: David Swanson)

Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, who faced criticism for her city's response to deadly fires in 2025, directed the fire department to deploy personnel and equipment ahead of the winds.

The fire department also asked for help from the state's Office of Emergency Services.

"It's a pretty widespread event of elevated fire weather, so the whole SoCal region should really be on alert," said Rose Schoenfeld, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service.

In some areas temperatures soared as high as 38 degrees Celsius.

The weather authority said fire danger would remain through much of Saturday, warning residents to be prepared for emergency evacuations.

They also cautioned drivers about dangerous crosswinds, particularly on elevated roadways.

Firefighters battle several blazes

Firefighters on Friday worked to contain two other fires that erupted on Thursday afternoon and triggered evacuation orders in the city of Azusa, east of LA, and Camp Pendleton, near San Diego.

More than 200,000 customers in California were without electricity as of Friday, according to poweroutage.com.

Some of California's worst wildfires have been sparked by power equipment, and utilities in recent years have begun proactively shutting off power in dry winds.

Firefighters use water hoses in San Clemente. (Reuters: Caroline Brehman )

Farther south, a fire at the Marine Corps base Camp Pendleton threatened buildings and doubled in size over one day to more than 8 square kilometres.

The blaze crossed containment lines on Friday morning, closing a section of the I-5 freeway as the fire burned steadily toward it.

Power cuts widespread

In Northern California, some communities in the Sierra Nevada and its foothills began experiencing strong winds, high temperatures and low humidity on Wednesday night.

The weather service issued a red flag warning for parts of central and Northern California throughout Friday morning, saying any fires would spread rapidly.

Such warnings are issued when weather conditions create an increased risk of wildfires.

Customers from the Central Coast to the upper corners of the Sierra Nevada could be without power through Saturday afternoon, Pacific Gas and Electric Company said.

AP/AFP

World.title: 'Oh, shut up': Moment in Maine sums up Trump's troubles
World.content:
Susan Collins carries herself like she could have run an etiquette school if she hadn't spent her life in politics.

The Republican senator has a genteel air of grandmotherly decorum. It distinguishes her from many of her MAGA colleagues.

And it made for a more striking moment when her Democratic opponent turned to her and said, "Shut up," during a debate this week.

Troy Jackson is a former logger with a rough-and-tumble brand of working-class politics. He was annoyed that Collins had accused him of planting a protester in the crowd.

"This is obviously one of Troy's supporters," Collins said as the audience member started screaming about data centres.

"Oh, shut up," Jackson replied. "I did not. I don't even know that kid."

The protester had actually posed as a journalist. Wearing an oversized laminated "press" lanyard, he convinced a worker he should have been on her media list and was escorted inside with me and another reporter.

But his outburst was more than a moment of isolated debate drama. It represented one of the big dangers to Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections.

Polls show Democrats and Republicans both generally hate data centres and their explosive growth across the country.

But Trump has shrugged off their concerns.

He says people who oppose them "want to end up being backwards and poor". He labels the backlash "a sick conspiracy".

It's on a growing list of issues motivating voters to punish Trump at the midterms, where he keeps telling voters to pretend he is on the ballot.

Anger with Trump

Maine's Senate race is one of the midterms' most important. It's one of a handful of toss-up contests that could cost Republicans their majority.

The debate, in the regional centre of Bangor, was only interrupted once. But it had several similar reminders of times Trump has dismissed voters' concerns as either conspiracy or stupidity.

This attitude towards voters' concerns has been forcing Republicans onto the defensive when faced with angry constituents on the campaign trail.

Maine is a key state in the battle for a Senate majority, and pollsters rate the race as a toss-up. (Portland Press Herald: Gregory A Rec via AP)

Affordability is an obvious one of those issues.

Collins and Jackson sparred over who to blame for rising prices. But Trump has repeatedly described the issue as a "hoax" concocted by Democrats.

All the surveys show it's a burning concern for voters and a big reason his approval rating keeps sinking further underwater.

In one recent poll, 65 per cent of Americans blamed high prices on Trump policies rather than on factors out of his control.

That's much higher than the proportion of Americans who blamed Joe Biden for high prices (44pc) before the 2022 midterms, when Republicans seized control of the House from Democrats.

Immigration and deportations are another issue that was once seen as a Republican strong suit but is now backfiring.

In January, ICE launched an immigration crackdown in Maine called "Operation Catch of the Day", a pun for the fishing state.

Many Mainers didn't appreciate the joke, or the operation itself. After public pushback, the operation was abruptly terminated, and Collins took credit.

But ICE operations later ramped up again in Maine. Three months ago, a 25-year-old Colombian father who had a US work permit was shot dead by an ICE agent during a traffic stop.

"One of those bullets went into that car seat that was in the back seat of his car," Jackson told the debate. "Luckily his daughter wasn't there, or she wouldn't be with us either."

Collins said she had made progress pushing for safeguards like body cameras for ICE agents. But she agreed more reforms were needed to improve how they operate.

Polls now show most Americans are not in favour of the national immigration crackdown. A Fox News poll last month found 53 per cent thought it had gone too far.

Loading

Then there's the increasingly unpopular war in Iran.

Collins told the debate that Trump "definitely" should have consulted Congress before attacking Iran, and he should have had a plan for the Strait of Hormuz.

Once the war started, she said, the War Powers Act gave Trump broad authority for 60 days. "After 60 days, that's when I voted every single time with Democrats to bring the conflict to a halt."

Distancing from the president

Collins, more than any other Republican senator, has worked to distance herself from Trump.

"I vote very independently," she told the debate. "The studies show that I am the most bipartisan member of the Senate."

Jackson mocked this claim.

"100 per cent of the time Donald Trump needs her, Susan Collins is going to be there," he said.

At one point, Collins helped to prosecute Jackson's point that she is not an effective check on the president.

When asked to name a time she successfully changed something by opposing Trump, she cited Pete Hegseth's nomination as defense secretary.

"At one point, I had organised people to vote against Secretary Hegseth," Collins said.

It was a curious example to choose. Her effort failed, the Senate confirmed Hegseth, and there is no sign he has held back on any of the contentious moves he planned.

The tactics at 'Trump-a-palooza' Donald Trump's approval rating is at dire lows. But he has deliberately tied his party's fortunes to his own popularity, and "Trump-a-palooza" showed his tactics are not changing.

Jackson wants to link Collins to Trump as much as possible because so many voters are angry with the president over so many issues.

The audience member who sat next to me during the debate could be an indicator that that strategy is working.

He told me he hoped Collins didn't spot him in the audience.

He knew her and had voted for her previously, but he was attending the debate as Jackson's guest.

"It's hard because she has helped us," he told me. But she had also done too much to "enable" Trump, he said.

"He's nuts," he added. "So we need a change."

World.title: The humble chickpea has just boomed in value
World.content:
Australian chickpeas are in hot demand, with delivered prices surging this month towards $1,000 per tonne in some regions.

It is a significant jump from earlier in the year, when the market was trading closer to $600 per tonne.

Grains Australia Pulse Council chair Peter Wilson said it was a great result for growers.

"We haven't seen $1,000 per tonne since 2024, so it's significant. It's a great price," he said.

" For growers who have ended up with a decent [chickpea] crop, this is balance-sheet altering. There's no other way to describe it. "

Chickpea prices have gone up considerably this month. (ABC Landline)

What is driving the chickpea boom?

So what is driving the sudden price surge for Australian chickpeas?

Mr Wilson said it was due to a combination of factors.

"There's a lot of volatility globally right now, which is creating enormous turbulence in logistics and supply chains, which is keeping buyers on edge," he said.

"We're also seeing the impacts of El Niño, which looks to have left parts of India with lower-than-average rainfall from the monsoon, which has caused their local chickpea prices to rise, which is pushing everything along."

The season's first delivery of chickpeas to the Mt McLaren receival site in Queensland. (Supplied: Marc Johnston/GrainCorp)

Mr Wilson said there were several nations wanting to lock in supply ahead of Ramadan, which starts in early February.

"Ramadan creates peak demand for a lot of our pulse crops [like chickpeas], and we see buyers wanting to have product pre-positioned at least one month ahead of Ramadan," he said.

"So we're seeing some urgency from buyers trying to get product onboard vessels for key destination markets such as Pakistan, Bangladesh and the UAE, so it's in the market and ready for that Ramadan demand."

In its most recent crop forecast, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics and Sciences (ABARES) predicted Australian chickpea production would fall by 52 per cent "to just over 1 million tonnes in 2026–27" due to significant cuts to area planted and expected lower yields in the major growing regions of northern New South Wales and Queensland.

ABC Landline has been told that forecast may be "optimistic" and the overall crop might be even lower, which is another reason why there is some buyer urgency at the moment.

Prices are expected to ease as harvest supply increases.

New season chickpeas arrive at the receival site at Yamala, Queensland. (Supplied: Fred Smith/GrainCorp)

Cashing in

North West Queensland chickpea grower Lucas Findley said he was pleased with his harvest, yielding about 1.2 tonnes per hectare.

Although he had already forward-sold most of his chickpeas at a lower price, he said it was still exciting to see the market rally.

"High prices are always good for any commodity and I'm happy for anyone who can take full advantage of these prices," Mr Findley said.

"We'd sold around 75 per cent of our chickpea crop prior to this recent price rise at a good price that we were happy with.

"But we still have around 25 per cent of the crop available to take advantage of the stronger prices, which will be a very nice finish to the season."

Hummus is made from cooked, mashed chickpeas. (ABC News: Wesley Mitton)

Mr Findley grows about 1,300 hectares of chickpeas as part of his grain and cotton rotation in Julia Creek.

His chickpeas will be exported out of the Townsville Port, which is gearing up for its second-ever dry bulk shipment of the pulse.

Last October, more than 38,000 tonnes of chickpeas were sent to India and Pakistan in a first-of-its-kind shipment from north Queensland, sourced from growing regions including Richmond, Julia Creek, Maxwelton and Marathon.

This year, the port will also export sorghum for the first time, which Mr Findley said was "fantastic".

"It just shows that people are supporting the expansion of North West Queensland farming more and more," he said.

Watch ABC TV's Landline at 12:30pm on Sunday or on ABC iview.

World.title: SA health care worker banned after cancer cure claims
World.content:
A man who abused "vulnerable" clients by claiming he could cure cancer and make an non-ambulatory woman walk has failed in a bid to overturn his "indefinite" ban from practising as a health care worker.

Adrian Fabio Mangini was providing health services in South Australia, including "hypnogym", hypnotherapy and yoga, before he was banned from practising indefinitely in 2024 by the Community Services Complaints Commissioner.

A judgement published by the South Australian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (SACAT) earlier this year upheld the decision after Mr Mangini asked for a review.

It upheld the previous findings by the Community Services Complaints Commissioner which included Mr Mangini's claim, in a YouTube video, that he made a woman living with a non-ambulatory disability walk "after an 11-minute consultation where he hypnotised her and counselled her by providing encouraging words".

Senior member of SACAT Jacqueline Rugless also reiterated in her judgment that there was "no evidence" the woman "was previously disabled or that she could not walk at all or could only walk with a frame".

"I am satisfied that the applicant claimed in advertising or promotional materials to have made … 'a disabled person' walk as a direct result of his provision of services, in circumstances where there was and is still no proof that [she] was disabled and could not walk prior to the consultation," she said.

Cancer cure claims

The tribunal also upheld a previous finding that Mr Mangini had claimed he cured cancer.

"The applicant [Mr Mangini] privately messaged a client about assisting a different client of his to be 10 years' cancer free, such that he represented he was able to cure cancer," the judgement said.

The judgement also upheld a finding that the health care worker had "engaged in behaviour of a sexual or close personal nature with a client".

The South Australian Civil and Administrative Tribunal upheld a decision to ban Adrian Mangini from practising. (ABC News: Eugene Boisvert)

"I am satisfied that the proven conduct of the applicant demonstrates a degree of overt abuse of the health and safety of vulnerable consumers together with open and deliberate dishonesty in his advertising about the alleged beneficial consequences of the services he sought to offer to consumers," Ms Rugless said.

"The applicant has demonstrated no insight into his behaviour and has displayed no remorse for his conduct. I am satisfied that he continues to pose a risk to the public.

"The proven conduct is completely incompatible with Mr Mangini continuing to be a health care worker or a health services provider."

Proceedings labelled a 'vendetta'

The judgment also outlined that Mr Mangini had argued in the tribunal that the proceedings were brought against him because of a vendetta by the Community Services Complaints Commissioner.

"I am not satisfied that there is any evidence of a 'vendetta' against Mr Mangini by a person or persons either known to him or unknown, or of a racist motivation behind the allegations that were before the Commissioner," Ms Rugless said in the judgement.

"In any event I am satisfied that the allegations found proved in the Commissioner's report have been independently verified by the Commissioner's investigation."

Mr Mangini has filed an appeal against SACAT's decision in the state's Supreme Court.

World.content:
WorldNorth AmericaCrime Mexican men sentenced to 158 years in prison for murdering Australian brothers Gabriela Martinez Michael Koziol and October 17, 2026 — 1:57pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items.
