World.title: Greens propose to abolish training wage
World.content:
The Green Party would abolish the training wage, saying people should not be forced to live in poverty while they learn on the job.

Currently, the adult minimum wage is $23.95, while the training and starting out minimum wage are $19.16 - set at 80 percent of the adult wage.

But the Green Party's co-leader Chlöe Swarbrick said apprentice numbers were at a 15-year low.

"Low pay, insecure work, and a lack of pastoral support mean that instead of focusing on learning their trade, our apprentices spend too much time worried about making ends meet. We can fix that."

Swarbrick said abolishing the training wage would mean apprentices were paid properly for their work.

ACT is campaigning to reduce the training wage to 60 percent of the minimum wage, which it would also freeze for three years.

A $30 million package would go towards Māori and Pasifika-led training, including pastoral and learning support.

Employers that "actively support" apprentices to complete training would get a completion bonus of $2000.

Swarbrick said the training wage had done nothing to increase the uptake of apprentices, and it was a barrier to people completing their training.

"If you look at the economic benefits of increasing wages, especially for those who are literally doing the work, this is good economic development. It is good for our local economy."

She said the average age of a person taking up an apprenticeship was 27 years old.

"That is actually people who are re-inserting themselves back into training, and therefore would be taking a pay cut in order to take on the training under the training wage regime. That is not fair."

Co-leader Marama Davidson said instead of focusing on gaining skills and learning their trade, apprentices were worried about their rent, debt, and the cost of getting to work.

"If we want people to enter trades and complete apprenticeships, it's time we fairly recognise their hard work instead of punishing them for trying to contribute."

The Greens would also introduce a $2000 equipment grant to cover tools, uniforms, and course materials - double the $1000 Labour is offering with its policy.

Labour would also expand the Apprenticeship Boost scheme back to two years, which the Greens have not committed to.

Labour leader Chris Hipkins said the training wage was not something he had looked at, and he wanted to review the evidence around the overall employment impact of the policy.

"The key thing we'd want to look at there is making sure that we're not doing anything that makes things worse for younger employees. And right at the moment, youth unemployment is a major issue. I want to leave no stone unturned in getting young people into jobs."

He said Apprenticeship Boost, which he first introduced as education minister, was hugely successful.

"We got record numbers of young people into apprenticeships."

National leader Christopher Luxon also expressed concern the policy would not be good for the businesses wanting to take apprentices on.

"No, we want to make sure that businesses actually take a chance on young people, and it's one of the ways that they might just step out and actually take a chance on a young person."

New Zealand First leader Winston Peters claimed apprentices "in the good old days" were happy to get the training wage, knowing in six months to a year they would be onto the proper wage.

"In the first week or two, and for quite some time, the apprentice is not of great help to the enterprise. But they're learning fast, and businesses don't mind that, because they're on a slightly lesser wage while they learn. They're on about 80 percent That's the way it's always been."

Asked whether that was enough for an apprentice to live on now, Peters said many were living at home and being supported by parents.

ACT leader David Seymour said the policy would make it $10,000 more expensive for a business to take on an apprentice.

"You almost wonder if the Green Party is not campaigning for Australia, because that's where more young people will end up with under their policy," he said.

The Greens' costings, which have been verified by Infometrics, have put the policy on $117.35m a year for four years.

That, Seymour said, would cover $2,000 per apprentice.

The policy follows the Greens' announcement on Friday that it would offer $380-a-week stipends for trainee teachers, nurses, and other health and social workers while they are on their placements.

World.title: Kāpiti Coast pizza store owner gets 10 months' home detention for tax evasion
World.content:
A pizza store owner on the Kāpiti Coast has been sentenced to 10 months' home detention for more than half a million dollars of tax evasion.

Wenbin Shi faced a representative charge in the Porirua District Court on Thursday of not providing GST, company and personal income tax returns.

He also faced a representative charge of aiding and abetting a Paraparaumu pizza franchise which was taking PAYE from staff wages and not passing it on to Inland Revenue.

Inland Revenue says Shi operated SWB Foods Limited (SWB), trading as Hell's Pizza in Paraparaumu, since 2014 and at the time an Inland Revenue audit started in June 2024 SWB had a tax debt of $400,000.

The review of SWB's accounts showed gross yearly sales of between $687,708 in 2017 and $1,390,341 in 2024. Shi stopped filing GST returns for SWB in 2020. The GST amount outstanding was $185,143.86.

Between April 2015 and April 2018 SWB largely filed and paid PAYE on time but between July 2019 and November 2022, Shi filed returns and took the money from staff wages but didn't pay PAYE to Inland Revenue.

PAYE arrears were deducted from the company accounts, and two statutory demands were issued which together resulted in a portion of the PAYE arrears being paid.

The amount remaining unpaid was $194,295.50.

SWB failed to file five yearly income tax returns between March 2020 and March 2024. The estimated amount that should have been paid is $124,415.77.

Inland Revenue says Shi had full knowledge and control over the tax obligations of the company and failed to file 25 GST returns, income tax for five years for SWB and failed to file personal income tax returns over the same period. He also failed to pay 23 PAYE deductions to Inland Revenue.

In November 2025 Shi filed all outstanding GST and income tax returns which added up to $503,855.13. Shi had repaid $100,000.00 before sentencing, resulting in a total loss amount to Inland Revenue of $403,855.13.

World.title: St John introduces female-form manikins to address cardiac arrest survival gender gap
World.content:
St John is changing the way it is teaching CPR to address the gender gap in survival following cardiac arrest.

It is introducing 16 female-form manikins, which have been donated by the Medical Assurance Society, to the free community CPR and AED training programme called 3 Steps for Life.

Spokesperson Jacci Tatnell said research had shown that women face additional barriers to receiving bystander CPR and defibrillation.

She said concern about exposing breasts, uncertainty around AED pad placement, and fear of causing offence could create hesitation in an emergency.

"So females have a 50 percent lower odds of survival following an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest as compared to men, and then they have a 60 percent lower odds of receiving bystander defibrillation."

Only around five percent of CPR manikins globally are female, meaning most people practise lifesaving skills on male models, Tatnell added.

It's hoped the female-form manikins will help address inequities for women experiencing cardiac arrest, while also making training more realistic. SUPPLIED/ST JOHN

As for why it had taken so long for St John to introduce them, Tatnell said it had been difficult to find a distributor in New Zealand. The female-form manikins had to be brought in from a supplier in Australia, and cost had also been a barrier.

"I also wonder that, actually, the stats around the differences between the community CPR and community defibrillation on women have only really started to be known, that there's such a big change, so I think maybe now there's more focus on, you know, is the training materials we've got the right training materials to help people feel confident in defibrillation and CPR on a woman."

Tatnell hoped the female-form manikins will help address inequities for women experiencing cardiac arrest, while also making training more realistic. They will allow people to practise CPR and AED placement on manikins with breasts, helping increase confidence when responding to different body types.

"Cardiac arrest itself is quite traumatic, actually understanding, you know, what might stop people from getting involved in doing the CPR and putting on defibrillation is really hard to measure.

"But what we're hoping is that by having the conversation around the importance of ... community defibrillation on women, you do need to expose the chest and that actually for a woman who's in cardiac arrest, that's the difference between them possibly surviving and not.

World.title: Can my stepkids sell my house? - Ask Susan
World.content:
Got questions? RNZ has a podcast, 'No Stupid Questions', with Susan Edmunds.

We'd love to hear more of your questions about money and the economy. You can send through written questions, like these ones, but even better, you can drop us a voice memo to our email questions@rnz.co.nz.

You can also sign up to RNZ's new money newsletter, 'Money with Susan Edmunds'.

My stepchildren and step-grandchildren are claiming my home, my main asset, and want it sold ASAP for their benefit. They started their demands at the funeral. Their lawyers are very demanding although I have provided everything requested. They say they will subpoena me.

My husband and I married over 50 years ago and we built our home in 1990. However my lawyer said I must sell to pay them and I must pay their legal fees as well. He left absolutely nothing in his name as we held everything jointly. I have had to value my home, my possessions and provide all our bank account information. My husband and I treated these children very well throughout his life and our same lawyer said recently they could not claim jointly held assets but has changed his mind.

He did not work after 1990 and needed home care more recently. I worked decades more and paid off our mortgage. How common is it that widows/ers are compelled to sell up and start over at a late age?

This sounds like a complicated situation, so Public Trust principal trustee Michelle Pope can only comment at a high level.

She says family and property arrangements can become complicated over time, particularly in blended families.

"That's why we encourage people to seek legal advice early and review their estate planning regularly. Getting advice when new relationships begin and assets are combined, or family circumstances change, can help provide clarity and reduce the risk of disagreements arising later on.

"Following a death, someone who believes they have not been adequately provided for may have options to make a claim against the estate. A surviving spouse or partner may also have rights in relation to relationship property. Every family's situation is different, and any legal proceedings will depend on the particular circumstances and the rights of those involved."

Usually, assets that are owned jointly pass directly to the surviving owner.

My partner and I have approximately $500,000 invested with Craig's Investments under separate accounts. My portion has been there for almost 30 years. We also have money invested at a bank, about $300,000 combined, in separate accounts, plus my KiwiSaver invested in Teacher Retirement Scheme. We are selling our rental property for $600,000. Are we best to invest this with the same financial company or for security diversify and invest with a different company? We are both retired and own our home.

Rupert Carlyon, founder of Koura KiwiSaver, says it's worth thinking about whether there's a way that you can set up your investments so you can access advice from someone who can see the full picture.

"I think what's most important is everything is looked at holistically … So if you've got money, a bank account, you've got some shares, you've got KiwiSaver, you need someone that's going to give you advice as to how to look at the whole thing together as a single block.

"They are all important parts of a portfolio that's meant to fund a retirement, and so you can't look at them independently.

"They might find an adviser that is more than happy to kind of advise on the whole lot, but only get compensated for advising on a small part. Or they might find a fixed fee adviser that builds out plans and they can then go and execute. There are different ways, but in my experience it's normally cheaper and easier just to get a single person looking after the whole lot. The one exception is that teacher's superannuation plan, because those have often got a lot of other benefits."

He advised working out what benefits were attached to the teacher scheme, then considering whether the Craig's account, bank account and rental property money could be brought together somewhere where it could be managed as one. "Ideally nothing should be in the bank account, if they are wanting to have a cash element it should be in a cash-style fund."

One of my friends had an acrimonious divorce and one of the outcomes was that half his KiwiSaver went to his ex-wife. The balance wasn't transferred to her KiwiSaver; she received it in cash. She has dual citizenship, so I suppose it could be released because she is from another country, but shouldn't the money be transferred to her KiwiSaver?

Not necessarily, if KiwiSaver is withdrawn as part of division of relationship property, a court can order either that the money be transferred to the other person's KiwiSaver scheme or it can be paid out directly.

Most people deal with KiwiSaver through offset, though. If one person has more of a balance than the other, they end up with less of the proceeds of the house, or other assets.

If my partner needs residential care, say due to Alzheimers, should we get divorced (but still live together) to avoid the government taking all (rather than half) of our assets for the care?

If you're still living together and caring for each other, you're probably going to still be classified as being in a relationship even if you are divorced.

The Ministry of Social Development said the criteria used to determine a relationship included things like whether you live together or socialise together, whether you share bills, whether people think of you as a couple and whether you give each other emotional support and companionship.

"Anyone who is unsure about how their income and assets could affect their eligibility for the residential care subsidy can visit the Work and Income website or contact MSD's Residential Subsidy Unit to discuss their circumstances," MSD said.

World.title: Live: Black Ferns v France women's WXV Global Series test
World.content:
The Black Ferns kick-off against France in the WXV Global Series test at Hamilton's FMG Stadium at 3.05pm.

Follow all the action in our live blog below:

Embedded content removed for printing

Rising winger Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a has been recalled in one of just two starting changes to a test-hardened Black Ferns side to open their home series against France.

Coach Whitney Hansen has stuck primarily with the side beaten 26-19 by England in a thriller in London three weeks ago, for Saturday's first Test in Hamilton.

Maama Mo'onia Vaipulu will start at lock and Laura Bayfield is demoted to the bench in the lone change to the pack which started at Twickenham, where the world champions won through a late intercept try.

Hansen has chosen to hand a start on the right wing to Chiefs Manawa flyer Tuliau-Tua'a, who pushes Mererangi Paul to the reserves.

The 20-year-old scored on debut off the bench against the Wallaroos in Auckland in August was handed a start in another big win, against Scotland in Edinburgh last month.

There are tweaks on the bench, where veteran playmaker and leader Ruahei Demant returns, having missed the three WXV Tests in Europe after injuring a calf muscle against South Africa.

Despite being among the reserves, Demant has returned as a co-captain, alongside starting hooker Georgia Ponsonby.

Hansen said selection was a delicate balancing act.

"Building on the momentum from our England performance, we needed to strike the right balance between providing opportunities for our newer Black Ferns, and maintaining the continuity and experience around them to succeed," she said.

"We've made changes to who starts and finishes, which will be a focus this campaign. Both are equally important, and we need players who can excel in each.

Black Ferns: Braxton Sorenson-McGee, Shyrah Tuliau-Tua'a, Amy Du Plessis, Logo-I-Pulotu Lemapu-Atai'i Sylvia Brunt, Ayesha Leti-I'iga, Hannah King, Maia Joseph, Kaipo Olsen-Baker, Elinor-Plum King, Liana Mikaele-Tu'u, Maama Mo'onia Vaipulu, Maiakawanakaulani Roos, Veisinia Mahutariki-Tu'u, Georgia Ponsonby (co-capt), Chryss Viliko.

World.title: Transport delays expected for Auckland's 'super Saturday of sports and sounds'
World.content:
Auckland Transport is warning passengers to expect some delays, as tens of thousands of people head to what has been dubbed a "super Saturday of sport and sounds".

Auckland FC's A-League season opener will be at Go Media Stadium, alongside sold-out concerts from Olivia Dean at Western Springs Bowl, Stan Walker at The Trusts Arena, and Macy Gray at The Civic.

The warning has come after some passengers waited up to 40 minutes for a train after last weekend's Bledisloe Cup match at Eden Park, due to a delay in closing a level crossing.

Rebecca Paul from Auckland Transport Operations Centre urged people to be patient and keep in good spirits this weekend.

"I think it's reasonable to expect that with moving large crowds for such busy events, that there will be some wait time involved."

Macy Gray. MAT HAYWARD

She said Auckland Transport would be monitoring the network and would update passengers if any delays occurred.

Paul said extra capacity would be added on some buses and trains, as those heading to the Auckland FC game against Melbourne City FC will also be able to travel for free from 1.30pm. Additional staff will also be stationed at Penrose Station, about a 12-minute walk from Go Media Stadium.

For the sold-out Olivia Dean concert, regular bus and train services will continue, while private event shuttles will run between downtown Auckland and Western Springs Bowl. Additional buses will also be on standby on the NX1 and 18 routes after the concert.

People heading to Stan Walker's sold-out show at The Trusts Arena can use regular bus services from Henderson Station, while those driving are being encouraged to use the Lincoln Road or Te Atatū Road motorway off-ramps.

Macy Gray is also performing at The Civic, with the show expected to finish about 10.30pm.

Paul urged people to plan ahead, allow extra time, and check the Auckland Transport website or mobile app for the latest information.

"We are monitoring the network from the operations centre. We're doing everything to ensure that you're kept up to date. If there are any delays, that information goes out immediately, and we're able to remedy things as they happen on the network.

World.title: Champi threatens Marianas as Guam braces for destructive winds
World.content:
Tropical Storm Champi is rapidly strengthening as it approaches the Mariana Islands with forecasters warning it could become a powerful Category 3 typhoon before passing just south of Guam on Sunday morning.

The US National Weather Service said Champi could bring destructive winds, torrential rainfall and dangerous coastal flooding across Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands, with damaging winds expected to arrive around midnight Saturday.

As of early Saturday, Champi had maximum sustained winds of 112km/h and was moving west at 24kph slowing from 38kph on Friday.

Forecasters expect the storm to intensify into a category 3 typhoon, with sustained winds of 177-to-209km/h before reaching the Marianas.

Guam and Rota remain under Typhoon Warnings, while Tropical Storm Warnings and Typhoon Watches remain in effect for Saipan and Tinian.

Flood Watches, Coastal Flood Watches, and High Surf Warnings are also in effect across the islands.

Guam is expected to bear the brunt of Champi, with peak winds of 168-to-193km/h and gusts reaching 249km/h Sunday morning.

The island could receive 12 to 20 inches of rainfall, with surf reaching 35 feet and coastal inundation of five to seven feet.

Governor Lourdes Leon Guerrero placed Guam under Condition of Readiness 2 at 1pm Friday, urging residents to secure their homes and prepare emergency supplies.

"Protecting the lives and safety of our people remains our highest priority," Leon Guerrero said.

She also warned residents to stay out of the ocean as dangerous conditions develop.

Meanwhile, Northern Marianas Governor David Apatang signed Executive Order 2026-023 on Friday, declaring a Significant Emergency across the Commonwealth to mobilise resources and coordinate emergency preparations.

Apatang also raised Rota to Typhoon Condition II while maintaining Typhoon Condition III for Saipan and Tinian.

Forecasters

Rota is forecast to experience winds of 96-to-128km/h, with gusts reaching 185km/h, rainfall of 10 to 15 inches and surf up to 25 feet.

Coastal inundation of two to four feet is also possible.

Saipan and Tinian could experience winds of 64-to-96km/h, with gusts reaching 128km/h, rainfall of four to six inches and surf reaching 20 feet.

Forecasters warned that any northward shift in Champi's track could bring significantly stronger conditions to Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

National Weather Service meteorologist Landon Aydlett said the storm continues to intensify, with the Joint Typhoon Warning Center indicating that rapid strengthening was imminent.

He said weather conditions would begin deteriorating Saturday as showers move across Guam and Rota.

"The window of opportunity for preparatory actions is shrinking and will get sloppy and gusty later this morning and afternoon as showers roll in," Aydlett said.

He noted that a further southward shift in Champi's track could offer some relief to parts of the Marianas, but cautioned residents against becoming complacent.

Shelters

Authorities are urging residents across the region to complete storm preparations by sunset Saturday.

In the Northern Marianas, emergency shelters on Saipan, Tinian and Rota were scheduled to open at 8am Saturday.

Residents still occupying temporary FEMA and STRONG tents following previous typhoons have been advised to seek stronger shelter.

The approaching storm comes as the Northern Marianas continues recovering from Super Typhoon Sinlaku in April and Super Typhoon Bavi in July.

Champi's passage threatens to compound damage to homes, public infrastructure and utilities already affected by previous storms.

World.title: Live: Wallaroos thrash Scotland 56-12 ahead of Wallabies' clash with All Blacks
World.content:
The Wallaroos score a massive 56-12 win to open rugby's historic quadruple header at Stadium Australia, before the Wallabies meet the All Blacks in the Bledisloe Cup.

The Australian women's and men's sevens teams will also play at Stadium Australia, when they take on New Zealand and Fiji respectively.

It is the first time all four national teams have appeared on the same match-day schedule.

Follow our live blog.

World.title: 'Decision next year': Nawaqanitawase keeps Wallabies options open
World.content:
Mark Nawaqanitawase is refusing to rule out turning his back on Australia for next year's home Rugby World Cup as a three-nation tug-of-war for the cross-code super talent escalates.

While Wallabies captain Harry Wilson and coach Les Kiss have no doubts Nawaqanitawase will be wearing the gold jumper at the 2027 global showpiece, the player himself is keeping his options open.

The in-demand winger's manager this week suggested Nawaqanitawase may choose to represent Fiji, to honour his father's heritage, or Italy, who the dual international is also eligible for through his grandmother.

Still only 26, the prospect of Nawaqanitawase defecting from Australia had seemed improbable.

Under World Rugby laws, if he chose to switch allegiances, following 11 Test appearances for Australia in 2022-23 before enjoying a hugely successful two-year stint in the NRL, the dual international would not be allowed to wear the Wallabies jumper ever again.

Wallabies in awe of Nawaqanitawase It was not just the 80,000 spectators, nor the millions of TV viewers in Australia, who were left in awe of Mark Nawaqanitawase's performance in the NRL grand final.

Representing Fiji or Italy could appear a more appealing scenario in the twilight of his career, but not his pomp.

However, the newly-crowned NRL premiership winner took to social media yesterday to reveal he had yet to make any decisions about his playing future beyond a looming two-year, $3 million stint in Japan under former Wallabies coach Robbie Deans.

"I just thought I would jump on here as there has been a lot of speculation on my future," Nawaqanitawase posted on Instagram.

"My only focus right now is moving to Japan in a couple of weeks and connecting with my new team at Saitama Wild Knights.

"I will weigh up my options and make a decision next year on my international future.

"Love, Marky."

After taking in the Kangaroos' thrilling Rugby League World Cup win over New Zealand on Thursday night with Nawaqanitawase in Sydney, Wilson is confident the free agent will be playing for Australia next year.

"I don't have to convince him," Wilson said ahead of the Wallabies' second Bledisloe Cup clash with the All Blacks in Sydney today.

" I played junior Wallabies with him, played Wallabies with him, saw him last night supporting the Kangaroos, so I think it's pretty obvious who he wants to play for. "

Coach Kiss is also optimistic about the 2023 Olympic sevens star opting for a Wallabies return next year.

"I think there's no doubt that he wants to be back in the game for us, that's for sure," Kiss said.

"We'll continue our conversations and go from there. I'm not going to speak on his behalf at all. But we know where he wants to play."

AAP

World.title: Tattoo artist brings queer joy to AFLW pride jumper
World.content:
When it comes to elite sporting teams, some adopt roaring tigers or bucking horses on the guernseys, but sometimes a "fruity" dolphin works best.

The playful design for the Gold Coast Suns' Pride Round guernsey, by Sunshine Coast tattoo artist Mady Peters, is bringing fun, and maybe some luck, to the Queensland AFLW side.

Ms Peters's design features a rainbow football boot, which she says highlights the support of the LGBTQIA+ community for women's football, as well as a carabiner, a symbol historically associated with the women-loving-women community.

She said the colours and characters reinforced Pride Round's message of self-expression.

Mady Peters, also known as Pokey Pokes, in her tattoo studio. (ABC Sunshine Coast: Nykayla Dux)

"It just came from a place of joy," Ms Peters said.

" I think that's everything that the Pride Round kind of stands for — this celebration and to show up authentically and as yourself. "

Among the more light-hearted illustrations is a dolphin holding a non-binary flag.

"I believe dolphins are a bit fruity," Ms Peters said.

Peters, Mithen and Lynch all shared the same vision for the 2026 Pride Guernsey: queer joy, self-expression, and a little bit of silliness. (Facebook: Gold Coast Suns)

The Sunshine Coast artist said she hoped Pride Round would help queer people relish and celebrate their identities.

"There is a world that still exists where people would rather not be here than be themselves, and that's so sad to see," she said.

Her work has won the endorsement of Mitch Brown, who last year became the AFL's first past or present player to openly come out as part of the LGBTQIA+ community.

Gold Coast Suns AFLW players Lily Mithen and Katie Lynch worked with Ms Peters to develop the guernsey.

LGBTQIA+ community 'in the fabric' of AFLW

Mithen said the team wanted the design to reflect their individual personalities.

"Katie and I are a bit loud and fun and silly and we wanted that to be felt through the jumper," she said.

Mithen said helping design the guernsey was an important way to honour the LGBTQIA+ community, which she said had been "woven into the fabric of the AFLW from the very beginning".

"[The AFLW has] always been a place where people have been really free to be themselves," she said.

Lily Mithen says Pride Round celebrates everyone’s individual strengths. (Supplied: Gold Coast SUNS)

For Lynch, her connection to football began playing with "the boys" at the age of four and grew into an enduring love of the game and a place where she felt accepted.

She said many in the AFLW had grown up knowing they "maybe did see themselves doing things a little differently", and that shone through in their sport.

Lynch said it was important to acknowledge a "very brave and courageous group" continuing to challenge perceptions of the LGBTQIA+ community in sport, including in the men's competition.

Head of AFLW at the AFL Players Association Julia Chiera said she could remember feeling like the "odd one out" as the only young girl playing football in her community, before finding a sense of belonging at Melbourne's Darebin Football Club as an adult.

Chiera said women's football had provided a welcoming environment for many queer people at the community level well before the national competition began.

She said football had historically attracted many queer women and gender-nonconforming people because of their "fearlessness" to challenge social expectations.

"It felt empowering to be amongst women who loved football and didn't really care if it was not socially acceptable for women to play sport," she said reflecting on her time at Darebin.

Julia Chiera says the AFLW’s culture of authenticity and acceptance extended beyond sexuality and is celebrated year-round in the women’s league. (Supplied: AFL Players’ Association)

However, Chiera said more work was needed to improve inclusion in the men's game, which did not have a dedicated Pride Round.

She said meaningful support for the LGBTQIA+ community required clubs, players, administrators and supporters to demonstrate genuine inclusion throughout the season and behind closed doors, rather than relying on a single round.

Ms Peters said she hoped the guernsey would bring the Gold Coast side the same good luck for their second and final game of Pride Round 2026 after the Suns won their first match last week.

"I knew it was lucky. I put lucky vibes into it," she said.

The Gold Coast Suns will wear the Pride guernsey for a final time against the Adelaide Crows in Adelaide on Saturday afternoon.

World.title: Dees dismantle Tigers to seal AFLW finals series berth
World.content:
Melbourne has secured a spot in the AFLW finals series after dismantling Richmond with ease in Pride Round.

Last night's 14.10 (94) to 5.2 (32) win was a return to form after the Demons' surprise first-ever AFLW loss to Gold Coast the previous week.

The defeat to the Suns was front of mind for Demons coach Tom Wilson ahead of the Tigers clash at Melbourne's Princes Park.

"We understood last week was far from our best performance," Wilson said before the first bounce.

"We thought around the ball we probably got a bit of a lesson in that space.

"Contest is going to be really important. (Richmond) having Monique Conti and Ellie McKenzie in there, it's a real weapon for them."

Conti returned to the field for the first time since an Achilles injury in round three and wasted no time getting to work.

Within seconds of the first bounce, the club's seven-time consecutive best-and-fairest winner won the centre clearance for the Tigers.

It was a welcome return given Richmond's struggles this season to win the loose ball. The Tigers rank second-last in the competition for contested possession.

But despite Conti's return, and Richmond ruck Poppy Kelly dominating with 23 hit-outs, the Demons won the centre contest time and again through Olivia Purcell and Tyla Hanks.

The pair heeded coach Wilson's call, with each picking up more than 30 disposals and a combined 13 clearances.

Their dominance set up Melbourne's 47 inside-50s to Richmond's 18, and spelled a long night for the Tigers' defence.

Ryleigh Wotherspoon kicked four goals to give the Demons some reassurance ahead of a finals series in which they may be without lead goal kicker Mia Austin, who has undergone throat surgery and does not yet have a set return date.

"We've got a lot of forwards that can kick goals, and even the mids can come through and kick goals, and so we're well supported and well balanced," Wotherspoon said after the game.

"We're pretty unstoppable."

AAP

World.title: Jillaroos lived up to their end of the bargain, but fans need to follow
World.content:
Seeing the Jillaroos in action is a rare privilege — a collection of the best women's rugby league players in the world, in the sport's global showpiece, on home soil.

The three-time defending champions opened their World Cup at Western Sydney Stadium with a flexing 40-0 win over Samoa, in a campaign that should engage and excite Australians and the vast diaspora of the other competing nations.

While that was the case for the earlier men's game between Samoa and France, with 13,174 fans, mostly representing western Sydney's large Samoan community, they left in large numbers at the end of that game.

And there were very few supporters — Samoan or Australian — left by the end of the women's clash, in a disappointing sight for an event of this stature.

A strong contingent of fans turned up to watch Samoa's men play France. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

This is not a new dilemma for women's sport. When and where to play, whether to have double headers, how best to engage existing fan bases and draw in new ones?

Women's State of Origin has been a good example of elevating the women's game in its own way, standing separately to the men's series, often in smaller venues, but packing them with passionate fans who are there only to watch the women. And drawing big numbers on TV too.

The World Cup presents a different challenge, with Australia currently in a league of its own on the field and another trophy considered by many as a fait accompli.

But the world is starting to catch up, and as the tournament progresses over the next month, it would be a shame for the event to go under the radar.

Rugby League World Cup live The all-conquering Jillaroos begin their women's Rugby League World Cup campaign against Samoa. Follow live.

Jillaroos coach Jess Skinner summed it up simply afterwards.

"Let's get around women in sport, right? All women in sport, and particularly this Rugby League World Cup. We've got a lot of talented women across all of the teams," she said.

"Stay and support that and the growth. Something really cool is happening in this generation of sport with our ladies, and you're going to miss it.

"There's history making moments over this World Cup, no doubt, and want to see our fans, particularly in the green and gold, to be a part of that. But also just in general, come and have a look."

The Jillaroos will play England and Wales in their next pool games. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

Samoa coach Frank Pritchard suggested the late 8pm kick off didn't help, and the women were keen to play before the men.

"Our fans and our supporters will always stick through it and and stay there," he said.

"I've seen a lot of blue jerseys out there. We had plenty of support, that's for sure."

Jillaroos captain Isabelle Kelly was less concerned with the crowd, than with ensuring the Jillaroos achieve what they set out to at this tournament. And all signs point to a four-peat.

Jillaroos just warming up

It was a straightforward win for the Australians, who were not at their ruthless, rampaging best, but instead showed they are warming to the task, and will likely ignite as the tournament progresses.

Five-eighth Jocelyn Kelleher had an impressive first outing in the green and gold. She was player of the match on debut, continuing the form that saw her guide the Sydney Roosters to the NRLW Premiership.

"Her kicking game was amazing. And she took her opportunities when she had them as well," Skinner said.

"So couldn't get better than that in a World Cup debut for the Jillaroos, become part of a legacy piece, and you get player of the match. So really proud of her."

Olivia Kernick made crucial gains through the middle, Tamika Upton pulled the strings in bursts without being at her fully devastating best, and Jaime Chapman, Julia Robinson, and Jess Sergis surged as needed, with all seven tries scored by different players.

Olivia Kernick was one of the Jillaroos' standouts. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

There were scrappy moments though, times where Samoa's defence jolted, and the visitors found ways to cut through the Australians when going direct.

Freedom Crichton Ropati's bone cruncher on Tiana Penitani Gray in the dying minutes was a highlight, epitomising Fetu Samoa's dedication to valiantly protecting their line, even with the result long gone.

Leading 28-0 at half time, the Jillaroos were restricted to just two tries after the break.

Overall, it was an effort that was enough for the Jillaroos to be content, without being complacent, and for Samoa to find light at the end of the tunnel, rather than wallowing in darkness.

"We spoke about pride in the jersey and what it takes to be here, sea of blue, effort on effort, and definitely showed that in the second half," Pritchard said.

"That second half proved to us that competing and staying in the fight is more than just a footy game."

Starting to see it

Athletes often speak of the honour of representing their country and their family on the world stage.

But for many of the Pasifika nations competing at this tournament, filled with players from the diaspora in Australia and New Zealand, it hits a little different.

Fetu Samoa's players say it has meant a lot to be at the World Cup for the first time since 2008. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

As with the men, tears streamed down the faces of the Fetu Samoa players during the national anthem.

And they continued afterwards, not of disappointment, but of deep understanding of what it means to be here.

"What our ladies are doing for our young girls at home with sport in general, especially rugby league, is massive," Pritchard said.

"It's something that our girls can gravitate towards."

It was an especially meaningful game for Evania Isa'ako, who has previously represented Australia.

"For me, it was not just coming and playing and putting on this jersey; it was being able to learn [about the culture]," she said.

"So off the field, culturally, everything that we've done. All the work that Frank's put in behind the scenes… outsourced people to come in and teach us, that's the really important stuff behind the scenes that people don't see."

They might not see it yet, but come the end of the tournament, maybe there'll be more eyes watching.

World.title: Proteas urged to wear down Australia's bowling machines in second Test
World.content:
South Africa have vowed to do better at wearing Australia's bowlers down in the second Test, desperate to rebound after the batters' meek surrender in Durban.

The Proteas are set to welcome back pace ace Kagiso Rabada for Sunday's second Test in Gqeberha, after he terrorised Australia on the last tour in 2018.

But the hosts have pointed to their batting as the biggest bridge that must be mended between the two sides after the series-opening 214-run defeat.

Aiden Markram was the only Protea to pass 50 in the Test, with seven others scoring between 30 and 49 across both innings.

That prompted coach Shukri Conrad to claim he was "pulling the very last strands out of his hair" as he axed both Tristan Stubbs and Kyle Verreynne.

South Africa number three David Bedingham spoke of the relentless nature of Australia's attack on Friday, with Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon offering little reprieve.

But with the three Tests in this series essentially being played back-to-back, he stressed the importance of putting work into the Australian bowlers.

"It's just about trying to take them to 80 overs, 100 overs, 120 overs," Bedingham said.

"And then, I know they're machines, but everyone gets tired eventually. Well, hopefully…

"When Kesh (Maharaj) and Simon (Harmer) were batting around the 68th over in the first innings, I'm not saying they were tiring, but the ball was a lot softer.

"It looked a lot easier. So if we could have maybe been four, five down there, then maybe the game would have a different angle."

Meanwhile, Rabada looks almost certain to play, as the Proteas fight to avoid their first home series defeat since England toured in 2019-20.

Rabada's record of 58 wickets at 21.39 is the second best of any quick against Australia this century, behind only Jasprit Bumrah.

He was the Proteas' arch-villain in the 2018 series, colliding with Steve Smith after taking his wicket in Gbqerha (then Port Elizabeth) and only avoiding a ban on appeal.

Kagiso Rabada missed the first Test against Australia with a hamstring tear, but he looks set to return in Gqeberha. (Getty Images: Sameer Ali, file photo)

Rabada has steamed in at South Africa training this week, showing no signs of the hamstring tear that sidelined him for through the ODIs and first Test.

"He's massive for us," Bedingham said.

"It looks like he's quick again, he's sharp.

"Even if you look back last year in the World Test Championship final, he took nine wickets against Australia.

"Against any team he plays against, he's ready. Hopefully, come this next Test, he takes nine or 10 wickets; that would be quite nice."

Batters Marques Ackerman and Matthew Breetzke are expected to come in at St George's Park, with Ryan Rickelton to take gloves from Verreynne.

AAP

World.title: Jillaroos flex muscle in 40-point World Cup win over Samoa
World.content:
Australia's quest for a fourth consecutive Women's Rugby League World Cup has started with a bang courtesy of a 40-0 victory over Fetu Samoa.

Unbackable favourites leading into the tournament opener, the Jillaroos overcame an ill-disciplined opening 10 minutes to shut out Samoa in the seven-try rout.

Things were far from easy for Australia in the second half, but the damage was already done by half-time, with five-eighth Jocelyn Kelleher and reigning Dally M medallist Tamika Upton leading the way with two try assists apiece.

Kelleher, making her Jillaroos debut, was named player of the match, where she was dangerous in attack and her kicking game troubled Samoa.

Speaking to ABC Sport, Kelleher said she had been waiting a long time for her chance to play for the Jillaroos.

"It's a dream come true," she said.

"Was in the squad last year, but got my debut jersey this year. So excited and so happy to be here."

Despite the 40-point win, it was far from a perfect performance from the reigning world champions.

"We still have a lot of things to fix from today. It wasn't perfect out there," Kelleher said.

Samoa, in their first World Cup since 2008, had several chances early but lacked the class to capitalise against their much-fancied opponents.

Gold Coast Titans star Jaime Chapman ended her three-year Jillaroos exodus by scoring Australia's first try in the 11th minute, beating opposite winger Freedom Crichton Ropati out wide.

Australia's greatest ever try-scorer, Julia Robinson, lived up to her reputation seven minutes later when she beat three would-be defenders for her 23rd Jillaroos try in 14 appearances.

Tries to back-rower Shaylee Bent and hooker Keeley Nizza followed in quick succession before lock Olivia Kernick crossed moments before halftime to seal a 28-0 lead at the break.

Kernick turned playmaker in the opening five minutes of the second period when she handed the ball off for Keilee Joseph to extend the Jillaroos' lead.

Brave defence might have turned the tide for Samoa, who ground their way to more opportunities at the Jillaroos end over the final 25 minutes.

Prop Laikha Clarke went the closest to securing some consolation points for Samoa, but was ruled to have dropped the ball over the line.

Of further concern for Samoa was a suspected knee injury in the dying stages to centre Sarina Masaga.

A try in the final two minutes from Australian centre Jessica Sergis capped the Jillaroos' victory and extended their almost three-year unbeaten run.

Samoa's men thrashed France in the opening match of the day, putting on a record score to win 78-4.

World.title: PNG Chiefs to go ahead with NRL logo launch after court decision
World.content:
New Zealand's High Court has knocked back an application for an interim injunction on the PNG Chiefs NRL franchise using its name in the country.

New Zealand Rugby (NZR) had rushed to court before the PNG team's logo and jersey reveal in Port Moresby next week.

The organisation claimed use of the Chiefs name, which is also the name of the long-standing Super Rugby Pacific outfit, would cause confusion and damage to the brand.

But a judge at today's two-hour Wellington hearing turned down the application after hearing an injunction could harm the NRL expansion outfit's efforts to attract players ahead of a 2028 debut.

"The PNG Chiefs welcome today's decision in the New Zealand High Court and look forward to the launch of our inaugural logo and supporter jersey in Port Moresby on Wednesday,," PNG Chiefs CEO Lorna McPherson said.

NZ Rugby to protect 'Chiefs' name New Zealand Rugby has sought interim and final injunctions before the NRL's Papua New Guinea team is officially launched later this month.

"As the matter remains before the court, no further comment on this matter will be provided at this time."

The dispute continues, with an application for a final injunction still before the court and legal action in Australia under consideration.

ARLC executive chairman Peter V'landys last week labelled NZR's action one of "mind-blowing hypocrisy", using the example of the Auckland Blues' arrival decades after NSW "had been the Blues".

"Today's decision is not a judgment on the strength of our case and the matter will still be heard in full," NZR boss Steve Lancaster said.

"As the trademark holder, our responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand hasn't changed. We remain open to working with the ARLC on a solution."

NZR's lawyer Earl Gray argued today that the PNG Chiefs' use of "PNG Chiefs" and "Chiefs" interchangeably created confusion for fans of both codes and that, with no clear distinction between the two, it would strip the rugby Chiefs of brand exclusivity.

He said NZR had trademark protections for the Chiefs in New Zealand that the NRL had not acknowledged.

ARLC lawyer Clive Elliot argued that the request for an urgent injunction, about a year after NZR became aware of the PNG Chiefs name, was not appropriate.

He said an injunction now would cloud the franchise's reputation ahead of a recruitment blitz once free agency opened next month.

The ABC of SPORT Sports content to make you think... or allow you not to. A newsletter delivered each Saturday.

AAP

Tech.title: All the news about the iPhone Duo
Tech.content:
Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo.

The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease. Instead of Face ID, it uses Touch ID on the power button. It has two cameras, a main lens and a wide-angle lens. Apple completely revamped iOS 27’s controls and apps for the foldable, including putting the dock on the side of the phone. And it has a flashy opening animation when you unfold the phone.

The iPhone Duo a big new bet from Apple, though one that’s a little late to the game compared to competitors like Samsung and Google. The phone isn’t cheap: it starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, and the prices only go up from there. Still, Apple said that preorder demand was “extraordinary,” so it could have a hit on its hands.

Tech.title: Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
Tech.content:
is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Apple’s App Store rules now more explicitly ban so-called “nudify” apps that generate intimate images of people without their consent using AI tools.

As part of updates announced Friday, Apple says that developers “must proactively prevent and remove” nonconsensual, sexual images as part of its content moderation requirements for App Store apps. Developers who “fail to implement adequate safeguards” or “don’t remedy violations after notice” may be removed from the App Store. Apple also clarified a rule that bars “bait-and-switch” apps, or apps that add or change features, including “nudification,” after they have been approved.

Apple’s rules also more clearly spell out that any apps that “facilitate human trafficking or the exploitation of children” will be pulled from the App Store and “blocked from alternative distribution.”

Tech.title: We can finally hear some of Wu-Tang Clan’s Once Upon A Time in Shaolin album
Tech.content:
is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Wu-Tang’s Once Upon A Time in Shaolin album has, for the most part, been extremely difficult to listen to, but you can now hear two snippets of the album thanks to the podcast Pablo Torre Finds Out, which just published an episode all about the exclusive record.

Once Upon A Time in Shaolin has a long history, which Pablo Torre Finds Out goes into in detail. Disgraced pharmaceutical executive Martin Shkreli bought the only copy of the album, which cannot be commercially released until 2103, in 2015 at auction. Shkreli had to forfeit the album to the US government, and the government sold it in 2021 to the crypto art collective PleasrDAO, which has allowed it to be played at special exhibitions.

Pablo Torre Finds Out, working with PleasrDAO, hosted a listening party for the album where they played it for Wu-Tang Clan member Method Man, who had never heard it up until that point. The podcast recorded the event and Method Man’s reaction, and you can hear two snippets from the album at 32:30 and 39:02 during the show.

Method Man’s review? “I do not hate this album.”

Tech.title: Tesla driver says he was asleep and using FSD when he crashed into highway patrol cars
Tech.content:
is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

After this horrific crash involving a Tesla driver who said he was asleep and using the driver assist mode, the California Highway Patrol warns that “Despite its name, full self-driving is not fully autonomous. Technology does not relieve drivers of their responsibility to safely operate their vehicles.”

Video released by CHP shows the Tesla speeding past flares, cones, and emergency lights where officers were on the scene of an earlier accident, before ramming into the back of a parked patrol vehicle. CHP says two officers were seriously injured in the accident and taken to a hospital.

Following numerous collisions with parked emergency vehicles, NHTSA launched an investigation into Tesla’s Autopilot software in 2021. It eventually issued a report finding the driver-assist features didn’t do enough to keep drivers engaged, linking them to hundreds of crashes and dozens of deaths when both the system and driver failed to respond.

Tesla released an update for Autopilot in 2023 adding more controls and alerts to prompt drivers to be in full control of the car when Autosteer is enabled, but NHTSA then had to open another investigation into whether those changes went far enough.

Tech.title: Why Apple is finally making its own smart home devices
Tech.content:
is a senior reviewer with over twenty years of experience. She covers smart home, IoT, and connected tech, and has written previously for Wirecutter, Wired, Dwell, BBC, and US News.

For more than a decade, Apple has told other companies to build smart home devices for its platform. This week, Apple launched its own. The Apple Home Collection is a lineup of cameras, thermostats, sensors, a smart door lock, and a video doorbell, all codeveloped with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. They arrive alongside HomeView, Apple’s first smart display.

Even after 12 years of HomeKit, Apple’s smart home ecosystem still felt underdeveloped, especially compared to the competition. Amazon’s and Google’s ecosystems support more products, and both have popular in-house brands: Ring and Nest. Apple had nothing of its own to point customers to as an Apple experience — and now it does.

But why now? And does Apple actually add anything new here, or is this mostly packaging? At Apple’s “Welcome home” event in New York this week, I spoke with Kaiann Drance, vice president of product marketing for home at Apple, about the company’s new approach to the smart home and what this means for Apple’s commitment to Matter, the interoperable open smart home standard it helped found.

Apple’s HomeView is viewed as a gateway to bring people into the smart home. Photo by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

Why now?

Drance says the big reason for this focus on new smart home hardware was the development of the right technologies. The first was Matter, which provided the ecosystem. The second was AI, which brought a more conversational Siri voice assistant. Both were necessary to create a dedicated home device in HomeView. “With the magic of Siri AI, it comes together in a way that we haven’t been able to deliver before,” Drance says. “That’s been a really critical piece of bringing this all together.”

The bigger play is HomeView as a gateway to the smart home.

The bigger play here is HomeView as a gateway to the smart home for Apple’s users. Buy one for playing music, guided cooking recipes, and checking your calendar, and you might soon want a camera or smart lock to go with it. Drance says they’ve seen that once people try a single smart device and find it easier than they expected, it “unlocks this delightful understanding of what’s possible once you bring these products into the home.” She argues that most people just don’t know what a smart home can do.

She’s not wrong. The biggest barrier to buying smart devices is that people don’t see any value in the products, according to research from Parks Associates. Privacy and security concerns and complexity also rank high, along with cost. While Apple isn’t addressing the cost concern here — the products start at $200 — the other elements are part of its pitch: one-tap setup, your data stays yours, one app to run it all. Apple’s stamp of approval also carries a lot of weight. “People who own Apple products are very, very loyal, and there is a large user base,” says Elizabeth Parks, president and CMO at Parks Associates.

Several Apple Home Collection products: LG smart door lock, indoor camera and video doorbell, and a Schneider Electric thermostat. Image: Apple

From a choose-your-own adventure to a tailored solution

Until now, Apple Home has been a bit like a buffet: You can pick from any brand that supports HomeKit or Matter and hope it all goes together. The Home Collection is more like the chef’s choice, a short list of dishes Apple promises will pair well. Drance says that’s what some customers were asking for. “There is a lot of choice with Matter, and there’s a lot of great products out there,” she says. “But sometimes we do get asked, ‘Hey, what product should I put in the home?’”

Rather than build devices itself, Apple chose to codevelop the lineup with partners that “have their own expertise in the home.” Both have a global footprint and home experience, she says, “LG more so in consumer products, Schneider through home build and home installations.” Drance says it was a ground-up collaboration with Apple bringing “the design aesthetic that would be suitable for the home and suitable to go with our family of products.” The company is also partnering with ADT through Apple retail stores to help people install the devices.

Drance says setup and ease of use were also a big focus in the products’ development. “The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app,” she says. “We just wanted that simplicity to be at its core, and of course, the privacy that we’ve developed together with our partners.” She says everything integrates through Apple Home; you don’t need to create an LG or Schneider account, and all data is end-to-end encrypted, so only you can access it.

Drance was clear that the Apple Home Collection isn’t replacing the buffet — the hardware ecosystem that has grown up around Apple Home. “We still have this incredible ecosystem with Matter, and with Works with Apple Home, that is going to remain,” she says. “We know that homes are not a one-size-fits-all solution, so our customers will continue to have that choice, and we remain committed to building that ecosystem as well.”

The hardware mostly backs that up. The lock, thermostats, and sensors are Matter-compatible; the lock supports Aliro and works entirely locally, and every device supports Thread. The exception is the cameras, which use Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video, not Matter. That’s the biggest lock-in. I was surprised Apple didn’t announce Matter camera support. But the Thread radios suggest the hardware might be Matter-ready, and Apple may be waiting for the Matter camera standard to support encrypted uploads, something HKSV already does.

So, what’s the benefit?

Does the Home Collection do anything other Apple Home devices can’t? In theory, no; in practice, yes. “What we’ve done with Apple Home Collection is we’ve added another layer on top of that, that deeper integration,” says Drance. There aren’t features exclusive to the Home Collection; it’s more that Apple is saying all the features will be here. It’s a bit like Google making a Pixel phone to show Android developers what Android can do: Apple’s products come with the full suite of capabilities the platform offers.

“The one-tap setup was really important to make it so easy, having no need for a separate account, no need for a separate app.” — Kaiann Drance, Apple

According to Apple, setup is as simple as tapping your iPhone to the device, like pairing AirPods, with no extra account or app needed and no scanning required. Every device uses Thread to stay connected if Wi-Fi drops, and Apple says each can update its own network credentials when you change your Wi-Fi. This could address the offline-device problems that plague Apple Home. Everything is end-to-end encrypted, and the cameras keep recording to onboard storage if your Wi-Fi drops.

The devices also support Apple Home features other manufacturers have been slow to adopt. The LG lock is only the third to offer hands-free Home Key unlocking over UWB, and both thermostats work with Apple’s Clean Energy Guidance and Adaptive Temperature, which adjusts around your location and sleep schedule.

At least that’s the promise. We’ll have to test these devices to see how well they deliver.

The LG door lock and video doorbell pair in the Apple Home app so you can unlock the door when you see who is at the door. Image: Apple

A curated garden path

Together, Apple’s new devices form a polished, cohesive starter kit for the smart home — albeit an expensive one. The cameras, lock, and thermostats cost $200 to $400, and camera history requires an iCloud Plus plan. As Drance said, the smart home isn’t a one-size-fits-all solution, so this won’t work for everybody. If you already have a Ring doorbell or Google Nest Hub, this probably isn’t for you. Instead, Apple is trying to guide its existing customers who haven’t bought a video doorbell or smart lock yet down a curated path into the smart home.

However, Apple faces a tougher challenge in the broader market: It’s arriving late. The smart display category is already mature; millions of homes have Echo and Google smart displays. Millions more have Ring or Nest doorbells, neither of which will work with HomeView at launch.

As a smart home platform, Apple Home ranks third in adoption, behind Google, with Amazon holding a big lead, according to Parks Associates research. But customer loyalty to those platforms isn’t guaranteed. Four in five smart-home households would consider switching, Parks says, especially if another platform lets them control everything in one place. “Interoperability will be critical, but the bigger prize is owning the consumer relationship,” she says.

With its Home Collection, Apple isn’t reinventing the smart home; it’s trying to make it easier to get into one.

Tech.title: The new Apple TV 4K just got its first (very small) discount
Tech.content:
Earlier this week, Apple announced its new Apple TV 4K, which costs nearly twice as much as the 2022 model did at launch. Amazon is now offering the first discount on the forthcoming streaming box (coming out on November 13th), just days after discounting Apple’s new smart display for the first time. Right now, you can preorder the latest Apple TV 4K ahead of its November 13th release date for $289.99 ($9 off) at Amazon. Yes, it’s a tiny discount, but every little bit helps given the higher price tag.

Powered by the new A19 chip, Apple’s latest streaming device now features support for Siri AI out of the box, which is coming to older Apple TV 4K models via a software update. Unlike its predecessors, though, the new model features far-field microphones so you can quickly make hands-free requests. You can, for example, ask for recommendations, like nature documentaries available on Apple TV, or ask questions about what you’re watching. Siri AI can also understand personal context, too, so long as you have an iPhone or iPad connected to your account that supports Apple Intelligence.

Apple has made a few other welcome upgrades, though — as my colleague John Higgins points out — not as many as some may have expected. While Apple skipped features we’d hope to see on a $300 streamer, like audio passthrough and support for 120fps output, it’s nice that the Siri Remote now supports Find My precision tracking, so you can make it ring when it goes missing or use the Find My app on your iPhone to pinpoint its location. The new Apple TV 4K also supports a more expansive surround-sound setup, allowing you to pair up to four compatible HomePod speakers instead of just two.

The device has plenty of computing oomph, is always connected to power, and looks like a perfect place to run a bunch of apps. And yet the HomeView is relying almost entirely on CarPlay. What gives here?
